Chan Master Wencai of Moon-Boat (Yuezhou) from Shaoshi on Mount Song had the pen-name Xubai (Empty White). He was a native of Tongzhou and belonged to the lineage of the Guangning Wang clan of Weizhou.
His grandfather’s name was Cai; he followed Emperor Taizong Wenhuang in quelling the internal rebellion and rose to the rank of Wude General before settling in Tongzhou.
At the time of the Master’s birth, his father dreamed that a monk came to stay at their home.
He was then born. Upon reaching adulthood, he donned the white robes of a novice at Wanan Temple in the prefecture and took refuge under Chan Master Baian Kong.

He traveled to Hangzhou to receive full ordination, then returned north to close himself in retreat. While reading the *Wansong’s Collection of Critical Comments on the Occasions of Staying Overnight*, which was like facing a blank wall for a long time, he suddenly attained realization, saying:
"The style of the Cao-Dong school has spread throughout the world; it possesses the art of weaving a palindrome."
This is a matter of merit. Unless one possesses the subtle, intricate, and winding mastery that does not merely touch upon the immediate point, one cannot act as the master for him.
Subsequently, he turned back and left the pass to study under Chan Master Wufang Cong, who clarified his own insights for him; Fang then patted him in approval and certified him.
In the first year of the Zhengde era, he took charge of Shaolin. Disciples gathered like clouds; though the bells were struck and the drums beaten, there was no [distraction].

On a day of the *xū* (void) stem, he addressed the assembly: "Bodhidharma came from the West to directly point to and transmit the Single Vehicle Dharma, enabling people to see their nature and become Buddhas.
When it reached my Shaoshi [Mount Song] monastery, it was like nine tripods suspended by a single thread.
You all, while your physical strength is robust and healthy, must strive to settle this matter; you must exert yourselves and not let the days pass in idleness. As for Yi Zhenghui:
Officials from the three provinces traveled back and forth to seek his counsel; all were moved by the transformative influence of his character.

In the third year of the Jiajing era (1524), the year of Jiashen, when the Master was seventy-three years old, his disciples established a retreat for him among the mists and clouds of the thirty-six peaks to provide for his retirement.

Chan Master Xiaoshan Zongshu of Zongjing Monastery in Beijing was the thirty-second generation descendant in the lineage of Chan Master Shaoshi Cui of the Qingyuan line; he was the son of the Li family of Nanhe in Shunde. Regarding his...

From his childhood, he was unlike ordinary children; while playing with other boys, he would imitate the performance of Buddhist rites. At the age of ten, his father sent him to school to study the Confucian classics.
Once he had mastered their general meaning, he closed his books and sighed, saying, "These are all worldly dharmas;

they are not the supramundane dharma. He then went to Kaiyuan Temple in the prefecture to shave his head and receive ordination. Hearing of the flourishing reputation of Master Yuezhou’s Dharma seat, he entered it.

He requested further instruction from Master Shi for eight years, during which time he received the transmission of the orthodox lineage. In the thirty-sixth year of the Jiajing era, Master Shu of Nanyue requested him to take up residence at Shaoshi.
The Master sighed and said, "More than thirty years have passed since the passing of my late teacher, and the tradition of the Cao-Dong school has nearly vanished."

A senior elder once said, "In these declining times of the Zen forest, those who propagate the Dharma are many, yet they falsely rely on themselves and seek only ease, failing to provide urgent support.
Its collapse could occur at any moment. Though I felt ashamed of this entrustment, what could I do but honor it? Thus, I took charge of the monastery.
At that time, a severe drought occurred; the rivers and wells had run dry. Once the dharma assembly was established, the springs surged once more.

In the year of Bingyin, he went to the capital and took charge of Zongjing Monastery. In the first year of the Longqing era, he traveled to the Western Mountains and reached Sanxue Cave on Guji Mountain.
Admiring the secluded and tranquil scenery of the mountain, he settled there for the summer retreat. In the winter, he suddenly fell ill on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month.
He took up his brush and wrote a verse, saying: "Mirror of the Source, Mirror of the Source! The Dharma of the mind completes its practice; This very day it is Perfect Enlightenment.
When the mirror is shattered, the Source is rectified. Having finished the verse, he sat upright and passed away. His secular age was sixty-eight, and his years as a monk were thirty-six.
His remains were cremated and divided into three portions: one portion was kept at Zongjing (Mirror of the Source) where a stupa was erected for it; another portion was sent to Shunde.
At the ancestral burial site, one portion was used to erect a stupa at Shaoshi.

On the day he retired from affairs at Shaoshi, the Dharma drum in the Dharma Hall fell to the ground without cause. At the onset of his illness, a large branch of the Qin-era Huai tree at Shaoshi broke off.
After he entered nirvana, that tree collapsed without cause. (The Master’s alternative style name was Dazhang.)
Chan Master Changrun Huanxiu of the Western Capital’s Shaosheng Monastery was a dharma successor of Chan Master Zongjing Shu;
he was the son of the Huang family of Jinxian in Nanchang. From his youth, he was twice as diligent [as others].
He was close to his father and followed him on excursions. He often observed the various entertainers with a look of detachment, as if struck by some profound realization;
he saw that all such illusions were but limited manifestations. What, then, is impermanence? Thereupon, he went to Mount Funiu to pay homage to Master Tantan Ping and shaved his head.

He lived there for three years. At first, he attempted to restrain his mind like pressing down a floating melon; yet thoughts of arising and ceasing multiplied, leaving him bewildered and at a loss for what to do. He sought to resolve his doubts, but remained undecided.

He went south to Mount Jing to inquire with Wansong. Wansong interrogated him, saying, "What is this doubt? What is this fabrication? The Master was still undecided; he withdrew and reported his situation.
One night at Jiuhua, he suddenly awakened and realized his body was identical to empty space. He approached a guest to question the nature of this state.

The guest considered it an obstacle of principle (*li-zhang*) and advised him to enter through the teachings. He then listened to lectures on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* until he reached the section on "Perfection" (*yuan*).
Upon reading the phrase, "Clearly and fully knowing that it does not depend on mental thought," he suddenly attained enlightenment. It was vast and open, like an image in a mirror;
it did not fall into illusory emptiness, and he realized that the external world was empty—merely a single breath of worldly toil.
Later, he went to visit Master Lian of Dafang and asked, "When an image appears in a mirror, what then? Lian said, "You must break it apart. The Master said, "After it has been broken apart..."
"How is it? Nanquan asked. Liang said, "It has not yet left the realm of mind and objects. The Master remained undecided and went to study under Chan Master Xiaoshan.
Upon his initial arrival, he raised the previous statement. Xiaoshan said, "Why must you break it? The Master said, "What can be done about the reflections in the mirror?

Xiaoshan said, "Where are the reflections in the mirror? At these words, the Master had an awakening. One day, Xiaoshan asked the Master, "Has your former doubt been resolved? The Master held up his palm.

Mount [Shan] said, "Are you not asking for a shadow by means of a phantom? The Master said, "Beyond this, there is nothing else that exists. Mount [Shan] said, "Try turning your robe inside out and searching for it.

For two years he practiced with increasing diligence and progress. Mount [Shan] brought up the case of Dongshan’s question, "I am not he now," and pressed him, saying, "Since you are not he, after all, who are you?

The Master attained realization and replied with a verse: The body is not the same as the mind; The mind is not the same as the body. If one wishes to know the true person, Look at the one before you.

[The Master] said: "If you wish to verify this person, there is a true message: formless, it fills empty space; having form, it leaves no trace. It has served as the teacher of Buddhas and Patriarchs;
it has often acted as the standard for heaven and earth. A whisk made of tortoise hair stirs up a pure breeze;

from the tip of a staff made of rabbit horns, the bright moon emerges. Shan [the student] said: "Do not merely repeat others' words; you must further enter the gate of awakening yourself. The Master said: "Still..."
"Not borrowing conditions—through which gate does one enter? Shan said, "If you do not borrow conditions, why have you come here?
The Master said, "Precisely because I do not borrow conditions, I have come here. Shan said, "Regarding the phrase 'not borrowing conditions,' what do you understand by it?
The Master said, "A colorful phoenix soars with body at ease; an iron ox gallops and bellows with mind ever at leisure. Shan said, "Excellent! You have clarified it."
On the day he took his leave, Mount [Shan] presented him with a verse, saying: "You shall surely become a Lord of Men and Gods; you must contemplate the autumn at Shaoshi.
The Master asked, "What kind of person is Changrun? How would I dare to presume upon such a position? Mount instructed him, saying, "The Way has long been in decline;

how can you fold your hands and do nothing? The Master responded with repeated assent. When Mount passed away, everyone deliberated that none but the Master was fit to preside over the seat. The Master accordingly accepted.

He was humble and modest; though requested twice more, he declined both times. The assembly then recited the verse of entrustment concerning Mount [Shao-shi]. The Master suddenly shed tears and said no further words.
In the autumn of the second year of the Wanli era (Jiaxu), he took charge of Shaoshi. The Master’s physical presence was robust and imposing, and his voice was like a great bell.
He shared in the simple frugality of the practitioners, yet his character was broad and expansive as he single-mindedly bore the burden of the Great Dharma.
Morning and evening he was diligent and never showed even the slightest sign of weariness. Two hundred and seventy people entered his quarters to offer incense.

On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month in the thirteenth year of the Wanli era, he wrote a verse and announced his passing. This is recorded in his *Yulu* (The Master’s informal title was Dàqiān).
Chan Master Changzhong Yunkong of Lingshan in Jianchang Prefecture asked Shouchang about the essentials of the Dharma.

The Master said, "If you can be diligent and refuse to deceive yourself, that is the practice from beginning to end. One day, hearing his brothers discussing the meaning of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* with great eloquence, the Master laughed and said, "If the eye of the school is not clear, it cannot be considered ultimate. Shouchang heard this.
Stupefied and lost, he asked, "What is the Eye of the School? The Master swept his robe and rose. Later, Chang requested further instruction.
The Master said, "I truly do not know; you must look for it yourself. Later, at Dahao Mountain, Chang attained awakening after hearing [the Master’s] words.

He then entered the abbot's quarters to communicate what he had realized. The Master said, "It is not that there is nothing to be awakened to, but you must ensure that your realization is functional and applicable before you have truly attained it."
Otherwise, I fear it would be nothing more than "mercury-silver Chan.
[This concludes the entry for] Chan Master Shaoshi Run, the thirty-fourth generation descendant of Qingyuan and the dharma heir of [his predecessor].

Chan Master Cizhou Fangnian of Beijing Dajue Temple was the son of the Yang family of Tang County. At the age of ten, he went forth under Master Yigong of Guangde Daci at Jintai to receive the tonsure and full ordination.

Upon hearing Master Daoguo lecture on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, when he reached the section on the "Investigation of the Mind in Seven Locations," he began to realize that conditioned phenomena are not substantial.
He subsequently traveled through various lecture halls, thoroughly investigating the essential principles of both the Nature (Xing) and Characteristics (Xiang) schools of Buddhism.
Realizing this was not the case, he abandoned it and went to Shaoshi to attend upon Chan Master Huanchou.
As soon as Huanchou saw him, he asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the north. Huanchou asked, "How do the teachings of the Dharma in the north compare to those here?

The Master said, "The waters branch into a thousand streams, yet they flow from a single source. Seeing that his speech was elegant and refined, Huanchou appointed him as the *venerable of affairs* (*weina*). One day—
While visiting the place where the First Patriarch sat facing a wall, he suddenly attained realization and said, "Before the Five-Milk Peak, what a wonderful message!
Large and small stones, every single one, rests firmly upon the ground. He went to the master's room to present this insight.

Xiu instructed him, saying, "From the Buddhas and Patriarchs of antiquity down to the present, each has transmitted their own realization to the next, desiring that all sentient beings know it exists. I have now obtained [this for you]."
Regarding this "Small Mountain" [teaching] of my former master, it has been transmitted as it was for over ten years. Now I bestow it upon you.

You should take the mind of the Buddhas and Patriarchs as your own mind to continue the life of wisdom. Nevertheless, even though this is so, you should remain hidden in forests and springs, emerging only when the time is right.
He then bestowed upon him a verse, saying: "The unsurpassed mind of nirvāṇa, Transmitted and entrusted from Buddha to Buddha and Patriarch to Patriarch, I now bestow it."

At the time of his ordination, dew fell upon the peak of Yunjing (Cloud-Pure). At the age of twenty-eight, he entered seclusion at Wutai Mountain. During the day he took but one meal; at night he sat alone.
Later, while traveling to the East Terrace to pay his respects, his two eyes suddenly went blind. The Master said, "This illusory body does not truly exist; from where could illness come?
After practicing meditative concentration for seven days, both eyes were restored to sight. He then traveled south to visit Putuo Shan and returned.
Next, while the assembly at Daishan Temple in Yue was requesting him to stay and preach the Dharma at Zhifengtu, Yunmen went to visit him.
The Master asked, "At Zhifengtu, facing the green mountains, with the city of the Prince of Yue nearby and the vast ocean far away—how is it? Yunmen said, "The moon pierces through the vast ocean;
the Persian does not raise his eyebrows. The Master further questioned him on the fundamental principle of the Dongshan school. Yunmen spoke this verse: "The Five Ranks."
Ruler and minister must know this most urgently: within this, why wait for thought? A barren woman is skilled at playing with things that lack needle or thread;
a wooden puppet can lift a mechanism beyond transformation. Red dust billows and swirls from the bottom of the well; white waves roll and fly over the mountain peak.

"Birth itself is originally effortless; without conscious striving, one naturally attains the imperial domain. The Master said, "The phrasing is dense and subtle, falling neither into beginning nor end.
You are truly the offspring of this house. He then summoned him into the room for certification.
Again he said, "In the future, when you open your two lips, you shall have the power to cut off the tongues of all people under heaven. He then bestowed upon him this verse: Cao...
A single drop of water from the source; Buddhas and Patriarchs have transmitted it to one another. To this day, at the time of its bestowal, the great earth becomes nectar.
*Tu!* At the peak of Wuyufeng, an unbarbed arrow struck the half-child of the South.

In the year Renchen, he was invited by the monastics and laypeople of Jiaxing to preside over Dongta. Subsequently, he accepted the invitations of Yunju and Mount Lu. The twenty-second year of the Wanli era, Jiawu.
In autumn, he was invited to open the Dharma at the ancient site of Qingliang on Mount Wutai. Both monastics and laypeople earnestly entreated him to remain. Later, he passed away.
His Dharma heir, Chan Master Yunmen Cheng, enshrined his remains in a stupa on the southern mountain of Xiansheng (the Master’s alternative style name was Qingliang).
Chan Master Wuyan Zhengdao of Shaoshi on Mount Song was the son of Hu Shi of Zhang County. He went to Shanglan Temple to receive the tonsure.
At the age of fifteen, he met the elder Zhi Xiu, who pointed out the essentials of Chan to him; he subsequently followed Xiu as his teacher.

While resting at Jingping Cliff on Mount Nanyue, he visited and questioned [his master] morning and evening. Xiu said, "If you wish to investigate and clarify this matter, you must thread through the entanglements of the teachings and the scriptures."
It was only after this that [Fengxue] began to gain recognition. He pointed [Fengxue] toward San’an Ang. An said to Xiu, “Wu Yan is fully worthy of being called a vessel of the Dharma.

You must by no means allow him to harbor mere fragments of knowledge or partial understanding within his breast. Simply send him north on a pilgrimage so that he may investigate for himself and awaken through his own realization.
Xiu then brought up the verse by Zhang Zhuo to test his actual practice. The Master said, “Since even True Suchness cannot be grasped, how could there be a verse? Xiu [was satisfied].
Seeing that he was exceptionally sharp, [Zhaozhou] directed him to go to Shaoshi to attend upon Chan Master Huanxiu.

One day, as Huanxiu ascended the hall, the Master asked, "What is the家风 (house style) of the Dongshan lineage? Huanxiu said, "Three flowering trees under the moon; twin cassia branches before the peak.
The Master asked, "Does the Master have anything else besides this? Huanxiu said, "There is only this one reality; there is neither two nor three. The Master...
Upon hearing these words, he attained great enlightenment. He immediately presented a verse, saying: "The spirit gathers at the mountain peak; the moon locks the secluded cliff.

The stone man claps his hands; the wooden woman smiles. Huan Yin then presented a verse, saying: "The ultimate meaning beyond words is not separate from words; The profound shout and profound raising are a wondrous, peerless transmission.
Today, the single transmission is personally bestowed as a seal; In years to come, the twin cassias shall benefit humans and devas. The 10th year of the Wanli era...
In the eighth year, the Gengyin year, he presided over Mount Shaoshi. The Prince of Zhou invited the Master to preach the Dharma for the preservation of longevity;
the King attained great awakening. When the Prince of Chongfan of Runing heard of this, he also invited the Master to preach the Dharma.

At that time, the Crown Prince suffered from a foot ailment and stood leaning on a staff. The Master led him forward, and after walking seven circuits, his sweat flowed like a torrent, and his foot [was healed].
He was immediately healed. A monk asked, "When the World-Honored One remained silent for a long time when asked neither about speech nor non-speech, what was his intent?

The Master said, "To move one's countenance is to reveal the ancient path; do not fall into the trap of the silent mechanism. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year?
The Master held up his whisk and said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Next year there will be even newer branches. Do not [seek it elsewhere].
I shall provide a detailed explanation using successive metaphors. One elderly master asked, "What is non-speaking? The Master replied, "The four seasons proceed.
Another master asked, "What is non-speaking? The Master replied, "The hundred things grow. The Master’s mental acuity was swift and sharp, and his disposition was plain and sincere.
Later, he passed away and was interred in the ancestral cemetery.

Chan Master Shouchang Wuming Huijing of Jianchang Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Linshan Zhong. He was a son of the Pei family of Chongren, Fuzhou. Initially, his birth had been difficult;

his grandfather recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* and he was delivered. From birth, he was exceptionally gifted, with a countenance that was ancient and dignified, like that of a soaring crane.
Lingkong was by nature serene and free from worldly desires. At the age of nine, upon entering the local school, he immediately asked, "What is this 'vast and majestic qi'?
His teacher marveled at him. When he grew up, he read the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* as if recovering a long-lost possession.
He stayed at Linsan for three years, constantly harboring doubts regarding the four-line verse. One day, he saw the verse by Master Fu Dashi: "If one speaks of the four lines..."
Verse: It should not be difficult; the body does not perceive it as refreshing. Thus he composed a verse: "The four-line verse of the Vajra has neither shadow nor form;
originally there is not a single character, yet it pervades the realms and radiates light.

At the age of twenty-four, while perusing the Great Canon, he reached the "Chapter on the Eye of the School" (*Zongyan pin*) and only then came to know the principle of the separate transmission outside the teachings (*jiaowai biechuan*). He then took his leave from the monastic granary.

Shan Yindun hid away on Mount E; ascending the summit and gazing about, he composed this verse: "Trampling upon the first peak above the clouds, The vast expanse before my eyes is but a small void. At that time, I had no way to meet you face-to-face; Today we encounter one another everywhere as equals. He lived in a hut for three years without anyone knowing of him. While reading the *Chuan Deng Lu*, I saw a monk ask Xingshan: "How is it? [Xingshan replied: "It is like a person holding a mirror and looking at their own face. Shan Yindun said: "I have been practicing the Way for thirty years, yet I have never seen such a thing. He then composed this verse: "Thirty years of practicing the Way, Yet I have never seen such a thing. If you wish to see the Buddha-nature, Look directly at your own face. Later, while reading the *Fozu Tongji*, I saw that when the monk Huizhao asked Mazu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Mazu struck him with his staff and said, "Go wash your bowl. Huizhao was greatly enlightened. Shan Yindun said: "I have been practicing the Way for thirty years, yet I have never seen such a thing. "This is the Way. Shan said, "A truly magnificent mountain. The Master exhorted himself day and night until he forgot both sleep and food.
One day, while moving a stone that was so heavy it could not be lifted, he pushed with all his might and suddenly attained great enlightenment. He immediately composed a verse, saying:
"If you wish to study the unsurpassed path of Bodhi, Hurry to clear away this magnificent mountain. Only when you know the Way do you realize the mountain is no good; Then you turn your body around—"
Having leaped through the barrier of the Patriarchs, he presented himself to Xishan, who recognized him as a vessel of the Dharma.
It was only then that he shaved his head and received full ordination. From that time forth, for twenty-four years, he never left the mountain, remaining there as if it were a single day.
In the thirty-sixth year of the Wanli era, the Jia-wu year, when the Master was fifty-one years of age, he resided at Baofang. A monk asked the Master: "While residing on this mountain..."
"Who have you ever met? The Master replied, "I have not yet traveled on pilgrimage. The monk pressed him, saying, "How can one judge the whole world by a single corner?
The Master appreciated these words and went to Shaoshi to pay respects to the Patriarch. There he met Chan Master Wuyan;

seeing that the Master’s teaching was extraordinary, Wuyan, together with the provincial governor of Henan, Duke Xiong Shangwen, invited the Master to instruct the assembly. Furthermore, he entered the fifth [stage].
He visited Master Ruifeng (the dialogue concerning Ruifeng is found in the Ruifeng chapter) and they questioned one another; [Ruifeng] held him in high esteem and he returned to his own monastery.

Subsequently, at the invitation of Dongyan, he extensively propagated the mysterious wind [of the Dharma]. Later, he presided over Shouchang. Ascending the hall, he offered incense and said: "Do you all understand?"
This is the inexhaustible foundation employed by all Buddhas of the three periods of time. They have cast it all at once toward the Sahā world;
yet Śākyamuni Buddha still has not exhausted its use. The successive patriarchs of India and China likewise have not exhausted its use.
Today, this mountain monk takes it up with a casual hand to deliberate with the assembly: is this the "separate transmission outside the teachings" or the "mystery within the scriptures"?
Does it encompass heaven and earth? Does it follow the waves and drift with the currents? Does it cut off all streams and offer it up for deliberation?
Does the Great Function manifest before us like a probing pole or a blade of grass? Is the Vajra Jewel-Sword cast out into the open?
To speak of this according to reality, it would not be exhausted even throughout kalpas; yet, those possessed of wisdom can discern and distinguish it: white is white, black is black.

[If one treats it as] black, one does not lump it all together as a single mass; only then can the right and wrong of the monastic community be determined and the success or failure of practitioners be verified.
Thereafter, whether responding to the holy or the mundane, one will naturally not be deceived by those who feign clarity.
One’s actions and responses to circumstances will then be invariably auspicious. Yet this Way has long been subtle and neglected. Among the assembly, there are...
A person of great wisdom should devote their very body and life to support this endeavor with all their might, making enlightenment their ultimate goal.
To benefit both self and others, one lifetime is not enough; they must devote a second lifetime, and even a third, until it is naturally attained. As the ancients said:

"If one does not enter the great ocean of birth and death, it is difficult to obtain the priceless jewel. This refers to those of dull faculties; a person of keen intelligence understands it upon hearing it once.
"Know the wondrous. Nevertheless, even so, were it not for the spring breeze, the flowers would not bloom. Let us speak for a moment: once the flowers have bloomed, the breeze blows them away.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas constantly preach the Dharma; there is no need to doubt or speculate as to what kind of Dharma it is."
Heaven and earth are dark blue and yellow; the universe is vast and ancient. Whether one penetrates the source or masters the teachings, it is valued only that one directly takes responsibility.
What is it that one takes responsibility for? Clouds rise and bring rain; dew falls and turns to frost. A dragon does not dwell in stagnant water; a fierce tiger does not walk by the roadside.
If you can penetrate these pivotal points, why need you wish to go to the Western Land? Do not ask about the past.

The Buddha is the patriarch of all who followed; his nostrils emit light just like ours. How does he emit this light? His transformation pervades the grasses and trees, reaching across the myriad regions.
Śākyamuni refused to let it leak out; Bodhidharma concealed it for nine years. Now, Mount Emei spares no effort in its verbal expression.
I shall now proclaim it for the assembly. But tell me, how do you proclaim it? [He] brandished his ruler once and said:

"Do not speak of others' shortcomings; do not rely on your own strengths. Ascending the hall, he said: "On this day, the anniversary of the Buddha’s Enlightenment at the Winter Solstice, the monastic communities prepare congee. For what purpose is this done?"
There is nothing that does not conform to worldly convention. Yet, the gate of the patch-robed monks need not be like this. Have you not heard it said:
"The Buddhas of the three periods do not know 'existence,' yet the cat and the white ox do know 'existence'? If it were so, the Buddhas of the three periods would already have been left in the dust.
"How much more so for the Buddha Kāśyapa! But tell me, in what way are the 'Tiger' and the 'White Ox' superior to all the Buddhas?
The Head Seat said, "It is because gold is refined by great smelting and jade emerges from the Lántián fields.

The Master said, "Even though it is so, I cannot help but drive both the Tiger and the White Ox out through the main gate at once. Why? Because the True Command is being exercised. He held [the staff].
The guiding principles were established and the monastic community was revitalized; the seas were calm and the rivers clear as the pure command was enforced.

All worthy men were gathered and brought back to the Treasure Place; the City of Transformation was toppled so that no one remained. Zhaozuo said, "Master, you say the City of Transformation is toppled and no one is left behind.
This may be acceptable from the Master’s own perspective, but for someone like me, it is not so. The Master asked, "How would you do it? Zhaozuo replied:
Casually carrying a cloth bag, he has no concerns at all; he laughs as he awaits that one person on the street. The Master said, "This too is merely a lute played idly. The assembly laughed heartily.
After the prostrations, they descended from their seats. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "In the vast sky where there is no path, the Chan practitioner walks alone.

Amidst white waves surging to the heavens, the man of wisdom can cross over. Even if one reaches the profound gate ten thousand fathoms deep, one still falls to 'that side. At a well a thousand cubits deep..."
Coming forth from within, he ultimately remains on this shore. Disregarding the hidden treasure of pure gold, why linger over a patched bag and a broken bowl?
Walking upon level ground, his heart is startled; treading the edge of a precipice, he lets go of all apprehension. Within the scope of one’s original nature, the eye of wisdom discerns all.

On the ninth anniversary of the late Master Yunmen, he ascended the hall and said, "The late Master passed away on the fourth day of the first lunar month in the year of Bingyin. He then counted off his fingers and said:
The first anniversary was in the twelfth month of the Dingmao year; then came Wuchen, Jisi, Gengwu, Xinwei, Renshen, Guiyou, Jiayu, and Yihai—thus there were nine anniversaries.
Although he has been deceased for nine years, from the very beginning he has never departed from this very day;
yet although he has not departed from this very day, it does not hinder the fact that it is again the ninth anniversary of his passing. How, then, can one explain this?
"If you have not yet understood, I, the decrepit old man, shall proclaim for you the five positions of the direct and the indirect to repay the kindness of my former masters.
He then let out a shout and said: "Before I stepped out of the Dharma Hall, there was originally no such shout;
it is only now that I have ascended this seat that this one shout exists. This is 'the direct within the indirect. Yet, this very shout is silent in its own place; this is 'the indirect.'"
This is the "Middle and Correct" (Zhongzheng). This very shout, free from names and words, is "Coming from the Middle and Correct. Now, facing all of you, there is this one shout;
because of this one shout, you all may know your own original possession—this is "Arriving at the Middle and Correct" (Jianzhongzhi).

This one shout of mine exhausts the sentiments of both sage and ordinary person, forgets both subject and object, and perfectly transcends existence and non-existence—this is "The Middle and Correct" (Jianzhong).

It has arrived. According to the discourse of the Jì (Ji) school: "The center within the biased" (*zhèng zhōng piān*) seizes the person; "the biased within the center" (*piān zhōng zhèng*) seizes the environment;
"coming from the center within" (*zhèng zhōng lái*) seizes both person and environment; "arriving at the simultaneous" (*jiān zhōng zhì*) leaves neither person nor environment seized;

and "reaching the simultaneous" (*jiān zhōng dào*) refers to the profound, essential, and wondrous principle. According to the Yúnmén (Yunmen) school, this single shout responds to the capacity of the interlocutor, as it is said:
This one shout is called the "phrase that encompasses heaven and earth" (*qián kūn jù*), which sweeps away both ordinary and sagely beings, cutting off all intellectual understanding.

This one shout is called the "phrase that cuts off the flow of all streams" (*jiè duàn zhòng liú jù*), wherein questioning about phenomena is answered with phenomena, and questioning about principle is answered with principle.

This one shout is called the "phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the current" (*suí bō zhú làng jù*). According to the school of Míngzhàng (Tiantai), this one shout directly manifests the Great Lunar Disc (*mahācandramaṇḍala*).
It is called the "Perfect Mark" (*yuánxiàng*). This single shout reveals the faculty that points toward the Ultimate;
it is called the "Dark Faculty. This single shout originally flows forth from one's own mind; it is called "Intentional Speech.

This single shout allows those who see and hear it to silently know their place of return; it is called "Silent Discourse. This single shout completely encompasses all immeasurable, wondrous meanings at once.
This is called the Ocean of Meaning. This single shout encompasses all forty-two letters as well as all worldly characters;
it is called the Ocean of Characters. From the perspective of the Fa-yen school, this single shout directly reveals the One True Dharma-realm;
it is called the "Total. This single shout possesses illumination and function, withdrawal and release, and both reward and reprimand.
Punishment is called "distinction. Although the distinctions between bestowing, taking away, rewarding, and punishing all ultimately return to a single mind, this is called "sameness.

Although they share a single mind, even if there is no bestowing or taking away, and no reward or punishment, this is called "difference. Although there are differences in the gathering and releasing of rewards and punishments, they all together constitute a single self;
this is called "accomplishment. Although they form a single entity, it does not hinder killing or giving life, or bestowing and taking away, each in its own way.
To abide in the fundamental position is called "destruction. It is not only the case with a single shout;
it applies even to a single blow of the staff, a single stroke of the whisk, a single phrase, or a single word, and even to raising an eyebrow, blinking an eye, or turning and bowing.

Mui said, "If you wish to know the meaning of the Buddha-dharma, you should observe the conditions of time and season. When the time and season arrive, its principle manifests of itself."
Manifesting the Virtue of Dhyāna: Tonight is the eve of the year’s end; tomorrow morning is the New Year.
The season has arrived—how can you manifest the principle of self-revelation? Elder, twenty years ago you were like a wooden puppet:

Thus, spending one's days in this manner, one remains entirely untainted by worldly vulgarity. Although one may appear dull-witted and bewildered, the laws of the world cannot deceive one for even a single moment.

when hot, one knows the heat. One pastes up the door-gods to welcome the New Year, and burns firewood to bid farewell to the waning winter.
Passing my days in this manner, there is indeed some measure of joy. Although I am merely drifting with the current, the Buddha-dharma cannot deceive me by even a single point.
O virtuous practitioners of Zen: this mountain monk, limping and dragging along, passes the time in just this way.
Now, it is acceptable to say I know; it is acceptable to say I do not know; it is altogether acceptable to say I both know and do not know. Why?

The Master said: "Gentle and harmonious. Question: "How does one cut down the central tree? The Master said:

"Have you read the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*? the Master asked. Wenyuan said, "I have heard of it. The Master asked, "When Maitreya receives his prediction of enlightenment after one more life, how will that be?
Wenyuan said, "Many people harbor doubts about this. The Master said, "And you go along with them in that way? The Master was struck by Wenyuan's response.

Later, while warming himself by the fire, he raised the case of a monk who asked an ancient worthy: "When the kalpa-ending fires blaze forth, will this [body] be destroyed or not? One replied, "It will be destroyed," and another replied, "It will not be destroyed."...
"It is unbreakable. What do you mean by this? Yuan said, "You have come here again in such a manner. The Master then spent the winter at Jie.
Yuan minutely investigated the places where the Master had attained realization throughout his life and interrogated him on the principles distinguishing the gateways and halls of the Five Houses.
The Master freely expounded upon his insights. Yuan sighed with admiration and said, "I did not expect that you would be able to penetrate so deeply into these secrets."
"This Dharma-gate—my life of skillful wisdom, O Shouchang—is entrusted to you to circulate and propagate. He then bestowed upon him a verse, saying:

"The Way flourishes through the many heroes of the patriarchs; Virtue is honored throughout ten thousand ages as the Teacher. Reverently inheriting the intent of all the Sages, He awakens my eternal longing and reflection."
The Master bowed and accepted [the invitation]. The following day, he accompanied Dongyuan to pay his respects to Shouchang.
Upon meeting Chang, during the course of their questioning, Chang looked at him with a smile and marveled at him, asking: "Where did you meet Dongyuan? The Master replied: "Not elsewhere. Chang said:
Thereupon, the Master said, "Does the Abbot have eyes? Chang remained silent for a long while. The Master said, "Take care," and departed.
The next day, he asked again, "What did Dongyuan ever say to you? The Master replied, "I was once deceived by him. Chang said, "..."
"How was he deceived by him? The Master said, "This old fellow has gone off in that manner again. Chang laughed and said, "Are you being strange, my son?

The Master replied, "It is the Master himself who brought this about. He then asked Chang again, "I heard that when Dongyuan gave the Master a single word at that time, why did you immediately grant him full approval? If it were I, I certainly would not have done so."
He let him off easily. Chang said, "As for what he said—'Master, do not act strangely'—what would you have done in that situation?
Just as the Master was about to open his mouth, Chang struck him a blow across the face. The Master said, "This too is drawing the bow after the thief has fled."
Chang said, "I am glad there is someone here who can take a blow from my palm. From that time on, he engaged in many dialogues and inquiries with Chang.

Chang was particularly delighted and secretly instructed him, saying, "Be extremely cautious! This is what the former sages meant when they said that for one who attains this Dharma, life is like a thread hanging by a single strand.
Chang then presented a verse, saying: "I now know that there is that one point; I shall simply wait for the opportune moment."

Conditions converged purely and naturally; there was no need for deliberation, as both sages and ordinary people found peace. Joy was forgotten in the midst of discernment, and the enjoyment [of the Dharma] was vast.
In the autumn of the eighth year of the Kuòchóng era (1635), the Grand Councilor Li Chánggēng invited Bǎofá to open the hall for formal instruction.

Encountering the chaos of banditry, he declined and went to Shòuchāng to sweep the pagoda. The Master Qiánrán invited him to preside over that seat. The following autumn, he presided over Fúchuán; again, the following autumn...
Master Yuantong ascended the hall. Layman Huang Duanduo asked, "The Dharma-thunder shakes the earth; the Buddha-sun rises in the sky.
Amidst the myriad phenomena and the vast cosmos, there is a great, hearty laugh. What is the single phrase for this fresh celebration?

The Master said, "Having picked up the dragon pearl, its light shines through and beyond; together we shall take hands and ascend the high peak. Duanduo said, "Min is an ancient Buddha who has returned! The Master then [laughed].
After prostrating, the Master drew a circle and said, "Do you understand? At Vulture Peak, the flowers bloomed as he personally revealed the separate transmission.
At Shaoshi, amidst the cold snow, he fully upheld the orthodox command. Seizing the ten directions, the stone笋 (stone pine) stands across the void;
illuminating the single path, the mud ox emerges from the sea. Therefore, of the eighty-four thousand [teachings], none are like the phoenix feathers; only these thirty..."
Three men enter the tiger’s den; from of old, this matter has been most extraordinary.

For several hundred years, its succession has not been easy to maintain, yet today the Venerable Shouchang has specifically ascended Mount Kuang and entered the Yuantong Chan Monastery, revealing his entire being.
He stands together with the ancient masters of the ten directions and all dust-motes and lands—those old riddles without a handle—and with all the dark-skinned slaves and white oxen.
We have met face-to-face. Now tell me, how would you express the single phrase for the opening of the hall and the offering of felicitations to the Emperor?
"Heaven reveals auspicious colors that illuminate the mountains and rivers; the ten thousand nations sing praises to celebrate the Great Peace. Be careful. [Ascending the hall:

"I happened to go to the riverbank to gather white water lilies, idly following my companions to offer sacrifices to the River God. Among the crowd, I did not dare speak clearly; I cast my golden coin in secret."
When Qian Bu divined for someone far away, he did not dare speak openly before the assembly because the person was one held in his heart.
Since the person was one held in his heart, even ghosts and spirits would have known nothing of it; why then seek fortune from the outside? Alas! Boundless longing is cast away in vain;
when touched upon in ordinary moments, it is most difficult to restrain. Be careful. As the Master traveled toward Macheng, he passed through [the area].

In Qizhou: At the request of the Prince of Jing, he bestowed the *dharma-pratītyasamutpāda* (transmission of the Dharma) and preached the Dharma for the palace attendants of the Crown Prince within the inner court.
In the summer of the Gengchen year, during the Taiding reign, at the request of the Prince of Jian’an, he opened the Dharma at Shanglan Monastery.
The Prince asked: "Is there any difference between a Dharma King and a secular king? The Master replied: "In the Dharma, he is the most honored among Dharma Kings; in the state..."
[The Master] said, "Among kings, one is most honored. The King said, "A king must necessarily honor the Dharma as supreme.

The Master said, "Your Majesty has won both prizes at once. The King asked, "Regarding Yongning Ancient Monastery, the site of Mazu’s practice hall, where the Great Master now ascends the seat for the veneration of devas and humans—what skillful means (*upāya*) should be employed to guide and lead them? The Master said, "Now, fortunately..."
The Prince personally witnessed this and said, "The bell has rung and the drum has been beaten; the Dharma talk is finished.
Does the Great Master intend to add further annotations? The Master replied, "Does Your Highness already possess that single eye prior to sound? The Prince said, "I do."
Linji’s single shout has both guest and host. Setting aside the guest and host for a moment, what is this single shout?

The Master said, "One must receive it directly at the point of its application. [The student] asked, "That which not even a thousand sages can encompass and not ten thousand demons can spy upon—does it ever perish?
The Master said, "Fortunately, the pivot of the matter still remains. [The student] said, "Xuansha wanted..."
"One shoulder-load of bottomless buckets—what do you intend to do with them?
The Master said, "Even if one had such a load, I fear Xuansha would have no place to set it down. [The monk] said, "There is a staff; give him another staff.
"I do not know what you would give him," the Master replied. "This 'Wish-Fulfilling Jewel' of Perfect Penetration has never been doubted by anyone."

The King was greatly delighted and said, "Not only shall the ancestral style be established here from this day forth in Jiangxi, but the Buddha-land shall also be opened throughout Zhendan (China) starting from here.

Subsequently, he traveled to various places including Min, Guzhan, Mount Huangyan, and others, before returning to Yuan Tong. At that time, he encountered bandits who had destroyed Wuchang, so he proceeded to Jinling.
There, a multitude of high-ranking officials invited him to the Ancestral Hall at Linggu Temple to observe the retreat for the Qianqiu festival.
The Abbot ascended the hall. Taking his *ruci* (whisk), he drew a circle and said: "Do you understand? Transcending the solar wheel, it accords with the dream; at midnight, there is perfect clarity.
Riding upon the elephant-vehicle, he meets the opportunity; at dawn, nothing is revealed. The noble scion of nature, as soon as born, points and looks about, claiming supremacy.
Established in the position of the Blue Palace, he immediately succeeds to the great lineage. The *udumbara* flower manifests eternal spring."
The flowers and calyxes are now fresh; the precious mandate flourishes as the foundation for ten thousand generations, with its branches and roots extending far and wide.

It succeeds to the sagely destiny of Heaven, Earth, and the Ancestors, and inaugurates the glory of the court and the altars of soil and grain. Now, on this occasion of the Prince Heir’s auspicious birth, how shall we proclaim and celebrate it?
May he forever wish for a thousand autumns as enduring as the sun and moon, and may we always behold him for ten thousand years.
His longevity shall equal that of heaven and earth. In the autumn of the Jiashen year, he arrived at West Lake. Encountering the assembly of Dharma-protectors from Wujiang, he proceeded to Yuhang.

At the invitation of Magistrate Zou, he took charge of Jing Mountain. Ascending the hall, he cited Master Miaoxi, who said: "The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the wooden Buddha does not pass through the fire;
the clay Buddha does not pass through the water; the true Buddha sits within the house. This is the disclosure of the heart of Venerable Zhaozhou.
[The Master] spat out his gallbladder to report this matter in such a way. Is there anyone who recognizes kindness and repays it? The Master said:
"Great and small Miaoxi do not recognize good from evil; every person in the great earth has had their eyes and nostrils gouged out by that old fellow Zhaozhou."
This "Real Man of No Rank" has been pushed down into a ten-thousand-fathom deep pit; to this day, he cannot emerge with his head above ground.
Jing-shan extends a hand from elsewhere to rescue and deliver him. But how does one rescue and deliver him? A golden Buddha must pass through the furnace;
a wooden Buddha must pass through the fire; an earthen Buddha must pass through the water; but a True Buddha is not permitted to remain beneath the Black Mountain.
He acts as a steward for the house of ghosts, directly causing them to walk upon the edge of a sword and run through the midst of flames;

he enters the stream of birth and death to open the path between the holy and the mundane, manifesting the great function of total capacity, and continues the Buddha’s life-force atop the head of the "Wish-Fulfilling Son."
"Do you understand? To change the bones and wash the intestines, one must reorganize and readjust; even with eyes and hands functioning throughout the body, one must still investigate further.
The wooden tablet of Chan Master Zhànrán Chéng, the eighty-first generation Abbot and former Chief Administrator (Fǔngòng), was enshrined in the Patriarchs' Hall.

The Master drew a circle with his *ruìyì* (monk’s staff) and said, "Do you understand? Within the Patriarchs' Hall of antiquity, there has never been a divergent teaching; within the various monastic communities, there has already been a commonality."
The wind: there is no need to arrange the sequence; front and back are naturally and perfectly so. Looking at one another, they raise their eyebrows and smile;
throughout the entire realm, flowers bloom in a spring beyond eons. Be careful.

Compiled by the Chan monk Jingzhu, successor to the Patriarchs at Mount Zhiti,
of the Linji school,
the sixteenth generation below Nanyue.
Chan Master Puan Yinsu of Cihua Monastery in Yuanzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Huanglong Zhong. He was the son of the Yu family of Yichun.

At birth, auspicious light illuminated the heavens, and lotuses grew along the path surrounding his dwelling. When he grew up, he studied under Master Shoulong Xian, who bestowed the *Lotus Sūtra* upon him. The Master said: "All..."
The profound intent of the Buddha prizes awakening within the mind; what benefit do numerical categories and ritual practices bring to the Way?

He visited Mukan at Mount Wei and asked, "All phenomena return to the One; where does the One return? Mukan held up his whisk to indicate this, and [the Master] attained realization. Upon returning to Shoulong, he was invited by official decree to preside over Cihua Temple.
One day, while reciting the *Huayan lun* (Treatise on the Avatamsaka), he reached the passage: "When the root is reached, emotional attachments vanish... and he came to know...

The essence of his mind merged [with reality], and he attained a sudden, great enlightenment, saying: "I have now personally realized the Dharma-realm of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra. He then spoke this verse:
"It cannot be formed into a ball when pinched, nor can it be dispersed when struck. Why go to Nanyue or Tiantai? At the gateway of the six sense-faculties, no one is making use of them;
thus, the barbarian monk has come for no reason at all. Later, the Elder Liu invited him to reside at Cihua. Ascending the hall, he said: "Three..."
The realms are mind-only; only a Buddha understands this. All phenomena are consciousness-only—who else could know it?

Delusion and awakening are fundamentally non-existent, established only as provisional means of transformation, just like yellow leaves used to stop a child’s crying. Nirvana and birth-and-death are like a dream; who are these ten stages of sages and three levels of worthies?
There is a reality prior to heaven that has no form or appearance; words cannot reach its essence—Amitābha. This very Amitābha is...
Your mind need not laboriously pursue appearances by searching outwardly. The three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* are established according to time; every thought-moment is precisely this very moment.
If a person does not realize that the mind is not an appearance, they will cling to objects, lose themselves in delusion, and become attached to form and sound.
When one realizes that form and sound are non-dual in essence, the mountains, rivers, and great earth preach the True Sūtra. I dare ask: how does the one who preaches the True Sūtra do so?
He spoke for a long while, saying: "The wondrous sound of the present and the past has never ceased; were it not for Kāśyapa, there would be no hearing of what is heard.
From that time on, the Master extensively established bridges and ferries, venerated stupas, and broadly warded off calamities and protected against afflictions.

Neither heaven nor earth, nor sentient beings nor ghosts and spirits, could fathom his transformations. His various miraculous traces are beyond counting. Someone asked: "What practices did you cultivate to attain this? He immediately replied: [text continues].

Drawing a line in the air, he asked, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not. The Master said, "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak. He once praised himself, saying: "Heaven above, heaven above!
Having realized the Dharma of non-arising, I discourse on that which is not called Chan. With these two flaps of skin, I encompass the earth and include the heavens.
What is the Buddha? One hundred and eight thousand [miles]. The twenty-first day of the seventh month, in the fifth year of the Qiandao era.

He wrote a verse, saying: "Rain and sun alternate; the precious elephant shines bright. Clouds swirl across east, west, south, and north. Countless people have lost their pearls and suffered the calamity of plunder.
Through the provisional skill of illusory response, I clear it for you. Having finished writing, he sat in the lotus posture and passed away.
The seventeenth generation descendant of Nanyue,
Chan Master Shaoyuan of Zhaojue in Chengdu Prefecture,
successor to Chan Master Yan of Donglin, ascended the hall and said: He cited a monk asking Yunmen, "When the tree withers and the leaves fall..."

"How is it at this time? The Gatekeeper said, "The body is exposed to the golden wind. The Master said, "To understand the mechanism of falling into the tiger’s trap, one must be a patch-robed monk of true substance.
Only then did Great Master Yunmen possess the samādhi that transcends the crowd;

he struck the joints and knocked open the locks amidst a flash of lightning, extending a single hand to untangle the sticky and remove the bonds, pulling out the wedges and extracting the nails—truly excellent indeed.
[Zhaojue said: "Examine this closely with your own hands; it is much like lending a ladder to a thief. Zhaojue, however, was not like this.
If a monk were suddenly to ask, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? he would simply answer him: "The setting clouds fly alongside the solitary wild goose."
"The autumn waters share the same color as the vast sky. Now tell me, is this the same as Yunmen, or is it different?
He spoke again: "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and inconceivable. Ascending the hall, he said: "Melting bottles, plates, hairpins, and bracelets into a single gold;
stirring butter, curd, and clarified butter into a single flavor. Thus, guest and host reach accord, and internal and external are harmonious. This is the Five Ranks of Lord and臣 (Minister)."
Piercing through all at once. These four kinds of discernment form a single string. If one lets go, there is a fine drizzle and a rustling autumn wind;
if one holds fast, it is utterly empty—dare anyone look upon it with a direct eye? Now tell me: is it better to let go for the sake of others, or is it better to hold fast for the sake of others?
He spoke again: "Casually, as if the autumn wind has arrived; unintentionally cooling others, yet people cool themselves."

Chan Master Miaofeng Zhiyan of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yuyang Guang. A native of the Liu family of Huzhou, he shaved his head at the age of thirteen.

Upon seeing the scriptures and treatises only once, he immediately grasped their essential meaning. He went to Mount Mao to study under Chan Master Fozhao, where he directly pierced the kōan regarding the wind and the banner.
Fengji (鋒機) sealed [the transmission] with a verse, saying: "Today I open a single thread for you; cutting through nails and severing iron, I shall raise up my school.
He then entered Mount Kuanglu and planted his staff beneath Miaogao Peak. He faced the wall for ten years. Initially he resided at Huíyīn, and later he resided at Línghǐn. Entering the hall, he said:
"Responding to things and manifesting forms is like the moon in water; picked up by a casual hand, it is revealed all at once."
Striking the left side of the meditation seat with his whisk, he said: "This is the cauldron of boiling water and the furnace of burning coals.
Striking the right side, he said: "This is the forest of sword-trees and the mountain of blades. "In front are Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta; behind are Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra.
As for that one stroke in the middle—do you know where it falls? He struck again and said: "Vipaśyin Buddha has long since set his mind upon this."
"Until now, you have not attained the subtle. He ascended the hall and said: "Long-time practitioners of high caliber—your eyes empty the four seas, your nostrils reaching toward heaven.
You see with intimacy; you speak with intimacy; you act with intimacy; you employ [the Way] with intimacy.
Yet you still do not recognize this old monk’s staff. Why? Because when one has nearly completed a mountain nine fathoms high, one does not..."
[The Master] advanced a single basketful of earth and addressed the assembly. Fenyang said, "If you recognize the staff, your journey as a pilgrim is finished.
[This is] wrong. Sanjiao said, "If you recognize the staff, you will enter hell like an arrow. [This is] wrong. I, the old monk, am not like this: "If you recognize the staff, it is wrong.
These three "wrongs" from Miaofeng are not medicine for those without illness. Pang Gong sells a colander.
Ching-p’ing-tao Mu-shao, about to manifest his entry into extinction, wrote a verse, saying: "Coming is thus; going is thus. Coming and going are one and the same;
a fresh breeze extends ten thousand li. Thereupon he passed away.
Chan Master Beijian Ju Jian of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an was the son of the Long family from Tongchuan. He received full ordination at Guangfu Monastery in his native district.
He studied under Biefeng Tudu, investigating the teachings in silent meditation. One day, while reading the records of Wan’an, he attained realization.
He subsequently visited Fozhao, with whom his spiritual faculties were in accord. From then on, he remained within that master’s gate for fifteen years before traveling to Jiangxi.

He visited Zhongwen at Luhu and engaged in discussion with him; [Zhongwen] marveled greatly at him. He subsequently entrusted to him the bamboo pointer (zhubi) that Dahui had kept at the Yangyu Hermitage.
The Master accepted this with humility. After some time, he emerged from seclusion at Ba’en Temple in Tai, and later moved to Jingci Temple.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "If you recognize the One, ten thousand matters are finished. Yet as for this patch-robed monk, he does not recognize a single character.

Even if you were to act in such a way, it would still not be called 'Fully Uplifting. Where the power of Yu did not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west. Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example:
"When Miji Shibo and Dongshan were at a pancake shop, Miji drew a circle on the ground and said to Dongshan, 'Bring it here.'"
[The Master] went out. Shanshan said, "Pick it up and bring it here. Later, Dharma Master Baoning Yong said, "Not only could those two not lift it;
no one in the entire world could lift it either. Beigan dared to say: "Baoning was at his wits' end and exhausted his strength.
[He then] ascended the hall and, citing Zhaozhou’s entry into the monks’ hall where he cried, "A thief! A thief!", and upon seeing a monk, immediately seized him and said, "The thief is here!"
Here, a monk said, “It is not I. Zhou Tuo opened his mouth and said, “If it is so, then it is so; you simply refuse to take responsibility.

The Master said, “Zhaozhou’s way of gathering in was too lax, and his letting go was too hasty. Jingci, however, is not like this: ‘A house-thief is difficult to guard against; the family wealth will surely be lost.
He struck the ground with his staff and said, “One may err in seizing, but one must not err in releasing. (Chunyou Bingwu)
In the spring, he manifested illness. He requested a brush and wrote a verse at the bottom of a scroll, further inscribing the six characters: "The first day of the fourth month;
take care. When that date arrived, he passed away while dozing.
Chan Master Zheweng Ruyan of Jing Mountain in Lin’an Prefecture was the son of the Zhou family of Taizhou.
Once, while ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Jiangshan calls this a 'staff'; you all also call this a 'staff.
Is there any distinction between them? Though we lean on the same railing, we view the mountain colors differently."
Chan Master Wujie of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture inscribed this on the portrait of Layman Yu:
"When the donkey stumbled on the bridge over the stream, He mistakenly took cowpeas for pearls. His children could not conceal their father's disgrace;
They made old Guizhi of Yangqi laugh until he fell over."
Chan Master Dongchan Xingkong gave a discourse from the high seat. He raised the following case: National Teacher Yanguan was once asked by a monk, "What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana?
The Teacher said, "Bring me the pure water pitcher. When the monk brought the pitcher, the Teacher said, "Put it back where it was before.
The monk returned to ask the question again. The Teacher said, "The ancient Buddhas have long since passed away. The Master [Xingkong] said:
It is difficult for the blind to participate in the splendor of patterns; it is difficult for the deaf to participate in sounds.
Since this monk failed to grasp the Master's prompt, the National Teacher’s efforts were rendered in vain. Yunmen said, "There are no tracks or traces—this will not raise up the National Teacher."
Xuedou said: "One hand points to heaven, one hand points to earth—how could it be otherwise? Yet he could not help the National Teacher rise. With his whisk, he drew a stroke and said:
'The preceding complications are all cut off at once. Now tell me, after all, what is the *Ratnaśikhin* (Lushena) of the future body?
He threw down his whisk and descended from the seat."
The Chan Master Xian, known as Master Puguang of Shangfang, offered this eulogy for Bodhidharma: "A single word once uttered is as difficult to recall as a team of horses;
Fortunately, the Sovereign let him pass. At the heart of the Yangtze River, he ferried across on split reeds; How could the cresting waves have been as perilous as his question?"
Chan Master Xiuyan Shougui of Yuwang in Qingyuan Prefecture ascended the hall and said: He cited the Great Master Huayan’s question to Baoci:
“What is the true nature of the Buddha (tathatā-buddhadhātu)? Baoci replied, “Who does not have transformation? [Huayan] did not attain realization and subsequently requested instruction from Huguo.
Huguo said, “Who has transformation? At these words, he attained awakening. The Master said: “‘Who does not have it’ and ‘who has it’—this is the expression of the total function (quanji).”
To turn oneself around upon hearing a word is not clever at all. Even if one were to act before the words are raised, it would still be like mistaking a winnowing basket for an ironing board.
A-he-he! If a person can immediately mount a donkey backward, they will never again follow after others for the rest of their life.

Chan Master Yiyun Tugou of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an was a native of the Huang family of Minqing, Fuzhou.

Upon arriving in Wu, he met Tie’an, who invited him to serve in the Hall of Attendants. One day, in the meditation hall, Tie’an questioned him:
The National Teacher called to his attendant three times. The Master immediately raised his hand to cover the attendant’s mouth. He then asked, "When the attendant responded three times, what then?
The Master shook his sleeves and went straight out. National Teacher An was greatly pleased. At that time, Fozhao was preaching the Way at Lingyin; the Master went to rely upon him.
When Fozhao moved to Yuyang, he appointed the Master to share the seat with him. Upon hearing his preaching of the Dharma, Fozhao sighed in admiration, saying:
This son’s proclamation was just like that of the late Master Xuedou Xing; my almsbowl and staff have found their rightful heir.
He went forth to reside at great monasteries such as Xiangshan and Yuyang, yet by imperial decree he was summoned again to preach the Dharma at Jingci Temple.
A monk asked, "Regarding the words of Sansheng, 'When I meet a person, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for others'—what is the meaning of this? The Master replied, "The Eastern Dipper."
He moved westward. [A monk] asked, "Xinghua said, 'When I meet a person, I do not come forth; when I come forth, I am already for the person. What about this?
The Master said, "The Southern Dipper turns north; the top of the hall. Ascending the hall, he said: "A rushing torrent passes the blade; a swift flame exceeds the wind.
The simultaneous snapping and pecking—ten thousand *li* to Yuzhou. Some say it is like a man learning archery: through long practice one becomes skillful. But they do not realize that..."

as for Upādhyāya Fu saying, "The holy arrow has broken"—what was his meaning? He gave a shout and said:
"If you do not sleep in the same bed, how can you know the hole in the lining of the quilt? In the fifth month of the second year of the Kaiming era, the Master manifested his subtle departure.

Feeling ill, he composed a verse for the assembly, saying: "The mind is in a state of frantic turmoil; the spirits of ten thousand people are withered. Regarding the upward direction of the Buddha-dharma, when have I ever set foot there?
At the moment of death, karma-consciousness is vast and boundless; let the various quarters speculate as they will. Thereupon, he passed away in peace.

it was actually Old Li drinking private wine.

then both body and mind are fully resolved, which is not difficult. One need not worry that the protective talisman will not fall into one’s hands.
Thus it is said: "The lofty mountains and flowing waters harbor a profound meaning; there are those who naturally understand and smile with a nodding head."

*Caoshan*. A monk asked, "What is it like when the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month arrives? The Master said, "There is no one at the gate demanding payment. Suddenly, he manifested illness.

Gazing afar, there is no further speech; the great earth becomes level mud, and empty space shatters asunder.

Transverse and vertical, lively and agile—there is letting go and there is gathering in. What is this? When one leaf falls, the whole world [falls]."

Chan Master Dongshan Yuan’s Verse on Master Xiandao: "Pitiable indeed, amidst heaps of paper money; As soon as that foul mouth opens, it is but entanglement.
Having swept away the impoverished livelihoods of the ghostly realm, To this day, no one travels to the ancient temple."
Chan Master Bianshan Qian’s verse on the occasion of Li Ao’s visit to Yaoshan says: Valuing the ear while despising the eye, He draws the golden arrow from behind his back;
Looking up at the azure sky, The arrow has already passed beyond the kingdom of Silla.

Chan Master Wuliang Chongshou of Ruiyan in Qingyuan Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Ruyi of Yuyang, was once asked by a monk: "The World-Honored One attained enlightenment upon seeing the morning star;
what is the meaning of this? The Master replied with a verse: "The moment he saw the morning star, his eyelids were pierced through. Han speech and Hu speech—"
"Ten thousand, ten thousand, a thousand. A beggar who became wealthy overnight—do not speak such dreams. In whose hearth is there fire without smoke?

Chan Master Wujing Che, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Tiandong Pai, cited the case where a monk asked Yantou, "How does one establish oneself as the host amidst the dust? Yantou replied, "Copper."
A sand pan filled with oil. The Master composed a verse: "A million brave soldiers enter the Han Pass; Their majesty is like a fierce tiger, their array like a mountain.
With a single blade, he straightway takes Yan Liang’s head; Had it not been Lord Guan, it would have been most difficult indeed."
Chan Master Shantang Shanji of Huqiu Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture, a successor of Chan Master Guanzhi of Tiantong, offered this eulogy for the Image of Guanyin Carrying a Fish Basket:
"Thick clouds for hair and heavy makeup, she forces a smile with such toil; For the sake of others' affairs, she enters the dusty world. She carries here living beings, yet no one buys them; Only—"
Treat this as an ordinary death-merchandise.
Zen Master Lingyin Jingrou Ruju of Lin’an Prefecture, a dharma successor of Zen Master Tiandong Ying, was a native of Wuzhou. He studied under Chidun and once presented a verse.

He said: "At Mount Zhong, with white blades and bare bodies, I have endured being buried alive many times. Since my family was destroyed and I lost my kin, I have realized there is no fixed position to arrange.
Later, while presiding over the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "In this new year, we beat the new drum and universally bestow the new rain of Dharma.
All things are renewed; each and every one conforms to the rules. The Great Being Samantabhadra rejoices and rides forth."
At that moment, he opened the door and let out the White Elephant King; it was nowhere to be found across the earth.
Holding up his staff, he said, "Only this one does not belong to the old or the new. To open its mouth casually is to swallow the Dharma-body. He threw it down and asked, "What is it?
Inside a peach pit from a thousand years ago, there is still the original kernel. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Rotten."
Winter Melon.

Chan Master Huanglong Wumen Huikai of Hangzhou, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Wanshou Guan, was the son of the Liang family of Hangzhou. He studied under Yue-lin, contemplating the word "Mu" (No).
For six years, Zihu had no realization. He then roused his will and chastised himself, vowing: "If I do not cast off sleep, I shall let my body rot.
One day, while standing by the Dharma seat, he suddenly heard the sound of the meal drum and attained realization. He spoke this verse:

"A clear blue sky and a bright sun— A single clap of thunder, And the eyes of all living beings across the great earth are opened wide. The myriad phenomena and the entire universe bow their heads together; Mount Sumeru..."
[Pei] danced three times. On the following day, he entered the room intending to communicate what he had attained. Lin suddenly said, "Where have you seen gods or ghosts?
The Master gave a shout; Lin also shouted. The Master shouted again. From then on, their verbal exchanges were perfectly harmonious.
In the sixth year of the Chunyou era, by imperial decree, he opened the mountain at Huguo Renwang Temple. Ascending the hall, he said: "Right and wrong are long known to the ears."
The winds—do not seek difference or sameness within them at all. You must remain unmoved by the eight winds; let the ground of your mind be as equal to empty space.
Old Master Ciyun only knew how to set sail with the current, but could not steer against the wind. Huanglong was not so:
having cast away both right and wrong, he sought realization within right and wrong. Why is this? Several times black...
The wind overturned the great waves; it was never heard that the fishing boat capsized. During a year of severe drought, Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty summoned the Master to pray for rain.
Upon returning, he sat in silence. The Emperor sent an inner attendant to inquire about him, and the Master replied, "In stillness there is no movement;
only when moved does resonance follow. Thereupon, a great rain fell. The Emperor conferred upon him the title Chan Master Fuyan.
Chan Master Miaoyin of Zhushan in Tanzhou was reading a sutra while gazing at the moon. He spoke this verse: "Before the tongue has moved, the literary brilliance is revealed;

The five thousand scrolls are traversed all at once. If you say you must wait for the moon to open the volume again, I dare guarantee that by the time of your donkey years, you will still not have reached the end."

Chan Master Xuanzou Xingduan of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Wuzhen of Jing Mountain, the nineteenth generation descendant of Mount Nanyue. He was the son of the He family of Linhai in Taizhou. Initially, he studied under Master Zang.

The Master withdrew his sitting cloth. The Old Man said, "I grant you thirty blows; go to the hall for practice. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. One day, while attending him, the Old Man said, "There are no monks in my land of Quannan," and immediately added: "Even if you were to see the Buddha, you would have to kill him; Even if you were to see the Patriarchs, you would have to kill them. If you can do this, you may enter the gate of my house; If you cannot, you will surely fall into the pit of hell. The Master then composed a verse: "The Great Way has no gate; How could there be a need for a staff? If you wish to enter the gate of my house, First you must kill the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
