In the year Wushen of the Zhida era, when Huiji moved from Baizhang to Jingci Monastery, the Master went there to study under him.
He happened upon Huiji ascending the hall and reciting a verse on the karmic incident of Elder Fu of Taiyuan, who heard the sound of a horn.

He said, "Qinsheng has entered the blue seas, and Taishi has traveled to the famous mountains. From now on, along the roads outside the city of Yangzhou, the regulations are strict and do not permit the gates to open early.
At these words, [the student] attained realization; he went to the master’s chamber and presented his understanding. Zhi nodded in approval and appointed him to oversee the office of the secretary.

He served diligently for seven years. In the year of Bingchen during the Yan'you era, he presided over Xiangfu Temple and authored the *Fozu Tongzai* (Comprehensive Record of the Buddhas and Patriarchs) in two volumes.
Twelve fascicles. Circulated within the monastic communities.
Zen Master Wuwai Zongkuo of Donglin in Jiangzhou was a dharma heir of Zen Master Yuanjing Yin. He was the son of the Wei family of Nanchang. Initially, he studied under Yuetang. Tang...

He asked about the karmic conditions whereby the sound of a brook is entirely the broad and long tongue [of the Buddha]. Their spiritual capacities and words accorded with one another, and he was subsequently granted a seal of approval.
Initially he moved to Yunju; later he resided at Donglin. His verse on the eve of his death says: "At the age of seventy-one, my worldly ties have now come to an end."
He toppled the five Sumeru mountains; at midnight, the sun rose. He suddenly passed away.

Master Yi of Mount Meng, a Dharma successor of Master Ning of Gushan, went to Mount Wan to investigate the "Mu" (No) koan. Having not yet attained realization, he traveled to Chengtian Temple to pay his respects.
One day, while Master Guchan Ying was sitting in meditation, the Head Seat entered the hall to burn incense. When he struck the incense box, it made a sound, and [Master Ying] attained realization.
He offered this verse: "Path blocked, resources exhausted; I trampled over the waves and found them to be water. Transcending the crowd— The old Zhaozhou!"
"His face and features are just like this. Next, he relied upon Xutang. Xutang pointed to a vase-plum tree and said, "Those who can compose a verse may return to the hall.
The Master said, "Having fought back the masses of yin and attained his intent, he stands as the vernal champion atop the hundred flowers.
Behold his skillful means in benefiting others; he releases forth the harmonious breath of spring. Xutang said, "Go back to the hall. He then went to study under Huanshan.
One day, while ascending the stone ladder, he attained great enlightenment (the words of which appear in the Chapter on Mount Huan). He addressed the assembly: "It is in Suzhou; it is in Changzhou.
An octagonal millstone runs through the void. Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha—face-to-face, the entire platter is set forth.
With that, he overturned the meditation seat and departed with his sleeves brushed, saying, "How fortunate for the Dharma-gate! Should there be anyone who still hesitates...
For one who acts thus, I can only take you by the hand and lead you home. "Awakening to the Way upon hearing sound; clarifying the mind upon seeing form. Holding up his whisk, he asked, "Do you see?
What is it that sees? That is form. Which one is the mind? He gave a shout and said, "Do you hear? What is it that hears? That is sound. Which one is the Way?
Only when the true eye is suddenly opened right now does one gain entry to the gate. Yet even this is merely shedding the white robe [of the ordinary].
Śrāmaṇeras, you must strive to keep pace with the patch-robed monks and advance one more step beyond the tip of the pole.
True nature is profoundly still, transcending all names and forms; it is empty yet spiritual, quiescent yet wondrous. Those who awaken to it are called Great Dharma Kings.
As soon as they emerge from the mother’s womb, they immediately walk seven steps, gaze in the four directions, point one finger to heaven and one finger to earth. Heaven...
"Up above in heaven, I alone am honored. But tell me, what matter does this clarify?
If you can realize it here, you will see that at every moment there are Buddhas descending to be born, and in every thought-moment there are Buddhas attaining enlightenment.
The Master established three "gate-words" (san guan yu) to test his students, saying: "When a tiny gnat sucks dry the vast ocean, where do the fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs find a place to dwell?"
He established his destiny. Again he said: "The water-jelly flies up to the Ultimate Heaven of Form (Rūpākṛtsna-dhyāna) and enters the eye of Maheśvara to perform a dance;
why is it not seen? Again he said: "The Lotus Lake Bridge is a direct pointing for all people; why does the person with clear eyes fall into the well?"

Chan Master Wuyong Kuan of Taho, Shuzhou, was a successor of Chan Master Zhennan of Jin Niu. When Yiyuan came to visit him, the Master asked, "Where have you come from? Yiyuan replied, "From Tongzhou.

The Master asked, "Regarding the tides of the Huai and Hai rivers lately, what is their state—full or empty? Yiyuan said, "They flood the sun and reach to the heavens; not even a single drop remains."
Tid. The Master said, "It does not touch the main channel. Yuan said, "Please, Master, speak. The Master then gave a shout.

On another day, he raised the verse on Realizing the Way and asked, "A flash of lightning strikes; with no regard for one's whole body, in the very moment of hesitation, there is no path for sage or ordinary being.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Yuan said, "When sparks fly and stars scatter, what hesitation could there be? To meet the situation face-to-face, there is no..."
"Is it so? The Master let out a thunderous shout. Yuan said, "What was that shout for? The Master replied, "Before the mountain of melons, he swallows a shoulder pole;
he seizes the clear breeze and strips off its skin. Yuan could not help but break into a profuse sweat.
He immediately prostrated himself on the ground and said, "Only today do I understand the Master’s application. The Master said, "Shut your mouth!"

Chan Master Haiyun Yinjian of Qingshou Monastery in Yanjing was a dharma heir of Chan Master Qingshou Zhang. He was the son of the Song family from Ningyuan in Shanxi. From birth, he possessed spiritual insight.
At the age of seven, his father taught him the "Opening the Sect and Clarifying the Meaning" chapter of the *Classic of Filial Piety*. The Master asked, "What is the sect that is being opened?"
"What does 'the enlightened one' (ming) mean? the father asked in astonishment. Thereupon, he took Zhongguan Zhao as his teacher.
One day, while supporting Zhao as he walked, Zhao said, "Master Faldeng’s Way says: 'Look at how busy his household affairs are! Now tell me, by whose power does this come about?
How do you understand this? The Master gave Zhao's hand a sudden tug. Zhao said, 'You wild fox spirit! The Master said, 'Yes, yes. Zhao said:"
One must further investigate this separately. Later, during a gathering while leaning on his staff, he encountered rain at Songpu (Pine Post) and stayed overnight beneath a cliff.
While striking a fire, he attained great enlightenment. He rubbed his own face and said, "Only today do I know that my eyebrows are horizontal and my nose is vertical.

He then took faith in the words of the old monks throughout the land, which are never spoken in vain. He visited Chan Master Zhonghe Zhang and subsequently received the seal of transmission (as recorded in the *Zhonghe Zhang*). The year was Xinmao.
The Master was celebrating his birthday. One day, he encountered several monks in the corridor. He asked the first monk, "Where are you going?
The monk replied, "To see the flowers. The Master struck him. He asked the second monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "To prostrate before the Buddha.
The Master struck him as well. He asked the third monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "Where are you going? The Master struck him as well. Then he asked the fourth monk.
"Where are you going? The monk was speechless; the Master struck him as well. He asked the fifth monk, "Where are you going?
He replied, "I am going to look for the Master. The Master said, "Why do you look for him? He said, "To give him a beating. The Master said, "With what will you beat him?"
He said, "Bring me the staff to strike you. The Master struck him four times and said, "You are a fellow who traffics in empty talk.

The assembly all fled. The Master called out, "Venerable elders! The assembly turned their heads. The Master asked, "What is it? Later, he passed away; his posthumous title was Buddhadayuanming Dafo (Buddha-Sun Perfectly Bright Great Buddha).
Chan Master Nanshi Wenxiu of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou,

a successor in the twenty-first generation under the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Wanshou Ren of South Peak, was the son of the Li family of Kunshan in Suzhou. He left the household life in his home district.
He resided at Shaolong Monastery, where he once questioned Chan Master Xingzhong of Huqiu on the essentials of the Dharma and attained the meaning beyond words.

In the fifth year of the Hongwu era, he took up residence at Pumen Monastery in Suzhou. On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked: "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, the heavens rained down four kinds of flowers;
when you, Master, appear in the world, what auspicious signs are there? The Master said: "One ox drinks water, and five horses do not neigh. The monk asked again: [The Master replied: "..."
"If it is thus, then the meaning of joyful serenity is transmitted through the ages; the patriarchal style of silent illumination spreads in all four directions.
The Master said, "Better that such good things never happened. He moved to Lingyan. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The treasury of the true Dharma-eye spans from antiquity to the present;
the true lamp of Prajñā illuminates heaven and earth. Facing it directly, there is no front or back; right here, there is nothing to accept or take up. It is vividly manifest alone, penetrating—"
Form penetrates sound; it manifests expansively before one. Beyond hearing and beyond seeing, it is ever-present in all places, yet is not constrained by any place.
It is not separate from any time, yet is not encompassed by any time. Herein, one sees that there is neither delusion nor enlightenment, neither after nor before.
The hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable wondrous meanings are fully realized without relying on thought.
All are fully complete. Within the dharma of manifesting transformation, this may indeed be acceptable.

However, if one is within the school of the patch-robed monks (śramaṇas), one must directly take wide strides atop a hundred-foot pole, hide one's body within the eye of a gnat, cast the Sahā world away to another realm, and pick up the Abhirati world and bring it here to this land.
One does not know by what power of grace one has attained such marvels. After a long silence, he said: "Accustomed."
Passing before the Five Phoenix Pavilion, he held a golden whip in his hand and celebrated the Great Peace. Not long after, he retired to live in seclusion above the Wu and Song rivers.

At the beginning of the Yongle era, an imperial decree was issued for scholars, Buddhists, and Daoists throughout the realm who were profoundly versed in literary meaning to compile the *Yongle Dadian*.
The Master responded to the summons and rose to serve; he remained in the capital for three years. In the summer of the seventh year, he resided at Mount Jing.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad phenomena of the forest and all things are sealed by a single Dharma. What is in front of you is Bowls Peak; what is in the middle is the Buddha Hall.
What do you call 'the Single Dharma'? After a long silence, he said: "National Teacher Guoyi was originally a native of Kunshan.
Four years later, the Master, due to old age and illness, retired to the Songyuan Cloister on North Mountain in Suzhou. He passed away without illness.

[The Record of] the Passing of Chan Master Xibai Lijin of Tianning Monastery in Xingfu Prefecture, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Ming of Mount Jingshan. He was the son of the Yao family of Wu Commandery. In his youth, he relied upon Baoji [Monastery].
He received the tonsure at the monastery. Initially, he visited Guding, who presented him with the story of Deshan seeing Longtan.
From this, he attained realization. In the *dingyou* year of the Zhizheng era, he resided at Rui Guang Monastery. When Tian Ning Temple was destroyed by fire, the Master undertook its restoration.

The Imperial Preceptor conferred upon him the title "Universal Salvation of Perfect Penetration" (*Yuantong Pujie*). Since his youth, the Master had lost his father and only his mother remained; thus, he departed for a location one [li] east of the city.

He abandoned his construction projects and established Guyun-an (Solitary Cloud Hermitage) to provide for his parents' support. Some criticized him for this, but the Master rebuked them, saying, "Do you not see the venerable master Bianpu Chen?

Why do you speak so lightly? At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he served as the abbot of Jingci Temple. In the spring of the fourth year, by imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Tienjie Temple.
In the winter of the fifth year, an imperial decree ordered the holding of a Great Assembly, and the Emperor’s carriage arrived in person to attend. He then commanded—

The Master propagated the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*). From the dukes and marquises down to the common officials, all gathered around to listen; there was none who was not delighted and won over.
One day, he suddenly said to his disciples, "I have a karmic debt from a former life that remains unsettled; I must surely repay it. Do not constrain me with worldly appearances.
Shortly thereafter, manifesting a slight illness, he passed away in accordance with the natural course. He was enshrined in a stupa at Jiaxing.
At the Huancui Hermitage west of the city was Chan Master Xiangyuan Renshu of Jingshan in Hangzhou, a native of Taizhou. One day, he rushed through the gate and cried out, "The execution has arrived!
The execution has arrived! How can one avoid it? Thereupon, he sat upright and passed away.

Chanshi Jueyuan Huitan of Tianjie Monastery in Nanjing was a dharma successor of Chan Master Longxiang. He was the son of the Yang family of Tiantai. His mother conceived him after dreaming of swallowing a bright pearl.
Upon his birth, his countenance was strikingly dignified. In his youth, he did not associate with other children; as he grew up, he relied upon Faguo of Yue.
He left home to become a monk at the temple and soon received full ordination. He thoroughly mastered and practiced the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra* and the teachings on *śamatha-vipaśyanā*.
At that time, Xiaoyin was propagating the Way in Central India. The Master went to visit him. Xiaoyin asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from traveling the mountains.

Xiaoyin said, "When the bamboo hat beneath you was pressed through to the bottom—how was it when you were universally visiting masters like Luopu? The Master replied, "It was presented before I had even entered the gate."
"It seems you have understood," said Yinyuan. "Why then do you not bring it forth right now? As the Master hesitated, Yinyuan let out a shout.

At that moment, the Master experienced a sudden, liberating realization. On another day, Yinyuan spread both hands wide and showed them to the Master, saying, "It has been opened wide with eight characters."
"Why do you refuse to accept? The Master said, "Stop trying to be so dull-witted. Yinyue said, "Come closer and I will explain it to you.
The Master immediately covered his ears and departed. Yinyue nodded in approval. He first resided at Zutang of Niushou and Qingliang of Shicheng;

subsequently, he moved to Baoning and Jiangshan. When the imperial decree changed Longxiang to Tianjie, the Emperor summoned the Master to serve as its abbot, specifically conferring upon him the title.
The Great Chan Master Yanfan Shanshi Ligu Chongjiao ascended the hall. He said: "A single phrase—pitch black, yet without a handle;
it has its standard. After a long silence, he asked: 'Do you understand? The pestle pounds in the southeast; the millstone grinds in the northwest. He then ascended the hall."
Before the peak of Shaoshi and beneath the gate of Caoxi, the lamps have been passed from one to another in succession, transmitted with absolute clarity.
From antiquity to the present, not even a hair’s breadth has changed. By what means may this be verified? On the upper and lower terraces, fire illuminates fire;

as carriages and horses pass to and fro, people look upon people. Entering the hall: those who are tall are the Dharma-body of tallness; those who are short are the Dharma-body of shortness. This very moment before us—
The assembly sat and stood, solemnly, some tall and some short; everyone knew and saw this clearly. Ultimately, which among them is the Dharmakāya?
If you can understand this, you may take up your alms bowl and go to the world of Gandhavyūha to eat your meal.

If you do not understand, then simply eat your gruel and rice on your long bench in the dormitory. [He] ascended the hall: "For the sutras there are masters of the sutras; for the śāstras there are masters of the śāstras. The Dragon...
The river releases a single thread, branching into sections and divisions as it flows away. Holding up his staff and striking it once, he said, "Tell me, what verse is this?
He ascended the hall and said, "This is simply a ready-made koan. Among the assembly, there are many who understand it, yet not a few who misunderstand it.
Consequently, gold and jade are not distinguished, and precious stone and common rock are not separated. Here at Longhe, I insist on—"
[The Master] discerned them and said, "Venerable Zhang! Venerable Li! One has long arms; the other has large eyes.
Both are just like the school of Bodhidharma today. Who will take up this burden? *Huh!* [He] descended from the seat. [Later,] he ascended the hall and said:
"Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja and after Maitreya Buddha, there is a ready-made public case that I have not yet dared to give."

You have spoken of "breaking through. Why? Because the mind owes nothing to others, and the face bears no color of shame. He shows it to the assembly: The spring breeze sweeps vast and wide; the spring days linger on.
A yellow oriole sings upon the branches of a hundred flowers. Within this, there is boundless meaning; who knows its secret message?
Before he had finished speaking, a monk stepped forward and asked, "What is it like when the mind, intellect, and consciousness cannot be suppressed?

The Master said in a stern voice, "Who is there to suppress them? He then addressed the monk within the room, saying, "During the twelve periods of the day and night, you have no share in chewing and swallowing;

you have no share in seeking and pursuing. Do you understand? The monk was at a loss. The Master said, "If you do not understand three eights and nine, it will be difficult to avoid sinking of your own accord."
*Yin*. In the third year of the Hongwu era, he was dispatched as an envoy to the Western Regions and arrived at the kingdom of Siṃhala. Its king served him at the Fo-shan Vihāra.
In the ninth month of the following year, he addressed the assembly regarding the interment [of his remains] within the Pratyekabuddha Stūpa.

Previously, that Buddha had made a prophetic declaration, and the current opening for interment now perfectly accords with those words. Upon the Minister’s return report, the Emperor issued an imperial edict bestowing upon him the robes of the deceased for the burial.
To the left of Huayu Terrace was the Zen Master Jitan Zongle of Tianjie Monastery in Nanjing. He was the son of Zhou of Linhai in Tai.

From the moment of his birth, he sat in the full lotus posture, which amazed people. At the age of eight, he followed Xiaoyin to study Buddhism; upon merely glancing over the Tripitaka, he could recite it from memory.
One day, Yinyuan asked, "The National Teacher called out three times, and the attendant responded three times. What do you make of this?
The Master said, "How can you turn meat into a sore? Yinyuan said, "I thought you were extraordinary; now I see that there is nothing to be gained. The Master gave a shout.

Yinyi raised his staff as if to strike; the Master shook out his sleeves and departed. At the end of the Yuan dynasty, Yinyi resided at Mount Jing; in the first year of the Hongwu era, he moved to Zhongzhu. He ascended the hall and said:
"The Diamond King’s sword is brandished horizontally, and a thousand demons vanish from sight. The Śakrāloka eye shines through with clarity, and the myriad things hide their forms.

Reaching this point, the rolling up and unfolding are within oneself; killing and giving life are applied according to the moment. It is truly enough to cause the Thousand-Year Rock to extend its arms in joy."

"Pao-tiao! The waters of the Qiantang River flow eastward, yet they flow backward. Do you all know that this is so, or not? He then held up his whisk and said, "The stone pillar in front of the courtyard has sprouted branches;
see how the phoenix dwells upon its lofty boughs. Emperor Taizu Gao (the Hongwu Emperor) issued an edict to summon eminent monks from throughout the realm who were learned and practiced in the Way.
The Master was the first to respond. By imperial decree, he came to preside over Tianjie Monastery.
In the year Ding-si, he was dispatched as an envoy to the Western Regions. In the fifteenth year, he returned to court; on all occasions, his responses accorded with the Emperor’s wishes.
When Empress Gao passed away, wind, rain, thunder, and lightning broke out during the period leading up to the burial. The Emperor was deeply displeased and suddenly summoned the Master, saying:

The Empress Dowager was about to proceed with the burial. "You must proclaim a verse," she said. The Master immediately responded: "Rain falls as Heaven sheds tears; Thunder rolls as Earth raises a lament.
Sons of the Buddhas from the Western Heavens Together escort the Tathāgata of the Horse. The Emperor was greatly pleased and subsequently raised the hearse.
He issued an edict bestowing one hundred taels of white silver upon him. Later, however, he incurred reprimand due to his association with the Hu faction and retired to reside at Chaya in Fengyang.

Feng. In the nineteenth year [of the Hongwu era], he brought him back to reside there. After some time, he retired due to old age. Crossing the river, he arrived at Shifo Temple in Jiangpu where he manifested illness.
Calling to his attendant, he said, "What is this? The attendant was bewildered. The Master said, "Suffering," and then passed away.
This was in the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu era; he was seventy-four years of age. His stupa was erected behind that of Master Yan at Tianjie Temple.
Chan Master Yuantong Yuezhi Chongfu was the son of the Chen family of Piling.
He went to visit Xiaoyin, who raised the koan of Linji’s “True Person of No Rank” and interrogated him, saying, “Do you know this yet? Without hesitation, the Master prostrated himself.
Yinyue said, "What have you seen that you prostrate? The Master replied, "The one being bowed to is not another.
Yinyue said, "That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure. The Master replied, "Master, please do not deceive people. Yinyue nodded in agreement.
Initially he resided at Nanchan, then at Yuantong, which coincided with the prophecy regarding the redness of Daoji’s stupa. He was subsequently transferred to Yuyang during the Hongwu era.
In the autumn of the fifth year, the Emperor established a Dharma assembly at Mount Zhong. The Master responded to the summons and arrived.
In the private hall, the Emperor questioned him on the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma. The Master presented a verse, which greatly pleased the Emperor; he was granted a meal.
While the Master was resting briefly before the Emperor, his breathing made a slight sound. A neighboring courtier pulled his robe to alert him. The Emperor laughed and said, "This old man."
Wu Jixin was truly a virtuous spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*). Later, he entered *parinirvāṇa* and was interred in a stupa on Stone Ear Peak.
Foyong Zhenfu Liang of Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou was a descendant in the tenth generation of Fan Wenzheng Gong.
He shaved his hair at the age of fifteen; upon receiving full ordination, he said, "I study the Buddha-dharma in order to clarify the mind. Without a teacher, the mind cannot be realized."
To demonstrate his grasp of the essential points, he subsequently joined Xixian at Longxiang Monastery. Upon first seeing him, Xixian recognized his potential.

On another occasion, when the Master asked further questions, his speech became even more forceful. Xixian smiled and said, "You have indeed attained it, yet in the end, you have merely reached the secondary meaning."
After a long time, he finally attained realization of the Dharma of the mind. Later, he appeared in the world at Zisheng Temple in Jiaxing, and in his later years resided at Lingyin.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "The single school of Bodhidharma has declined until it is nearly extinct. You all must apply yourselves with effort as if your hair were on fire.
Yet, the hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable wondrous meanings can be fully known within the tip of a single hair. If you know this, then even the vast becomes small."
The earth shall become gold; you should accept this without hesitation, otherwise you will incur the shame of eating the bread of idleness.
Time flows like lightning; you must urgently cultivate yourselves toward the higher goal. On the sixteenth day of the first month in the fourth year of Hongwu, he passed away.
Chan Master Qingyuan Huaiwei of Baoxiang Temple in Shaoxing Prefecture was a native of the Wei clan of Nanchang and the nephew of Xiaoyin.
At birth, a divine mushroom grew from a locust tree in his courtyard; subsequently, he displayed exceptional brilliance, reciting the classics without waiting for formal instruction from a teacher.
At that time, Yinzhu was residing at Longxiang. Hearing of this, he said with joy, "This is a 'thousand-li colt' of our school. He invited him to his presence.
As Longxiang was a metropolitan center in the southeast, eminent scholars from all quarters frequented Yinzhu.

Some revealed the secrets of heaven and human nature, while others expounded the methods of literary composition and the opening of the gates [of eloquence]. The Master was able to hear these teachings, and his learning progressed greatly; everyone vied to admire him.
Muzhi said, "This man is a tiger among scholars. The Master replied, "Do you gentlemen think that I am specializing solely in this field?
Buddhist Dharma and worldly laws do not contradict one another; therefore, I have engaged in this with my remaining strength merely to bring luster to its religious tradition.
If you were to boast based on this, would you truly know me? One day, Yinying was startled and inspired; among his disciples, there had been none [who had achieved such things].
"Correct," [the Master] replied. Yunzheng stepped straight forward and spoke bluntly; Yunzhen shook his staff and let out a single shout. The Master’s spirit was not the least bit discouraged.
As they engaged in a back-and-forth exchange of difficult questions and challenges, Yunzhen laughed and said, "You may enter my chamber. He appointed him as the Head of the Record Office (Jishi).

As Yunzhen approached death, he summoned the Master, saying, "I have occupied this master’s seat for over forty years. The number of people I have encountered is not small, yet none were able to propagate the Way of Dahui so that it would not..."
"Those who have fallen [into error] are none other than you and Zongle. You must exert yourself! Later, you presided over Baoxiang in Kuaiji, Baoguo in Hangzhou, and Daochang on Lake [West].
During the Hongwu era, you presided over Jingci. While the Master was traveling to transform others, a Mrs.
Chen requested instruction from him. The woman suddenly attained a realization; before the Master had walked even a hundred paces, the woman and her family..."
He passed away while seated in his quarters.
Chan Master Gufeng Mingde of Daochang Monastery in Anji Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Zhuti Lin. His surname was Zhu, and his family lineage was from Changguo in Mingzhou.
His father had a close friendship with Pu-tuo Jie. Having heard the cry of a rooster, Jie entered the Way; whenever he preached the Dharma, he would invariably flap his wings and crow like a rooster.
Long after Jie had passed away, the mother dreamed that Jie came to seek lodging. Upon waking, she became pregnant and gave birth after fourteen months.
While still a child, she delighted in sitting in the lotus posture. When asked what she sought to attain, she replied, "I wish to study seated meditation and seek to become a Buddha."
Thus it was. When he grew up and became a monk, he first went to visit Zhuxi. Zhuxi asked, "From where have you come? The Master replied, "I have come from Mount Jing'e.
Zhuxi asked, "How high is Mount Jing'e? The Master replied, "Its peak is not visible. Zhuxi rebuked him.

One day, Zhuxi raised the anecdote of the World-Honored One holding up a flower. The Master suddenly felt as though he had attained an understanding. Later, he visited Huiji at Jingci Temple. Huiji asked:
"Who comes like this? The Master replied, "Hū Zhangsan and Hē Lisi. Jī asked, "From morning until evening, while you are putting on clothes and eating meals, do you still recognize yourself?
The Master replied, "Hū Zhangsan and Hē Lisi. Jī raised his staff. The Master shook out his sleeves and left.
One day, he arrived at Xuedou, where he encountered Zhutian ascending the hall to give a discourse, citing the story of Yishan's mud.
Regarding the "Story of the Ox Entering the Sea": At this, the Master’s many doubts were suddenly dispelled. Later, he resided at Dongchan in Songjiang, and subsequently moved to Baoning and Jingci.
At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he retired to his home monastery at Zhulin Hermitage. One day, he instructed his disciples, saying:
"Though my body is humble, the one true, perfect nature is equal to that of the Tathāgata. Worldly phenomena arise and perish no differently than sparks from a flint or a flash of lightning."
"Practice diligently day and night without giving rise to regression. After my passing, you should follow the Buddha’s regulations and consign me to cremation;
do not allow the fourfold assembly to wear hempen clothing and wail. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
Jiefeng visited Chan Master Cheng, Zhishan of Daci in Hangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Xin of Tianchi. The Master said, "Where did you see those gods and ghosts come from?
Jiefeng said, "I have caught the thief. The Master asked, "Where is the stolen property? Jiefeng gave a shout. The Master said:
"Neither opening the mouth nor closing the mouth is the upward path. Bring forth a phrase. Feng said, "The entire world is clearly manifest, not hidden away.
The Master raised his bamboo stick and said, "To call it a 'bamboo stick' is to encounter resistance;
not to call it a 'bamboo stick' is to turn one's back. What do you call it? Feng then overturned the meditation seat. The Master struck the bamboo stick three times and said, "Blind!"
"Han, you dare to come here and stroke a tiger's whiskers! Feng then prostrated himself and attended the Master for three years.
One day the Master said, "The ancients sought teachers and chose friends so as not to let their time go to waste.

Although you have attained the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, you have not yet been able to turn yourself around toward the Ultimate. Thereupon he cited the case of Fenyang seeing Shoushan, who said: "Ten thousand ages, the azure pool is empty..."
Realm Moon. Only after repeated searching and grasping can one begin to know; only then does the Peak allow for a fleeting glimpse.
Chan Master Tieguan Fashu of Tianbao Mountain in Jianning Prefecture was a native of the Lin family of Pingyang, Wenzhou.

At the age of seventeen, he went to Huazang to pay respects to Zhuxi and took him as his teacher. Having received full ordination, he studied under Zhongfeng and Wumen, but found no resonance. Thereupon, he visited...
At Shimen, Yuanwu instructed him to contemplate the saying, "The three 'nots'. One day, after the midday meal, as he stepped off his mat, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
He composed a verse, saying: "Not mind, not Buddha, not things; I have squeezed out the very bones of empty space. A golden-maned lion cub— How could it linger in a wild fox den?
Hu! Hu! He immediately went to the abbot’s quarters. Yuanwu asked, "What is it? The Master replied, "Nanquan has been caught by me!"
He was defeated. The Old Man said, "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, it is not an object—what is it?
The Master said, "A set of bones for teeth; two pieces of skin for ears. The Old Man said, "Not so. Speak another way.

The Master said, "The singing of the oriole, the warbling of the swallow, the chirping of the magpie, the cawing of the crow. The Old Man said, "Wrong. The Master also said, "Wrong. The Old Man said, "Where is Nanquan now?"
"Where is he? The Master then gave a shout. The elder said, "Setting aside that one shout, where is Nanquan? The Master shook his sleeves and departed.
Thereupon, he traveled extensively to study under various masters before returning to Shimen, where he remained in attendance, managing the master’s robes and whisk for fifteen years.
He then traveled south to Jianzhou, where the regional commander invited him to head Tianbao Temple. Later, he resided again at Puzhai in Songxi. Ascending the hall, he said: "Fu fu."
"Fu! Mo mo mo! Cuò cuò cuò! He looked at his attendant and asked, "Does this old monk still have his tongue? In the third year [of his retirement], he returned to Tianbao.
On the fifteenth day of the eighth month of the sixth year of the Zhizhi era (1279), he wrote a verse: "Fundamentally there is no coming or going;
one phrase of gold lifts the crimson clouds, pierces the azure void, and the bright sun circles Mount Sumeru. Having cast down his pen, he passed away.

Chan Master Tieshan Qiong, a successor of Chan Master Mengshan Yi, went to visit Xueyan. Xueyan asked, "What matter do you have? The Master replied, "The Five-Phoenix Pavilion before my gate is magnificent.
Xueyan struck him two or three dozen times with his staff and said, "Not yet; go back and apply yourself to your practice. [The Master] then requested paper...
He received these words of Dharma: "The wind blows through the forest leaves; the four windows are empty and bright. Sitting alone on a single branch, the myriad phenomena are as clear as a mirror.
You have managed to prop up an iron boat and carry an iron mountain down into the sea; only then will I speak to you.
That each and every thing is already fully manifest is still to mistake the zero point on a scale. The Buddha-dharma is like a vast ocean; ahead, the surging waves reach the heavens. Turning—
Entering ever deeper, the verse says: "When the void is squeezed until it shatters into dust, Flowers bloom upon iron trees and jade branches scatter.

This is the upward matter for perpetuating the Buddha-seed; Yet behind the head, as before, one blow remains lacking. Once, while suffering from a headache and wishing to decoct medicine, he took a medicinal jar in his hand.
Encountering Jue Chibi, [he said: "You must be the Prince Nalaka, who cut his own flesh to give to his mother."
Only after returning the bones to one's father can one begin to preach the Dharma for one’s parents. Suddenly, he shattered his mass of doubt and uttered this verse:
"A jade tower appears upon a single blade of grass; I have discerned the idle topics of past and present.
Lifting the moon from the peak of Jiyun Peak, I toss it before people like a ball of flowers. Upon the passing of Zhizhan, he went to Donglin because of Dongyan.
Next, during a period of private instruction (入室), [the Master] raised a question: "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way. How do you understand this?
The Master replied, "To cry out in grievance while clutching one's own stolen goods. [The Master] asked, "If it is neither mind, nor Buddha, nor any thing, what is it?

The Master replied, "A falcon from Liaotian flies straight out from between the eyebrows. Later, when he arrived at Mount Meng, every time he entered for private instruction, he would simply say, "I am still lacking. Later, at Ding...

He struck the character "deficiency" (欠). Thereupon, his body and mind were suddenly and thoroughly penetrated to the very marrow of his bones. He seized Mount Shan and said, "What have I lacked all these years?
Mount Shan clapped his hands three times. The Master prostrated three times. Again he said, "O Mute Iron Mountain, you have occupied this position for many years;
today it is finally finished. The following year, he served as the Head Seat. On the winter solstice, he held the whisk and said: "Winter is in the month..."
In spring, sell the quilt to buy the ox; in winter, at the end of the month, sell the ox to buy the quilt.
[Zhaozhou] leaned on his staff and said: "Here there is no 'end. Midway, we rest together. Walking, rest and rest; staying, rest and rest; sitting, rest and rest; lying down, rest and rest.
When sleep is cast off, the five clouds manifest their auspiciousness. Radiant wind and clear moon reach everywhere. The plum blossoms on the withered branch."
Branches. At an ancient ferry-head, amidst the wind, the dark fragrance occasionally drifts forth. Although one has reached this point, as for the single path that transcends all:
how can one perceive it at the precipice ten thousand *li* from Chuzhou? Leaning on his staff, he said, "Enough, enough."
Chan Master Zhuyuan Shuisheng of Miaoguo on West Lake was a dharma heir of Chan Master Wuneng. He was the son of the Fan family from Leping in Rao.
He first visited Master Yueting Zhong at Jiangshan, where Guzhou Ji served as the First Seat. [Shuisheng] took up the words spoken by Mount Wan regarding Mount Meng.
He showed it to him. Five years later, [Zhao]zhou attained a realization. Linji said, "Master Moshan once said: 'The monk Song was born without the two conditions.
After Bodhidharma was buried at Xiong'er Mountain, he returned to the West with a single shoe. Was this truly due to supernatural powers, or is the Dharma simply like this?
The Master replied, "It is merely that both his physical form and spirit were wondrous. Linji said, "Not so. You shall understand this for yourself in the future."
He understood this. The Master went to Wúwéi Prefecture to see Wúnéng, taking what Jì had raised as a point of inquiry. Wúnéng said, "It is because you do not understand.

The Master suddenly attained great realization. In the *Jǐyǐ* year of the Tiānlì era, he presided over Mìguǒ Monastery on West Lake. In the summer of the *Dīnghài* year of the Zhìzhèng era, he manifested his passing.
The Chan Master Rūhai Zhen of Mount Jingyun in Chongqing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Wuyong Kuan. When Master Bi-feng visited him, the Master drew a circle on the ground.
Bi-feng brushed it away with his sleeve. The Master drew another circle, and Bi-feng added a stroke across its center.
He wiped it away again. The Master painted it once more as before. The Peak added another stroke to form a cross.
He wiped it away again. The Master painted it yet again as before. The Peak added four corner strokes to the cross to form the *svastika* (卍) symbol. He wiped it away again.
The Master then drew thirty circular diagrams in total. Xuan answered each one individually. The Master said, "Only now do you realize that the Buddha-dharma is so vast and supreme.
Xuan went to Shuofang, where his Way flourished greatly.
Chan Master Yongning of Longchi Yiyuan in Changzhou was the son of the Zhu family in Tongzhou, Huaidong. His family had been a lineage of officials for generations.
At the age of nine, he earnestly sought to leave secular life and took ordination at Guanghui Temple in Lihe Prefecture. This temple was a renowned monastery of the region;
during the Song dynasty, Chan Master Zhao of Huaihai had preached the Dharma there to save sentient beings, making his fame heard throughout the time. On the eve [of Yongning’s ordination],...

The assembly of monks at the temple shared a dream that they were welcoming [the Master] from Huaihai. On the following day, the Master arrived; those who understood this marveled at it. He went to visit Wuyong at Taihu.

Wuyong’s monastic style was lofty and severe; as soon as the Master entered the gate, Wuyong shouted at him and drove him out. The Master performed a prostration outside the gate and stood there with palms joined.
After a long time, Wuyong finally permitted him to enter for an audience. The Master withdrew to the meditation hall and remained there throughout the night without sleeping.
While sleeping one day, he heard Yong cite Yunmen’s words, "A single thought does not arise. Before the sound had even faded, he attained realization.
He hurried into the hall, and Yong struck him immediately. Recognizing that the Master had attained sudden enlightenment, Yong ordered him to compose a verse on the story of Zhaozhou’s dog.
The Master composed it on the spot, saying: "Zhaozhou’s dog has no Buddha-nature; The myriad phenomena all beg for their lives together. An bottomless basket..."

A dead snake. Adding much and subtracting little leaves nothing behind; he used this as a cause for a silent, profound smile. In the Guihai year of the Zhizhi era, he was invited to Longchi in Yixing to establish a Chan monastery.
He selected a remote peak to build a dwelling where he resided. Later, he emerged to preside over various monasteries, including Lishan and Tianning.
Emperor Shundi of the Yuan dynasty bestowed upon him the title "Great Chan Master Fohsin Liaowu. He subsequently returned to Longchi.
In the sixth month of the Jǐyǒu year of the Hongwǔ era, he manifested a slight illness. He instructed his disciples to cut paper and prepare inner and outer robes, saying, "I am about to depart.
He moved his reliquary shrine to a remote mountain peak. After seventeen days, the Master arose, bathed, and sought a brush to write a verse:
"Seventy-eight years of guarding simplicity; A clear and bright scene of failure. The clay ox turns its body at the bottom of the sea."
In the sixth month, amidst the blazing heat, snow fell. Having finished writing, he lay on his side and passed away.
He was the twenty-second generation descendant of Nanyue and the Dharma heir of Chan Master Yin of Shuanglin.
Chan Master Yuejiang Zongjing of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was the son of the Ni family of Lanxi in Jinhua.

While reciting the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he reached the passage on "the finger pointing at the moon" and attained a sudden realization. He went to visit Zheng’an, who asked, "When Huangbo struck Linji, what did you do?
The Master replied, "I pressed down the ox's head so it would eat grass. Later, while residing at Mount Jing, he wrote a verse as he approached his final passing.
He said, "A guest at the gate of the Patriarchs speaks of non-arising with open mouth; I, an old man, do not understand a hundredth part of it—midday strikes the third watch.
Thereupon he passed away.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Tan of Tianjie.

Chan Master Dingyan Jingjie of Linggu Temple in Nanjing went to visit Jueyuan. Jueyuan presented him with the karmic cause and condition regarding the bursting of a wooden barrel hoop and questioned him about it.
As the Master hesitated and was about to respond, Jueyuan said in a stern voice, "It is already eight *ke* late! At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Subsequently, the Master compiled the *Xukeng Songgu Lianzhu* (The Continued Carving of Linked Pearls on Ancient Cases) for circulation within the monastic community.
Chan Master Jiefeng Shiyu of Wushan Mountain in Quzhou was a successor of Chan Master Dachicheng. He was the son of the Yu family from Xi'an in the prefecture.
Initially, he studied under a dozen masters, including Guranya and Shimen, receiving their dharma talks. Subsequently, he studied under Zhiryan, who raised the question: "It is not this."
"The mind is neither Buddha nor a thing. One night, sitting until the latter part of the night, he heard a neighboring monk recite the *Zhengdao ge* (Song of Realizing the Way):

"Do not eliminate delusive thoughts, do not seek the truth. Suddenly, he felt as if a heavy burden had been lifted from his shoulders. He uttered this verse: "Time and again we face each other, yet never meet;
Having exhausted my mother’s life-force, my strength is spent. At midnight, suddenly forgetting the finger that points to the moon, The void bursts forth."
As the sun rose, it was red. Yuanwu went to see him and asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Daci.
Yuanwu asked, "How deep is Daci’s nostril? The Master struck his staff once. Yuanwu said, "If the staff were broken, what would you strike with?
The Master then bowed and said, "Today I have personally seen the Teacher. Yuanwu said, "Out of consideration for you as teacher and disciple, I let this pass."

"Thirty blows! When [Zhao]yan returned, the Master went to pay his respects. That night, he raised the case of Fenyang seeing Shoushan, who said: "The moon in the empty expanse of the ten-thousand-year-old green pool—only after repeatedly searching for it will you finally know it.

[Zhao]zhen attained sudden enlightenment. Later, while staying there, a monk asked him: [The Master said: "Thirty blows! When Yan returned, the Master went to pay his respects. That night, he brought up the case of Fenyang seeing Shoushan, who said: "The moon in the empty expanse of the ten-thousand-year-old green pool—only after repeatedly searching for it will you finally know it. Zhaozhen attained sudden enlightenment. After he took up residence, a monk asked:
Leaving behind Mount Wushi, he came to dwell at Stone Creek Mountain (*Shíxī Shān*). He revealed the path for devas and humans; how does one pass through the Patriarch’s barrier? The Master said:
"A dragon gives birth to a golden phoenix chick, which pierces through the azure lapis lazuli. [The student] said: "If it is so, then we do not recognize each other face-to-face;

though a thousand miles apart, we share the same wind. The Master said: "Layer upon layer are the mountains and roads of the barrier. [The student] said: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, he did not establish [anything]."

"Words and letters directly point to the human mind, enabling one to see one's nature and attain Buddhahood. [The student] asked, "Since you do not establish words and letters, how is it that they have been transmitted down to the present day?

The Master said, "In official matters, even a needle cannot pass; in private affairs, carriages and horses may travel through. [The student] asked, "Directly pointing to the human mind—what mind do you point to?
The Master said, "When the mouth opens, it is not on the tongue. [The student] asked, "'Seeing one's nature and attaining Buddhahood'—where does this nature reside?"
[The Master] said, "The Taihu Lake spans thirty-six thousand mu; night after night, the moonlight shines bright upon its waves.

[The student] said, "I recall it being stated in the Lotus Sutra that a great wealthy elder is none other than the Tathāgata. Does this refer to someone who has come through many kalpas, or does it refer to one who attains realization in this very life?
[The Master] immediately said, "The mountain stream is deep and the falling flowers drift far away; the mountain is high and the tree shadows stretch long. [The student] said, "In the past..."
[The student] said: "In the past, Anāthapiṇḍika established a vihāra; today, this layman has donated his wealth to build a site for the Way.
Are these two cases the same or different? The Master said: "When the lion roars, the fragrant grasses turn green; where the elephant king walks, the hundred flowers bloom red.

[The student] said: "Truly, such a meeting occurs but once in a thousand years. The Master said: "It illuminates the past and shines upon the present. [The student] said: "Since it is thus, tell me, what have you attained?"
"What is the karmic fruit? The Master said, "Life after life one returns to the Buddha-ground; birth after birth one enjoys the realms of humans and devas.
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then the fourfold assembly shall receive your grace. The Master said, "Throughout the heavens and across the earth.

[The monk] asked, "On the day the flower blooms at the pestle-head of Huangmei, the robe was transmitted at midnight to Lingnan. Is this matter truly so, or not? The Master said, "Not a single thing exists from the very beginning."
[The Master] said, "Neither the wind moves, nor does the banner move; it is the mind of the worthy one that moves. [The monk] asked, "What about this?
The Master said, "To know that the lamp is originally fire; to believe that water is not separate from the waves. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how does one maintain this?
The Master said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, you must present your sword; if you are not a poet, do not offer your poem. [The monk] said, "Master..."
"How about one phrase for the sake of people? The Master said, "A slap across the cheek and a blow behind the head.

[The monk] said, "To you, this is a motherly heart that is too earnest. The Master said, "If one does not cast fragrant bait into the white waves, how can the golden-scaled fish ascend the fishing boat?
Ascending the hall, he said: "At the summit of a ten-thousand-fathom peak, give them a shove; their bodies will shatter and their heads split, leaving no room for doubt or hesitation. Suddenly—
Yet, having passed away, he revives once more; the myriad phenomena and the vast cosmos open their laughing eyes. But tell me, after all, what is it they laugh at?
"This time, having recognized the path from whence one comes, one shall no longer enter a mother’s womb. (He lets out a shout. He ascends the hall.
The Master spoke through non-speaking; his words filled the world. The World-Honored One taught through non-teaching; his teachings pervaded all humanity.
These two great elders propped their tongues against the Brahma Heaven and emptied the four seas with their eyes, yet they still did not possess the hand that can cast a net.
Under Shixi’s gate, there is a distinct vital energy: speaking through non-speaking, clouds drift in layers atop the peak of Tianbao.

To speak without speaking: the waters of the Tóngchuān ravine flow with a murmuring sound. Although it is thus, this is still a phrase for turning the body; it is not yet the phrase of the total presentation.
But tell me, what is the phrase of the total presentation? He plants his staff and says: "Holding Mòxié crosswise, he issues the full and correct command;
throughout the realm of Great Peace, he slays the dull and stubborn. Ascending the hall, he said: "The cloth bag is long."
The worlds of the ten directions are entirely contained within it; the cloth bag is short. The great earth, mountains, and rivers cannot fill it; the cloth bag is wide.
The bodies of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are seen as one; the cloth bag is narrow. The myriad phenomena are dense and their radiance is magnificent;
yet tell me, when the cloth bag is neither long nor short, neither wide nor narrow, how is it then? North, south, east, and west—there is no facing away or turning toward.

Above, reaching the celestial canopy; below, the wind-circle. Regarding the illness of the eye, I ascend the hall: the illness of the Buddha, the illness of the Patriarchs, and the illness of all sentient beings—I set these aside.
Elixirs, wondrous medicines, and the medicines of the immortals—I cast these to one side.
Apart from this illusory body of the four elements, tell me: what is the illness? What is the medicine? If you can realize it here, I grant you all my approval.
To possess this single eye is rare; yet, if you have not yet attained it, I, this old monk, shall clearly point out the source of the illness for all of you to see:
when the four elements disperse, where will you find a place to settle your body and establish your life? "A phrase with no illness but no medicine":
the radish of Zhèngzhōu, the cypress tree, the dried turd, the three *mǎn* of hemp. "A phrase with medicine but no illness": [the thousand...]
"Where do all dharmas ultimately return? Zhaozhou replied, "I made a cotton shirt in Qingzhou that weighed seven *jin*.
This is a phrase for treating illness with medicine. "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing; the dog has no Buddha-nature.
This is a phrase for the simultaneous forgetting of both medicine and illness, intended to treat the five desires and eight winds within the minds of sentient beings.

The afflictions, the dust of worldly toil, delusive thoughts, attachments, and all manner of illnesses—the entire Great Canon of the Teachings is, in its entirety, a medical prescription for saving the world;
the seventeen hundred public cases of the patriarchs are all efficacious elixirs and wondrous medicines. When one has an illness, one should take the medicine;
when there is no illness, the medicine itself must be expelled. Is there anyone among this assembly who can come forward and say: "The Master himself does not..."
[The Master] said, "It can be treated. Why treat an individual? I simply say to him: 'I have kept a pair of blue and white eyes to laugh at the countless people coming and going.
Generally, when Master An came to visit, the Master asked him, 'What sutra are you lecturing on?'"
[The monk] said, "In the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, I attained a place of realization where there is nowhere from which one comes and nowhere to which one goes.
The Master asked, "Since there is neither coming nor going, for what reason have you arrived here? [The monk] said, "It is precisely because there is neither coming nor going.
The Master asked, "Where are you right now? The host gave a shout. The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment the shouting and the fist-wielding..."
[Zihu] said, "When the four great elements disperse, where do you establish yourself and sustain your life? [The monk] replied, "If one writes 'the great earth,' where is there that is not oneself?
The Master said, "What if you suddenly encounter the kalpa-fire blazing forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed?

How will you be then? [The monk] said, "At this point, I simply do not understand. The Master said, "The Sixth Patriarch did not understand how to split firewood or tread upon the pestle; Bodhidharma did not recognize [his own nature]."
"Facing the wall for nine years—you do not understand. What did you see? He replied, "I simply do not understand. The Master said, "Blind fellow! Please be seated and have some tea.
In the twelfth month of the third year of the Hongwu era, he manifested slight illness. He wrote a verse, saying: "Birth is fundamentally no birth; extinction is fundamentally no extinction.
Casting off my hands, I go forth; the sky is one bright moon. Having cast aside his brush, he passed away.
Chan Master Xuefeng Niche Zhishun of Fuzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tianbao Shu. He was the son of the Chen family of Ruian, Wenzhou.
His mother fashioned an image of the Venerable Zhi (Zhiyi) and served it. One night, she dreamed of a monk who came against the current and beckoned her, saying, "I shall be your son."
She conceived while still dreaming. At the age of seven, she left the household life. Upon reaching maturity, she traveled to Min to visit Tieguan, who transmitted the essentials of the mind to her.
After more than a month, while using the toilet, she saw a bitter gourd in the garden and attained a realization. She presented what she had awakened to in order to seek verification.

Tieguan said, "This is merely an entry point; the supreme One Vehicle is still far off. He then instructed her, saying, "You should completely cast aside your previous understandings and focus exclusively..."
If you exert yourself at the "Gate" (Guān), you will naturally enter its innermost depths.
One day, while attending the evening session (wǎncān), as he was about to leave his mat, he suddenly attained a state of great clarity. He said to Guān, "The failure of Nánquán has now been seen.
Guān asked, "It is not the mind, not the Buddha, and not a thing—what is it? The Master replied, "Bricks on the ground, tiles on the roof."
The roof was covered with tiles. Guankui asked, "Where is Nanquan right now? The Master said, "A hawk flies over Silla.
Guankui said, "Wrong. The Master also said, "Wrong. Guankui said, "Wrong, wrong. The Master performed a prostration with his head touching the ground. Guankui assembled the community to test him.
The Master smiled and said, "Before a word was uttered, we were already beyond each other's reach. Where, then, are you, Master’s eyes? Furthermore, for this reason..."

"It is indeed a drama," Guan said, "but it is necessary that everyone know. When Guan passed away, the Master succeeded him in overseeing the affairs of the monastery and subsequently resided at Baoen Guiyuan.
The imperial court bestowed upon him a Dharma robe and the title "Fóxìng Yuánbiàn" (Perfectly Discerning Buddha-nature).
After some time, he distributed all his robes and alms-bowl accumulations and retired to a single room. There, he dug the earth to serve as a hearth and broke bamboo to fashion chopsticks.
He was as serene and unassuming as a plain surface. When Pingzhang Yanzhihuwa was dispatched to govern the province of Min, he invited the Master to reside at Dongchan Xuefeng.
At the beginning of the Fawu era, an imperial edict summoned ten monks of realized virtue to Mount Zhongshan to establish a religious assembly; the Master ascended the seat to preach the Dharma.
The Emperor’s carriage visited him in person, and his consolations were most thorough. Upon returning south, he resided at Jingci Monastery.

It happened that the central court summoned the virtuous Jingtuzhu to the capital to serve as a counselor; the assembly unanimously recommended the Master. He arrived in the capital and stayed for four months, after which he bathed, wrote a verse, and passed away.
Chan Master Wumen Cong of Xiangshan in Ruzhou was a successor of Chan Master Tie-shan Qiong.
He was a native of Xiangshan. Initially, he studied under Dugu Weng, who instructed him to investigate the koan "The Three Are Not.
For some time, he had not yet attained awakening. One day, the Venerable Jing said to him, "If you wish to know the ultimate meaning, look at the Big Dipper."
Facing south, he gazed. One night, he attained a realization. He then went to seek out [Master] Jing. Jing asked, "Who is it that comes?
The Master replied, "Neither person nor self. Jing said, "If it is neither person nor self, what exactly is it? The Master replied, "When hungry, I eat; when tired, I sleep.
Jing threw down his meditation cushion and told him to compose a verse. The Master said: "A single perfect circle, Everyone desires to see it. Sitting..."
Severing the ten directions, the cold light flashes like lightning. Jing again raised his fan and said, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
The Master said, "Clearly raised up—how wondrous indeed! A pure breeze circulates, penetrating one’s very heart. Within this, there is not much of a message."
Since I have experienced this universal joy throughout my entire being, Tie-shan has recently returned from Goryeo.
While at Shi-shuang, he heard that you had attained a point of enlightenment, so he asked, "Where is your honored residence? I replied, "Ruzhou.

He asked, "In the midst of such worldly bustle, what is the true countenance of the Patriarchs? I replied, "Venerable Sir, please stop for a moment; it would take twenty years of diligent effort to explain it."
[The monk] went all around. Iron Mountain seized him by the throat and asked, "What is the meaning of 'No'? The Master said, "I have recently come from Tanzhou;
I have not received news from Hubei. Iron Mountain said, "That is not it; speak again. The Master said, "When did you leave Goryeo, Preceptor?"
[Shishuang] said, "That is not it; speak further. The Master let out a shout, shook his sleeves, and departed. Shishuang said, "These brothers are all well, yet they have one great illness:
they claim to have attained realization. The Master was deeply moved by Iron Mountain’s instruction on the subtle and vast Dharma-gate.

Later, he resided in Gwangju. He practiced alone in walking and sitting for seventeen years before finally attaining liberation. He gave a general discourse, saying: "Dharmas have no fixed characteristics;
they become the ultimate principle upon meeting conditions. Wielding the Vajra sword, one swallows the thorny *liji* fruit and cuts off the tongues of the monks."
Sitting upon the very crown of Vairocana, one erects a single blade of grass to become a sixteen-foot golden body, and takes that sixteen-foot golden body to become a single blade of grass.
This is neither the drum-beat of Heyshan nor a separate transmission outside the teachings; it is simply to remain utterly naked, with not a thread of silk hanging on.
When the moon is cold in the autumn sky and cold ashes flare into flame—should one reach this point and call it "Buddhadharma," they fall into hell.
It is like being struck by an arrow. To not call this the Buddha-dharma is likewise to fall into hell as if struck by an arrow.
O worthy ones, how ultimately shall you understand it? To open your mouth is to lose your body and forfeit your life;
to keep your mouth shut is to rot your tongue. Have you not seen the Boatman say: "For twenty years at Yaoshan, where I hid my body, there was no trace; where there was no trace..."

Do not hide yourself. Although you have thus proclaimed and chanted—opening up the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, establishing the Great Perfect Mirror, raising the banner of Nirvana, and extolling Prajna;

though you have raised both the "knocking" and the "singing," harmonizing and penetrating them both, with illumination and function occurring simultaneously—when viewed through the True Eye, all of these are merely idle furnishings.
They have no connection whatsoever to the immediate concern of us monks. (He raises his whisk.)
He asked, "Do you understand?
Master Bifeng Baolin of Lingjiu Peak on Mount Wutai in Daizhou was a Dharma heir of Chan Master Jin Yunzhen. He was a native of Yongshou in Qianzhou and his secular surname was Shi.
Both his parents were devoted to the good. At that time, there was a śramaṇa who presented an image of Avalokiteśvara to his mother and instructed her, saying, "Serve this with reverence;
you shall give birth to a son of wisdom. Before long, the Master was indeed born, and a brilliant white light shone radiantly throughout the room.

As a child, he suffered frequently from illness. His parents suspected this and said, "This boy will surely return to the Śākya clan. At the age of six, he consequently left the household to study under Yunji and Wenfa.
As a disciple, he received full ordination upon reaching adulthood and traveled extensively to lecture halls to exhaustively investigate the principles of *Xing* (nature) and *xiang* (phenomena).
After some time, he said, "Can this truly bring an end to birth and death? He then abandoned his studies and departed. At that time, Chan Master Ruhuizhen was expounding the Dharma at Jinyun;
the Master went there and was shown the essentials of the Way. Great doubt arose within him, and he once happened to carry a basket along with Huizhen as they gathered vegetables.
In the garden, he suddenly sat motionless for three watches before finally awakening. Haikong asked, "Are you in samādhi? The Master replied, "Samādhi and movement do not concern me.
Haikong asked, "Who is it that neither concerns himself with samādhi nor movement? The Master lifted his basket. Haikong did not approve.
The Master set the basket on the ground and stood with his hands crossed. Haikong still did not approve. The Master let out a shout, and Haikong lunged forward, thrusting at his chest.
He replied, "The shortcut. Master [Huineng] built up Hai’s chest and threw him down. Hai laughed and said, "Dust and toil have momentarily ceased, yet your power of concentration is not yet deep.
You must cause the path of the mind to be cut off and penetrate the Patriarchal Barrier; only then can the Great Dharma be clarified. Later, he rested his staff at Mount Emei.
For three years, he ate pine and cedar daily and did not let his side touch the mat. One day, he heard the sound of wood being felled. Suddenly—

He attained enlightenment. Previously, while in meditative absorption, the Master had seen a mountain of exquisite beauty, with multi-storied pavilions and magnificent towers shimmering in gold and azure.
Within it, various Buddhas and fifty-two Bodhisattvas were practicing the Way. One of them beckoned to the Master, saying: "This is the Secret Demon Rock of Wutai.
You practiced the Way here in a previous life; your sacred remains are still there. Why have you forgotten this? Once [he emerged from meditation]...
Xuanwu then set out for Mount Wutai. On the road, he encountered a woman with disheveled hair wearing tattered garments of five colors and walking slowly barefoot, followed by a black mastiff.
The Master asked her, "Where are you going? She replied, "I am entering the mountains. The Master asked, "What will you do there?
She said, "I shall do nothing at all. After a long while, she vanished. When the Master questioned his companions about this, none of them knew anything of it.
Some claimed he was an emanation of Mañjuśrī. The Master then established the Lingju Hermitage on the mountain; his reputation and brilliance became manifest day by day.
Hearing of him from all quarters, people came from as far as a thousand *li*, carrying provisions and grain to offer him, arriving in daily throngs.

In the *wuzi* year of the *zhizheng* era, the Emperor dispatched an envoy with an imperial decree summoning him to the capital, where he was treated with great reverence. He was ordered to reside at Haiyin Temple, where he diligently...

He declined the offer with haste. The Emperor bestowed upon him the title "Jizhao Yuanming" (Silent Illumination Perfect Clarity). When Emperor Taizu, the August Emperor, ascended the throne, he issued an edict summoning the Master to Nanjing.
There, the Emperor met him in the inner palace and inquired about the essential meaning of the Buddha-dharma.

The Emperor established the Pujihui (Universal Salvation Assembly) at Mount Zhong and selected ten monks of eminent conduct to preside over its affairs; the Master was among them. He received exceedingly generous imperial favors and gifts.
The Master himself took up the brush and bestowed upon him a poem of twelve verses. Not long after, he manifested a slight illness.

His disciples requested that he leave behind his final words, to which the Master replied, "If even the Dharma-treasure of the Tripitaka is but old paper, what purpose would my words serve? He then passed away with serene composure.
His secular age was sixty-five; his monastic seniority was fifty-nine. Upon cremation, he obtained śarīra relics of five colors. His teeth, tongue, and prayer beads remained entirely unharmed.
He was the twenty-third generation descendant of Nanyue.

Chan Master Lizhong Cheng of Ciguang Temple in Hangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Liaozhen of Jingci Temple. He was the son of the Sun family of Qiantang. Having first visited Master Liaozhen, he requested instruction.
Liaozhen then presented him with the koan regarding the "mountain burning in the twelfth month. The Master offered this verse: "The white clouds obscure the old [path],"

Traces of his movement: In the twelfth month, the fire burning the mountains is still glowing red. When the breeze of compassion blows upon it once more, the freezing cold is transformed into a warm glow.
Yan Sheng praised this as a vessel of profound depth.
Chan Master Wuya Feihuan of Linggu Monastery in Nanjing was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wushi Yuchan. He was a native of Xian County in Quzhou and became a monk under Master Jiefeng.
When Jiefeng asked him where he had come from, the Master replied, "Empty space has no front or back. Jiefeng then pointed to the monastery bell and instructed him to compose a verse about it.
The Master said: "Rolled forth from the furnace of a hundred refinements, empty space has never been defiled by dust.

Now it hangs upon the heads of men; when struck, its great resonance pervades the nine realms. At that time, [Feng] was twelve years old. Xingfeng took him under his care and immediately had him tonsured.
In the Dinghai year of the Yongle era, when the Emperor Wenhuang of the Taizong reign performed sacrifices at Changling, he summoned the Master to enter the capital.

His words accorded with the Imperial intent, for which he was greatly honored with rewards and gifts. He was commanded to reside at Linggu Monastery. In the spring of the Gengzi year, the Emperor established a religious assembly.
When the Master appeared indifferent to it, his disciples questioned him. The Master smiled and said, "I have a matter of great importance of my own that is extremely urgent;
how could I have leisure for anything else? He then wrote this verse: "Birth and death drift on, severed from worldly ties; Having received the Imperial grace, I shall enjoy eternal bliss."
An ordinary year. This time, he cast off his hands and returned empty-handed; the snow has cleared, the clouds have vanished, and the moon is perfectly full.
He then passed away. Chan Master Taechu (Gigen), of Japan, resided at Samgungsa Temple in Nangyang.
At the age of nineteen, he visited forty-five masters in the Land of the High Sovereign; finally, he received the Dharma from Jeokpung. Later, he dwelt at Samgungsa. One day, he wrote:
The verse says: "In life there is an iron face; in death there is an iron face. With a single blow, he was shattered into a hundred pieces, wandering by day around the Iron Ring Mountains.
He then cast aside his brush and passed away. His stupa was erected to the south of the monastery.
Among those who have attained realization in the Chan gate, there are some who did not emerge from the world, while others emerged into the world whose dharma heirs remain undetermined;

these are appended here. Chan Master Fo Jue of Qingzhou (belonging to the Yunmen lineage; his dharma succession remains undetermined) offered this verse on Master Shizi of Yangshan: "A single color does not exceed [it]."
Pointing the Way: Within the world of white silver, he yawns with transcendence; he knocks one down and then raises one up.
How can this compare to the fresh warmth of the eastern wind and the rising sun? At that time, Chan Master Furi Yao held up the Linji Chan lineage and took up residence at Sheng’an.

He divided the monastic quarters and entered the hall. One day, he personally beat the drum and ascended the dais to preach, elevating the spiritual winds of the Yunmen and Linji schools and sharing the assembly in equal halves.
He then took his leave without a word of farewell; the Master remained unperturbed and paid him no further mind.
Yuantong Shanguo (who belonged to the Yunmen school and was a successor of Fojue) was traveling from Jiangyou to Yanjing when he stayed at Dasheng'an Temple.
One night, while he was engaged in a nocturnal conversation with Fojue Huidang, the Master [Yuantong] was twelve years old and stood in attendance by his seat.
Yunju said, "I have come from the South, and not a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma has been struck by my staff.
The Master joined his palms and stepped forward, saying, "This is simply because your staff, Reverend, is too short.
Yunju was greatly startled and said, "I pray you, take this man to continue our Linji lineage. The Master replied, "How could there be two [lineages]—Yunmen and Linji? Yunju praised him highly.
When Emperor Gongsun Ye (Emperor Jin Shizong) visited the Shrine of the Auspicious Image at Sheng’an Temple, he asked the Master, “Is it proper to pay homage?
Or is it not proper to pay homage? The Master replied, “To pay homage is to show mutual respect and honor; not to pay homage is for each to claim their own supremacy. The Emperor was greatly pleased.
Later, while residing at Yansheng Temple, he addressed the assembly, citing Dongshan: “In the early autumn and late summer, brothers may go east or west; go directly...”

"One must go to a place ten thousand *li* wide where there is not a single blade of grass. He asked again, "But how does one go to such a place where there is not a single blade of grass ten thousand *li* wide?
Shishuang said, "As soon as you step out the door, it is already grass. Dayang said, "Even to say 'I do not step out the door' is already a vast expanse of grass.
The Master said, "Now tell me, what is the phrase at the very bottom of your feet right this moment?"
"If you say, 'The Way has not even a blade of grass,' I allow that you have seen Dongshan. If you say, 'As soon as one goes out the door it is grass,' I allow that you have seen Shishuang.
If you say, 'Even when one does not go out the door, it is a vast expanse of grass,' I allow that you have seen Taiyang.
If you cannot say anything at all, I allow that you have seen Yansheng. Why? Because there is only a fine breeze."
Coming to the assembly, he spoke no idle words regarding the human realm. Addressing the congregation, he raised the story of Guanyin’s sesame cake.
The Master said, "The Elder of Shaoyang may indeed be said to have sung ever more loftily while those who join in the chorus have become ever fewer.
Now, however, he enters the Samādhi of the Square Net upon the whisk of Yansheng. He enters meditative concentration in the East and arises in the West; even entering with a male body..."
The female body arises from meditative concentration. Do you understand? The wild landscape is no longer cut off by mountains;
the moonlight flows directly into the water. Long ago, two monks were traveling together. The one who was impatient called out to the one behind him, saying, "Time passes swiftly!
Hurry up and come here! The monk behind replied, "The Great Way is vast and wide; why such haste? The Master composed a verse on this: Light...
Yin quickly ran up the path; at the head of the road, he stepped upon a blooming *utpala* flower. "The Great Way is vast and wide—what is the hurry?
He opened his belly and wrapped everything within it at once. When the Master saw that Xuanwu’s words were frivolous and mocking, he rebuked him, saying:
"If everyone were like you, how could the Buddha-Dharma have reached its present state?"

Chan Master Xuanwu Yu of Qingshou Monastery in Yanjing (belonging to the Yunmen lineage and succeeding Yuantong) was summoned by Emperor Xianzong of Jin, who commanded an imperial messenger to bring a sheet of paper upon which the two characters "Mind-Buddha" (心佛) were written.
The Emperor asked the Master, "What characters are these? At that moment, Yuantong was seated in the assembly and replied immediately:
"Neither mind, nor Buddha. This response pleased the Emperor. The following day, an imperial decree was issued granting him various lengths of silk.
The verse says: "If one can simply realize purity, what need is there to ask about the causes and conditions of the myriad dharmas?

In daily life, remain in non-action; do not harbor further doubt throughout the twelve hours of the day. One must always freely recognize this: from the beginning, there has been no attachment or obstruction.

Buddha after Buddha, mind after mind—if the mind relies upon the Buddha, it is still a defilement. The Master replied in thanks: "Non-action and non-creation—yet even to cling to non-action is still [a delusion]."

Bondage and illumination function simultaneously; even "lightning rolling and stars streaming" is already too slow. It is neither mind nor Buddha; yet to call it "not mind" is still to treat it as a thing.
When both person and environment are empty, the myriad phenomena are arrayed within a single realm.
The lay practitioner Zhao Wenyu of Huangshan (of the Yunmen lineage; successor of Yuantong) once composed this verse: "Deluded thoughts are originally and fundamentally true;
To try to eliminate them is to raise another layer of dust. Who provides the power for speech, thought, movement, and stillness? If you examine closely, there is no one other than yourself."
When Master Ding of Gaoyou (of the Yunmen lineage; successor of Xuanwu) first visited Xuanwu, the master raised the following case in his room:
A monk asked Xuansha, "What is the pure Dharma-body? Xuansha replied, "It is dripping with pus. At this, the Master attained realization.
Later, when a monk asked, "What does the golden fish that has passed through the net eat? the Master replied, "Dry dung."
Chan Master Bao of Puzhao in Zhengzhou was the son of the Wu family of Cizhou. While he was constructing Yangshan Temple in Fuyang, someone suddenly inscribed a poem upon a pillar that read:
"People say the turtledove is clumsy; I say the turtledove is clever. With one piece of wood and two pieces of wood, One’s household needs are fully provided.
The Master attained great enlightenment and immediately retired to the Western Mountains to dwell in a thatched hut. He then traveled extensively throughout the region.
The various mountains [were shaken]. He went to Baoyan Temple in Hongyu, where one night a great wind shook the earth;
he sat in meditation and passed away. Chan Master Yun’an Qing of Jingshan in Hangzhou was a native of Jianyang.
When a monk asked Yangqi, "What is the Buddha? Yangqi said, "A three-legged donkey prancing with its hooves. The monk said, "Is it not just this? Yangqi said, "The lake..."
To Elder Nán, the Master then uttered this verse: A donkey of Yangqi, its eye-light flashing like lightning;
It tramples all people underfoot—what need is there to speak of three legs?
Chan Master Zhulin Juchuanhai’s verse on the wind chimes says: Copper lips and iron tongues, so sharp and new;
Hung from the corner of the tower, they have forgotten spring. A hundred thousand samādhis beyond words— Through the wind, they speak to those who truly understand.
Chan Master Xuming Jiaoheng of Qingshou Temple in Yanjing was the son of the Wang family of Rencheng in Jizhou.
Previously, there was a monk named Fuan of Ciji Temple in Bianjing who had lived in mountain retreats for many years; he passed away leaning against a tree in Mangshan Village.
