Seeking lodging in a dream, he eventually became his teacher. At the age of seven, he left the household life; at fifteen, he traveled abroad.

Hearing of the excellence of Master Bao’s Dharma assembly at Puzhao Monastery in Zhengzhou, he went there to pay his respects. Although he visited and inquired every morning and evening, he had not yet attained realization.

On another occasion, while traveling to Suixiang for business, he stayed overnight at Zhaodu. Suddenly, while on horseback, he recalled the circumstances of striking the wooden board and attained awakening.

His state of doubt remained undispersed. As they neared the river crossing, his companion was startled and said, "Brother, this is the river crossing. The Master dismounted; grief and joy welled up within him until he wept. Upon returning, he told Bao about it. Bao said, "This man who has been lying stiff as a corpse seems ready to move. He then showed him the *Gong'an* of Nittō Kokushi (Nichi-men Butsu). Later, hearing the sound of the wooden board, he attained a sudden and direct realization. He presented a verse: The sun’s face shines everywhere, The moon’s face is always bright. When the sound of the board falls, The whole body is revealed. He said: "The sun’s face and the moon’s face; stars streaming and lightning spinning. If you hesitate any further, an arrow will strike your very face!

Alas! Bao, I cannot deceive you. Later, he sat upon the seat of enlightenment five times. He again stayed his staff at Puzhao Monastery in Jizhou, where he presided over the Qingshou and Xingding temples by imperial decree of Emperor Zhang.
On the tenth day of the seventh month in the autumn of the Jimao year, he took up his brush and wrote this verse: [Verse follows]
The final phrase says: "Eh! One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. He sat firmly without moving and passed away.
Zen Master La of Jianshan in Zhenfu was asked by a monk, "Where is the stupa of Iron Ox Worthy? The Master pointed his finger toward it;
the monk suddenly attained awakening and then presented this verse: "Iron Ox, Iron Ox! Seek nothing else further. If someone asks..."
I raised my finger. Chan Master Yuantong of Tōgyoku Tsūgen-an once composed the "Hundred Questions" to exhort his disciples. The first question was:
"Why is the bottomless boatman's vessel without leakage and solidly firm? He then raised his whisk and said, "I have finished preaching Zen for you."
"How do you understand this? He then picked up his staff and said, "Is there anyone who can produce a turning phrase regarding the tip of this staff?
He then drew a circle and said, "The Buddhas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs are all contained within this.
How do you understand this? He then made a dot in the air with his hand and said, "Tell me, what about this one dot?"
Pointing out what matters at the boundary, he held up one finger and said:
"The Venerable Guizong is here, emitting great radiance and turning the Great Dharma Wheel. Do you all see him? He also said: 'A broken-legged cauldron is sufficient for livelihood.'"
Making a life of the "pierced-heart bowl," sitting at ease within the Tongxuan Hermitage, he pays no mind to the affairs before the mountain that are as numerous as hemp seeds.
But tell me, who is this person who sits so at ease?
The Great Master Yuanfan Huihong of Wutai Tieqin Monastery, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, reached the passage: "When one person gives rise to the truth, those in the ten directions perish.
He suddenly attained awakening. He then went to see Chan Master Wen of Heshuo and presented his realization.
Wen approved it. His verse at the time of death said: "Sixty years of springtime, plus eight more; the floating clouds have cleared away, revealing the blue sky. As he was departing, he gave a kick.
He turned Mount Sumeru upside down. Later, during the final watch of the night, when the moon was perfectly full at the mountain peak, he changed his robes and passed away while seated.
Chan Master Hui-kong Yuan-mo of Jiangshan in Jianning Prefecture was the son of the Su family of Gutian.

In the year of Great Virtue (1060), on a day in the Zhenghe era, he entered meditative absorption and traveled to Jiangshan. Upon reaching the site of the former Chan Master Xuan-jang’s monastery, there was an old man.
He came forward to greet him and said, "I have guarded this mountain for five hundred years as your servant. Having finished speaking, he transformed into a black dragon and departed.
Upon waking, [Fayan] said, "I shall return to my origin and restore my source upon this mountain. He then established a hermitage there.

One day, he said to the assembly, "In the presence of the Buddha, I was known as the Bodhisattva Huikong. Now that my karmic conditions for transformation are exhausted, I shall immediately enter nirvana."
Because he has expounded the Dharma of the Four Noble Truths, he further speaks in verse: "For over forty years I dwelt amidst the dust of the mundane world;
Now, at last, I reveal the Honored One within this very midst. A night wind arose from the east upon the crag; It blew the flowers open, bringing spring to every tree.
An iron ship, without rudder nor sail, Is steered into the ocean of the nature of the golden lotus. The final pivot of the mechanism is now revealed."

White clouds have never been separate from the vast sky; throughout the great earth, mountains, and rivers, no trace can be found. When empty space is struck through, the ultimate reality is revealed.
Even if an iron wheel were to spin upon the crown of one’s head, the original nature—perfectly luminous—is never lost. He spoke again:
"The third patriarch of the Western Heaven, the Venerable Śāṇakavāsa, while dwelling on Mount Gajaśaila, manifested the Dragon-Fury Samādhi and preached the Dharma."
Having subdued the various non-Buddhists, he then transformed himself into fire and incinerated his own body. "I shall now go before the Elephant Trunk Rock and act in the same manner," he said.
Thereupon, he entered the Dragon’s Vigorous Display Samādhi (*nāgavikrīḍita-samādhi*). At that time, clouds and mist rose from all sides and thunder and rain broke forth violently;
subsequently, he transformed himself into fire and consumed himself. The assembly collected his sacred relics and enshrined them in a stupa to the west of the hermitage.
Chan Master Foguang Daowu of Puzhao Monastery in Zhengzhou was a native of Guanzhi in Lanzhou, Lintao Prefecture.
While staying overnight at Wanzi Inn, he heard the neighing of a horse and attained sudden, great enlightenment. He spoke this verse: "Seeing! Seeing! Seeing! (Jian ye la, jian ye la.)
"Pervading all of space is just this. He returned and told his mother, "I picked up something on the road. His mother asked, "What thing?

The Master replied, "Something that has not been seen since beginningless time. His mother struck him with her palm and said, "Why are you so joyful? Thereupon, he took his leave to travel and seek instruction elsewhere.
His mother asked, "Where will you go? The Master replied, "Water flowing must reach the sea; a crane emerges from atop the white clouds. Thus he departed to seek a teacher.
Chan Master Baibun Hai subsequently received the seal of transmission. In the twenty-fourth year of the Taiding era, he went forth to preside over Puzhao Monastery.
Clad in white robes, riding a yellow calf, and blowing a short flute, he wandered through Luoyang. He once said: "If you say I am an ordinary person, I have come from the rank of the sages.
If you say I am a sage, I have gone to the rank of the ordinary. If you say I am neither ordinary nor..."
"Holy one," [he replied]. "Yet, atop the crown of Vairocana, there is yet another place of practice. In the fifth year of the Taihe era, he entered nirvana.

Zen Master Chupeng of Pujue at Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou, during the fifth year of the Jiayou era, was granted imperial authorization to restore the ancient road of Jiusong for the Jiqing Monastery.
He ascended the hall and said: "A single plot of idle land before the mountain; vast and great kalpas have passed, yet it remains without boundaries."
Having been restored to the present day, it has returned once more. It cuts off both the head and the tail;
east is so, west is so—north, south, east, and west are not otherwise. Ultimately, how does one repay this grace?
Ten li of lotus flowers, nine li of pines—a single incense offering before the Hall of Direct Pointing.
The verse of the late Head Seat Shou of Jiufeng at the time of his death says:

"Seventy-two years spent here and there, Eating the food of the ten directions, Studying the Chan of Bodhidharma— This morning, with one cast, I turn over and depart; I laugh until the bystanders' eyes are split wide open."
Chan Master Wujin Zudeng of Yunfeng on Mount Tiantai was a native of the Wang family of Siming.
He visited Master Rixi Yong at Tianning Temple and asked, "The matter of birth and death is great, and impermanence is swift; I beg you to grant me some instruction. Rixi said:

"Throughout the twelve periods of the day, investigate this closely and secretly. When you suddenly strike upon it, come back and ask me again. The Master raised his voice and said, "Impermanence is swift;

the matter of birth and death is great. Before he had finished speaking, Xī gave a shout. The Master immediately prostrated himself. Xī asked, "What principle have you seen that you prostrate yourself thus?
The Master replied, "To open one's mouth is already an error. Xī nodded in approval. The Master then departed to travel and study under other teachers.
The various elders of the mountain followed him as he planted his staff atop Yunfeng Peak; for fifty springs and autumns, his shadow never left the mountain.

On the eighth day of the second month in the second year of the Hongwu era, he manifested a slight illness. When the night was nearly half over, he looked to those around him and asked, "Is the sky beginning to brighten?
They replied, "Not yet. Someone asked, "At this very moment, what do you intend to do, Master? The Master broke into a smile and said, "In the past..."
Deshan was sitting in illness when a monk asked, "Is there anyone who is not ill? Deshan said, "There is.
The monk asked, "What is this one who is not ill? Deshan said, "A-ye, A-ye. After a long silence, the Master said, "Can such a thing as this be called being ill?"
The assembly remained silent. The Master said, "The physical body is impermanent; seek realization early. The time has come; I am about to depart. The attendant held up paper and requested a verse.
The Master said, "It shall not be that there is no verse. Would you rather I not die? As the attendant’s request grew more insistent, the Master then wrote:
"Arising and ceasing, coming and going, Are fundamentally the Tathāgatagarbha. Crushing down the five Sumerus, Vast and open..."
Yet he showed no sign of turning away; he set down his brush, sat upright, and passed away.
Chan Master Xueting of Xianlin Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Gui family of Rende in Hangzhou. He lost his father when he reached the age of losing his baby teeth.

Suffering from carbuncles and wind-disorders, his two eyes became short-sighted; though he harbored these ailments without recovery, he repeatedly sought to leave the household life and visit Master Xiu.

Upon meeting him at Xianlin, they were immediately in accord. While reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he encountered a point of doubt regarding the passage: "Upon the tip of a single hair, there appears a jeweled royal land."
Later, while at Qianming Temple in Jiangyin, he suddenly beheld the golden and azure majesty of the Ten Thousand Buddhas Pavilion towering before his eyes, and attained a realization.
On New Year’s Eve of the first year of the Hongzhi era, upon hearing the sound of the temple bell, his years of spiritual practice were suddenly and completely liberated. He composed this verse:
"The perfect resonance is not heard by the mind; the great thousand-fold world is illuminated as one. Having crossed over the highest peak, there remains no further mystery."

Excellent. In the year Yimao (1675), he accepted an invitation from Jing Temple in Hunan. The Master again attended upon him to inquire and investigate the Dharma, whereupon he received his seal of approval.

The Master’s style was Mei Xue Yinren (Hidden Man of Plum and Snow), and he was also called Huan Ji (Illusory Dweller). He once said: "Illusion is the trace of dwelling; dwelling is the mark of illusion. When illusion arises, dwelling perishes;
when dwelling is fully realized, it is entirely illusion. When illusion pursues dwelling, it gives rise to life; when illusion is fully realized, it is entirely dwelling."
When the eyes are obscured, flowers appear; yet when the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are seen as such flowers of obscuration, they do not arise.

Within the true reality of emptiness, illusions are merely entrusted thereon—truly a child’s play! The Master cited a monk who asked Yunmen, “If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still fault?
Yunmen replied, “Mount Sumeru. Fortunately, this monk failed to realize the point at the moment it was presented and thus missed Yunmen; this remains truly so to this day.
The streets were barricaded and the alleys blocked, leaving no place to store it. If this monk had been able to utter a single phrase, saying, "I cannot place it here;

please, Master, move it aside," not only would he have become a free and joyful recluse for all eternity, but he would also have pressed Yunmen so hard that the latter would have been left flustered and at a loss for what to do. Let him loose!
Once gathered up, it cannot be held; once held, it cannot be scattered. Is this not the mark of a true man?

Nevertheless, to dwell thus in illusion is no small exertion of the spirit. Tell me, is there still a place where one may find rest? [The Master] spoke on his behalf, saying: "Look at what Yunmen said.
The Master then cited the anecdote of Baizhang’s realization through fanning the fire for Huaiyang and pointed, saying: "When the house is poor..."

Wealth is known only by father and son; flowers fall and bloom, while the spring breeze pays them no heed. To merely act in accordance with the times and seasons is inevitably to incur the laughter of bystanders—ha ha!
The old do not cease their restless minds, and the young do not exert themselves.
Bian Tun Wukong Wudun Chan Master was of the prominent Chen clan of Xizhou in Kaifeng. He suddenly took leave of his parents to seek ordination.
His father said, "This child habitually extends his tongue past his nose; he possesses the marks of one who is no ordinary man. He was thus sent to Shaolin.
One day, kneeling before the master, he requested a dharma name. The master said, "The Way is fundamentally formless."
"What is there to have a name for? The Master replied, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time all have names. He then bestowed the Heart Sūtra upon him.
Upon reciting it until he realized that the five aggregates are all empty, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment. He then said, "If even the body is an illusion, where can one seek a name?"
One day, his teacher wove a large flat basket with his own hands before him and said, "Flat Basket is your name.

The Master replied, "Since it is named 'Flat Basket,' there is no emptiness within it. The teacher said, "Only when you realize the separate transmission outside the teachings will you accord with these words."
Later, he went to the place where the Great River flows beside the Immortal’s Mountain (Xianren Shan). For three days, his responses were as fluent as a cascading torrent.
The River Spirit said, "Truly a lion of Shaolin; in the future, you shall cut off the flow of all streams. Later, he reached Mount Emei and dwelt there in a thatched hut.

One day, arriving at the middle of the Yangtze River at Kuizhou, he said, "The Way is vast and boundless; it cannot be exhausted even when encountered by every person. Having said this, he stepped ashore and sat upright.
Shi. When Chan Master Yongning Guyuanqing of Jinling heard the crowing of a cock, he attained realization. His verse says: "The golden cock crows loudly as dawn breaks;
Were it not for its sound, how could one know? The three thousand worlds are entirely like snow; Mud at the bottom of the well."
Shewu Zhiyi performed the *zhazhi* dance for Chan Master Gulinxiang. Gulin shouted, "Talkative fellow!
Wu'ai Mingli of Funiu was the disciple of He Shi of Fenzhou. He went to attend upon Master Dafang of Songzhu Man.
While participating in the seven-day intensive retreat (*qijiu*) with the assembly, he uttered the phrase: "One sound shatters the void; the King of Dharma alone is revealed. Later, together with...
Dayuan Yue’an entered Zhongnan Mountain. One day, while at the hermitage, he brought up the saying of Gao Feng: “A silver mountain, an iron wall.

The Master attained sudden enlightenment and composed a verse, saying: “A single awakening and the mind is empty; doubt is instantly dispelled. Picking it up and letting it go, one is naturally carefree. Carrying water and hauling wood—the whole body is fully manifested;
The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms are all encompassed within the single nature. He further said: “The wondrous essence is suchness, fundamentally self-...”
Empty. There is not a single thing to be sought after. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, waves surge; the sun never departs from heaven and earth.
After this great seal was verified, Fang said, "I do not ask about the seven-day retreat at Funiu, but what is the meaning of the quiet chamber at Zhongnan?
The Master said, "The seven-day retreat at Funiu is but a lump of mud and a clod of earth; the quiet chamber at Zhongnan radiates a great light."
Mingfang Zhenwei gave a shout and asked, "Where is the radiance right now? The Master stepped forward and struck him with his palm.

Mingfang laughed heartily and said, "So it is, so it is. He then bestowed upon him a verse, saying: "I entrust you with the golden brocade to benefit all beings; A single shake of the Empty School clears the seas and rivers.
The Nature encompasses the myriad phenomena, revered by humans and devas; Within the gate of Buddhas and Patriarchs, you shall unfold the transformative mechanism. (Dafang)
He was the twenty-sixth-generation descendant of Linji (the lineage of his dharma succession remains unspecified).
The Great Master Yunlou Lianchi Zuhong of Hangzhou Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of Renhe County. At the age of seventeen, he entered the local school (*xiang*).
He would always write the four characters "The Matter of Birth and Death" upon his desk. One day, he accidentally dropped and shattered a tea bowl.
He had a realization while in Ou and made seven strokes with his brush to record his resolve. He went to Mount Xishan to have his hair shorn under the Venerable Xingtian.
Traveling north, he visited Bianrong; later, he called upon Xiaoyan at Liu’an to seek instruction. Xiaoyan said, "You have come three thousand li away seeking my instruction;
what instruction do I have to give? The Master was suddenly enlightened. Taking his leave, he passed through Dongchang on the way. On the road...

Upon hearing the sound of the drum from the watchtower, he suddenly attained enlightenment. He spoke a verse: "The events of thirty years ago are suspicious; what marvel is this meeting three thousand *li* away?
To burn incense and cast down my halberd is but a trivial matter; demons and Buddhas vainly contend over right and wrong.
Later, while residing at Yunlou, the Minister Wang Zongmu asked him, "Last night the mice were chirping; they recited the entire Avataṃsaka Sūtra."
The Master asked, "What is it like when the cat suddenly bolts out? Wang was speechless. The Master provided an answer on his behalf:
"The Dharma Master has run off, leaving behind only the lecture desk. He then offered this verse: "The mouse squeaks; the *Avataṃsaka* is clearly manifest.
How strange, Minister Wang! You have been deluded by a beast. The cat suddenly bolts out before the painted hall; At the head of the bed, the preaching of the Dharma leaves no trace."
No further news. *The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya*, Chapter One: "The World-Ruling Sovereign’s Sublime Adornment.

Regarding the circumstances of the Minister of Selection, Lord Yu, during the Chunxi era, who had the Master Huiri (Hui-ri) examine five hundred sick monks: the Master said, "Huiri has willingly accepted the status of a pauper;
he has abandoned himself to follow others. Xi-yuan has humiliated an ordinary citizen, leading one from life toward death—what a pity for these five hundred monks!"

They merely understand how to point and then act; never once have they remained in high repose, refusing to rise. This causes the sun of wisdom to appear strange and deludes the masses, bringing calamity upon their descendants.
Your Excellency, Lord of the Prefecture, has deeply felt the sores of the people; I, a mountain monk, am in haste as the times are difficult.
In my sudden rush, I lost my bamboo staff, so I cannot help but strike the ground with my empty fist upon the abscess of this layman.
Strike once! I guarantee that the chronic ailment will disperse, the toxic blood will flow out, the ten thousand vessels will circulate, and the hundred limbs will be relaxed and at ease.
Even so, how can one person cause the multitude to arise? Have you not heard it said: "When a single leaf turns back toward the sun, spring fills the thousand forests"?
Let this matter rest for a moment; what about when, all day long, one holds the bamboo staff and points east and waves it west? No...

It is like being constantly with a piece of wood, guarding it morning and evening. Through this constant guarding, suddenly the withered wood blossoms again—this is the dead person coming back to life.
If one speaks of it in this way, then bamboo, wood, and all things throughout the great earth—the grasses, trees, and forests—all shall attain Buddhahood.
Why is this? For the essence of emptiness beyond the green objects is itself the Tathāgata.

Now, with a firm and sincere heart (he once praised himself, saying: "A painting that does not resemble [the original] at all vexes the painter to death; perhaps this one comes close enough to leave it here as an offering.

If you say this is it, it remains two different things. If it is not two different things—thirty blows!"). He asked: "Can Chan meditation and the recitation of the Buddha's name be used in a mutually integrated way? The Master said: "If they were two separate things, one could use them in an integrated manner. He asked:
"When the World-Honored One remained silent for a long time, the non-Buddhist said, 'You have cleared away the clouds of my delusion.'"
Śūnyatā-janman sat in meditation without speaking. Śakra said, "Excellent is your exposition of Prajñāpāramitā.

The Master said, "For a long time you have sought to dispel my delusion, yet the gloom has spread for ten thousand miles. While at the side of one in meditative seclusion you intended to hear Prajñā, much time has passed since the teaching was finished.
Even so, though you may grasp the essential meaning by striking the horse's head, as for those who see flowers flying in the void—what exactly do they see? This was shown on a spring day.
"Assembly, today we celebrate the New Year; the seasons have changed once again. But what will it be like tomorrow?

On the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month, at the time of his passing, he addressed the assembly half a month in advance, saying, "I am about to depart for another place. No one could fathom this.
When the appointed time arrived, he manifested a slight illness and passed away while facing west.
Daguan Zhenke was the disciple of the Great Master Zibai (Liu Hongzhi) of Juqu. By nature he was fierce and bold;

he was generous and ardent, and in his youth he did not enjoy playing with toys nor did he like seeing women. At the age of seventeen, he shaved his head and began his travels. There, he heard the recitation of the verse by Zhang Zhuo.
"To eliminate deluded thoughts is to increase one's illness; to strive toward True Suchness (Tathatā) is likewise an error"—this was his great doubt.
One day, during a midday meal, he suddenly attained awakening and said: "If I had been under the seat of Linji or Deshan, a single slap would have awakened me;

what need was there for 'how' and 'what'? He traveled to the capital to study under Bianrong. In the autumn of the Wuli *Gui Mao* year, a seditious book (*yaoshu*) was suddenly circulated; at that time, the Master...
He met with disaster. Previously, when Emperor Shenzong had personally transcribed the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, his sweat happened to soak through the paper.
Suspecting that it should be replaced, he urgently sent an attendant to consult the Master. The Master presented this verse: "A single drop of Imperial sweat is a bridge for ten thousand generations;
The inexhaustible treasury of Dharma shines forth from this. The Emperor was greatly pleased and thereafter paid close attention to him.

Upon seeing the memorial submitted on his behalf, [the Emperor] felt great compassion for him. However, according to the law, he could not be spared. Consequently, he was arrested. When the imperial decree was issued, it stated only: "Let him be interrogated thoroughly.
During the interrogation, his countenance remained composed and his arguments were most upright. With this decrepit and exhausted body, he endured every form of flogging and torture;
yet until the end, he did not yield. He entered prison on the fifth day of the twelfth month. The Ministry of Justice then determined his sentence.
He wished to pass away. His teacher spoke a verse, saying: "A single smile has its own cause from the beginning; Who would have known that the Great Mass does not admit even a speck of dust?
From now on, I shall gather up my natural feet; The iron stake will blossom without waiting for spring. He spoke again, saying: "Such is the nature of worldly phenomena (*saṃsāra*).
What is the use of staying long? Then, having requested a bath, he instructed his attendant, saying: "I am going. Please convey my thanks to Jiangnan."
The various Dharma-protectors spoke in verse, saying: "Only when affairs arise does one see the heroic bones; did Master Da and Mr. Wu share a karmic affinity from past lives?
I shall return to the West while you go to the North; our conversations over many lifetimes will become even more distant. He then sat upright and passed away.
Chan Master Wunian Shendao of Huangbo in Gwangju was the son of the Xiong family of Macheng in Huangzhou. Having shaved his head, he wandered through the mountains.
A renowned elder said to him, "A single grain of light from the ten directions is as heavy as Mount Sumeru;

if you do not realize the Way, you shall return with fur and horns. Upon hearing these words, the Master secretly departed to visit various teachers. He heard a monk cite a question asked of [Master] Da...
Hui asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? Hui replied, "Cucumbers and eggplants. The Master was greatly perplexed.

He subsequently traveled to Mount Wutai and Mount Funiu, visiting renowned masters everywhere. Upon reaching Mount Lu, he went to consult Da’an. An asked, "What is your dharma name? The Master replied, "Wunian (No-Thought).
An asked, "Which one is No-Thought? The Master was at a loss for an answer. He returned once more to his home mountain to consult with his friends.
He recounted his travels over several years. His companion asked, "Why do you not ask about your own self? The Master asked, "What is this 'own self'?

The companion replied, "That which grasps objects is not the hand; that which eats food is not the mouth. One night, hearing the sounds of laughter and weeping occurring together, he attained realization.
On another day, while sitting in the assembly hall, he happened to see a basin of noodles. He picked it up and carried it toward the storage cabinet, but without realizing it, he lost his balance.
The lid of the cabinet struck him on the head, causing sweat to pour down his entire body. Clapping his hands, he laughed and said, "The entire great earth is this very state of non-thought;
what cause for doubt could there be? Later, when they entered Longhu, one day he and the layman Zhuo’wu went to Sima Mountain. There, they encountered a Dharma master who was giving a lecture.
When he arrived, a layman asked, "If it is fundamentally pure and still, how did the mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?

After the Dharma Master finished his lecture, the layman said, "Preach this to me from the state of no-thought. As the Master was about to open his mouth, the layman pushed him on the knee and said, "What about this?
The Master was suddenly and completely enlightened, and spoke a verse: "For over forty years I did not rest my effort; I investigated and investigated until I turned back."
"Without trace. Now, having reached the point of total dependencelessness, I finally regret that my previous efforts were applied in error.
Later, he said to the assembly: "In the study of Zen, one must know oneself. Do not seek clarity within the words and phrases of the *gong'an*.
For several decades prior, I had been seeking clarity solely within *gong'an* such as 'the yellow gourd' and 'the eggplant'; this was nothing but looking outward. Afterwards..."
Come and listen: that one takes things not with the hands and eats rice not with the mouth. Turn back and reflect upon yourself;

only then will you know that this kōan—this cucumber and eggplant—is not something external. He further said: "I would rather teach you to seek elsewhere; it is far more difficult to teach you to simply rest. Question:
"Master, you were a contemporary of Li Zhuowu, yet there was no formal transmission between you. How could you possibly have been deluded?"
[The student] said, "I am a follower of that school. The Master said, "If there were any transmission, it would be a deviant dharma.
I am not a person under the banner of any of the five schools. All Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations have all emerged from this one school.
[The student] asked, "Is the Way fruit existent, or is it non-existent? The Master said, "To speak of non-existence based on existence—both [extremes] become established."
[The student] said, "How can one immediately attain it? The Master said, "Seek nothing, and you will immediately attain it. [The student] asked, "What is the essence of the Way?

The Master said, "Though my mouth is full, the Way cannot be expressed. [The student] asked, "What is it like when the four elements disperse? The Master held up his fist and said, "This does not belong to the four elements.
[The student] asked, "The ancients said, 'Setting aside the throat, lips, and mouth, bring forth a single phrase. What is that?"
"How can one speak a single phrase? The Master said, "I have not removed my throat, lips, or mouth; you, for your part, try and speak a phrase. The monk had no reply.
The Master said, "Your mouth has been blocked by sounds. [The monk] asked, "Is it true that seeing one's nature is attaining Buddhahood?"
The Master said, “It is. [The monk] asked, “Nature is formless; how can it be seen? The Master said, “Nature has form; it is simply that you do not see it.
[The monk] said, “I ask the Master to point it out for me to see. The Master said, “I am telling you that you do not see it.
[The monk] asked, “How does one transcend birth and death? The Master called to the monk. The monk responded, “Yes. The Master said, “Go forth from here. [The monk] said, “Master...”
The student said, "I do not understand what he further said. The Master said, "When you do understand, what will you be able to do?
The student asked, "Why did he deceive people? The Master said, "You have not yet awakened from your dream, yet you blame others."
Chan Master Yifeng Fangtan of Baima Temple in Kuizhou was the son of the Luo family of Dazhou. He studied under Yun’an of Jinfoshan, who instructed him to contemplate:
"What is this pivotal mechanism that ghosts and spirits cannot perceive? After three years, he attained realization.

He left the gorges to visit various spiritual teachers at length, eventually settling in a thatched hut by Shuangxi. One day at noon while cooking rice, he heard a sound from within the steamer and suddenly attained great enlightenment.
He composed a verse, saying: "The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials have no source from which they emerge; Exhausting all clever thoughts, there is nowhere to seek them.
A step taken before the window, a descent before the hearth— White clouds and blue peaks nod their heads in unison. Nodding in unison! Mount Nanyue and Mount Tiantai share but one tally.
He spoke again: "An eighteen-year-old girl marries a new husband; She spins hemp and twists thread just as she always has. According to her family's means, she is well-provided for."

Jian was passing through the area at that time. He relied on the incense burning before the hall for his sustenance. Upon hearing this, Wuhuan remarked, "This man must have practiced subtle and refined cultivation.
In the autumn of the Renchen year of the Wanli era, he returned to Zhongxing Monastery in Dazhou. When a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
the Master replied, "Fire burns at both ends, yet smoke issues from only one. He constantly held a small hand-drum (*táo*) in his hand.
The drum: on one side it bears the character "chù" (矗), and on the other side it bears the character "bēn" (犇). Whenever responding to questions, he would frequently raise and shake it.
He entered nirvana and his stupa was enshrined at Longshen Mountain.
Chan Master Xian of Yang’an at Ehu in Guangxin Prefecture was the son of the Zhu family from Shangrao in the prefectural capital.

Once, while visiting relatives, he encountered a practitioner discussing the meaning of the four modes of birth (*catur-yoni*). Upon hearing these words, the Master thoroughly realized the great principle of the equality of self and others.
He went to Taiting in Luoyang to shave his head, then returned south to Jiaoshan to observe the winter retreat (*laba*). There, he heard that while pushing a boat through the river, there was...

[The Master] reflected. A verse says: "The night is still, the river vast and empty; I push my boat with a *li-li* sound. Knowing not where it goes, One side of the pack-bag has grown light. He visited Huashan.
Hearing the Master’s presentation of the "one piece of livelihood, not caught in the six" koan, he applied himself with fierce intensity.
After seven days, his body and mind were liberated. He subsequently returned to his hometown and resided at Lingshan. He painted a great circle on the wall and said:
Do not allow the interior to be smeared black; do not allow the exterior to be made white again.

If there is anyone who can provide a commentary upon both the interior and the exterior of this circle, I grant you permission to study the Way without doubt. Otherwise, it will all be nothing but *mālava* (vain effort). Later, while residing at Ehu for ten years, he did not appoint a seat-head (*zuo-yuan*).
Boshan came to study with him and attained resonance through the "No-Word" (*wuzi*) koan of Zhaozhou; he was subsequently invited to reside there.
The Abbot presented him with a verse, saying: "Ten years at Gehu, the position was vacant; for what reason did you suddenly establish yourself as a youth?
Two eyebrows, eight strands—know that Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot precede this. He once installed the "Gateless Lock" on the wall of the Hall to test those from all quarters.
He wrote a verse: "The lock handed down from antiquity / Relies on your wisdom-key to open it. If there is no opening..."
The Method of Sealing. On the final day of the second month in the Dingmao year of the Wanli era, the Master ascended the hall to preach the Dharma and prepared a vegetarian feast.
As a parting gesture, he presented this verse: "Within eighty-odd years of illusory dreams, An iron ox plows through the vast void."
As he was about to depart, he entrusted [his disciples] with a single phrase: "At midnight, the golden sun brings forth the crimson light.
He then sat upright and passed away. *Wudeng Huiyuan Xulue*, Scroll Two, Part Two, Phonetic Glossary.
Cuì (qù, sound). Cù (cāngmò, qì; sudden/impetuous). Bèn (bēiyàn, qì; to lower the coffin). Zhī (zhuójiē, qì; the exposed root of a withered tree). Shèng (shízhèng, qì;
remainder). Yù (yúliù, qì). Tāo (yúzhāo, qì). Dùn (a vulgar form of the character tún). Lí (línxī, qì; to encounter/suffer).
*Wǔdēnghuìyuán Xùlüè*, Scroll Three, Part One.
Compiled by the Chan monk Jingzhu, a successor to the ancestral lineage at Zhiti Mountain,
of the eighteenth generation below Nanyue in the Linji school.
Chan Master Pò'ān Zuǎn of Wòlóng Mountain in Kuīzhōu was a dharma heir of Chan Master Tiāntóng Jié. He was the son of the Wáng family from Guǎng'ān Prefecture.

Initially, he studied under Mìmǎn and attained realization upon hearing the words of his formal address. Later, when Mìmǎn resided at Línghǐn Monastery, he appointed Master Zuǎn to share the teaching seat. A practitioner of the Way then requested [instruction].
Yi asked, "When a monkey cannot be caught, what then? The Master said, "What is the use of trying to catch it?
It is like wind blowing over water; ripples form naturally. Later, after he had settled in his abode, he ascended the hall and said, "It is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing.
Unable to restrain my impatience, I shall provide for you all a way to cast off [delusions]. He took up his staff, struck once, and said, "The flowing water is dark..."
*Extinguishing Stones by the Stream*: An Exhortation to Eliminate Right and Wrong.
Chan Master Songyuan Chongyue of Lingyin Temple in Lin’an was the son of the Wu family of Longquan in Chuzhou.
In his youth, he aspired to the Dharma of world-transcendence. Having met Dahui at Mount Jing, Dahui praised him in the Lecture Hall, saying that Ying’an’s way of guiding people was direct and swift.
Upon hearing this, the Master set out before dawn. Once he arrived, he consulted with him morning and evening.

When Yan’an cited the words, "The World-Honored One had secret words, which Kāśyapa did not conceal," the Master remarked, "This leaves me at a loss. Yan’an let out a thunderous shout, and the Master attained realization.
Yan’an was greatly pleased and regarded him as a vessel for the Dharma. At the beginning of the Longxing era, the Master finally received full ordination and went to Min to see Muguan.
Dongshan Shouchu said, "There is a phrase and there is no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree. The Master said, "Torn asunder! Dongshan said, "Langye says, 'What a pile of rotten firewood!
What do you think? The Master said, "Adding a point to an existing arrow. They exchanged such responses several times.

Dongshan said, "My brother’s utterances are such that even an old monk like I cannot surpass them; yet, they are still not it. In the future, when the fly-whisk handle is in your hands, you must act for others."
"No, it cannot be verified. The Master said, "For one who acts as a teacher, it is indeed difficult to cause an ordinary person of common ground to leap directly into the realm of the sages.
But for one who verifies others—if they strike right before one's face and one already knows their very marrow without waiting for them to open their mouth—what difficulty could there be?
The Hermit raised his hand and said, "Clearly I have told you: opening the mouth is not a matter of the tongue."
[The Master] said: "Later, you shall know this for yourself. Over a year later, he met Mian at Xishan. Whenever [the Master] questioned him, Mian would simply smile.
The Master was so intent on reaching ultimate realization that he forgot both sleep and food.

On one occasion, while Mian was entering the room and questioning a monk about the phrase, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing," the Master, standing by his side, attained a sudden and great enlightenment, whereupon he exclaimed: "Today..."
He then met Mudan Dao, who said, "The opening of the mouth does not reside on the tongue. Naturally, his skillful eloquence was unrestrained.

He subsequently appeared in the world at Chengzhao in Pingjiang, and later moved to Guangxiao, Yeyu, Jianfu, Xiangshan, and Huqiu. In the third year of the Qingyuan era, he received an imperial decree to take charge of Lingyin.
Upon ascending the hall, he said: "In general, to uphold the lineage of the school, one must possess the correct eye upon the crown of the head."
Hanging the numinous talisman behind his elbow, it was just like when Baoshou opened the hall and Sansheng pushed forward a monk;
Baoshou struck him immediately. Sansheng said, "To act as a teacher in this manner is to blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to his quarters. These two venerable masters, in their casual jostling and pressing one another, suddenly gave rise to [the realization].
To clarify the mind-essence of Linji: it is simply that one does not realize that life and nature are entirely in the hands of this monk.
Is there anyone who can discern this? In years past, seeking fire, I obtained smoke; today, carrying water, I return with the moon. To the assembly:
An ancient said, "When lifted up, heaven turns and earth revolves; when set down, the grass bows and the wind blows. Yeshu...

It is not so. When you pick it up, heaven and earth turn pitch black; when you let it go, even rubble gives off light. Suddenly, if there is one or half of a person who, in a flash, blinds the aperture at the crown of the head, the Dharma-lineage of Bodhidharma will not yet have reached its decline.

[He addressed the assembly: It is not so. When you pick it up, heaven and earth turn pitch black; when you let it go, even rubble gives off light. Suddenly, if there is one or half of a person who, in a flash, blinds the aperture at the crown of the head, the Dharma-lineage of Bodhidharma will not yet have reached its decline. [He addressed the assembly:]
Regarding the kōan of Linji’s “weed-whisk,” Xuedou said, “Linji’s letting go was too precarious; his gathering back was too swift.
The Master [Zhaozhou] took up his staff and said, “Linji acted according to the mandate, yet he did not realize he had brought shame upon Huangbo.
Xuedou carried this burden with all his might, but he saw only one side. Now tell me, where does the crux of Jianfu lie?”
"Where? He threw down his staff and addressed the assembly. Citing Fenyang, he said: "Fenyang said, 'If you recognize this staff, your journey as a wandering monk is finished.
Although Fenyang was like opening his mouth to show his gallbladder, he could not avoid falling into the second place.
Suddenly picking up the staff, he said: "This one must not be called a staff; it is a lacquer bucket! [He then gave] a turning phrase for the meditation hall.
He said, "Is it the wind that moves, or is it the banner that moves? The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him. Again he said, "It is not the wind that moves, nor is it the banner that moves.
The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him again. He further said, "Why does a person of great power fail to lift their foot?
Again he said, "The opening of the mouth is not upon the tongue. Again he said, "Why does a monk with clear eyes..."
He struck him and lost his nose. "There is a thief, but no stolen goods. A monk asked, "What is the first: 'The same, the same substance'? The Master said, "Torn asunder.
The monk asked, "What is the second: 'The same, the great matter'? The Master said, "To settle heaven and earth upon the tip of a single hair.
The monk asked, "What is the third: 'All together participating'? The Master said, "Frogs, earthworms, centipedes, and blind turtles. The monk asked, "What is..."
[Question: "What are the four 'identical true wisdoms'? [Master: "One is not established; two are not so. [Question:
"What are the five 'identical partial and universal'? [Master: "Taking up the entire earth, there is not even an inch of soil. [Question: "What are the six 'identical fulfillments'?
[Master: "There is still one thing lacking. [Question: "What are the seven 'identical gains and losses'? [Master: "Entering the mud, entering the water. [Question: "As for..."
"What is the eighth, 'killing together'? The Master said, "One cannot even save oneself. "What is the ninth, 'roaring with the same sound'?
The Master said, "An octagonal millstone rolling in the void. "What is the tenth, 'entering together'?
The Master said, "Hanshan meets Shide. "With whom do you enter together? The Master said, "The Hu Zhangsan and the Black Lisan."
[The student] asked, "With whom does he share the same sound in roaring? The Master said, "The cat and the white ox. [The student] asked, "How do they share the same life and death?

The Master said, "Deishan’s staff and Linji’s shout. [The student] asked, "What thing shares the same gain and loss? The Master said, "Rolling about in the grass. [The student] asked, "Which one is fully endowed with it?
The Master said, "Picking up whatever comes to hand; every stroke is direct. [The student] asked, "What is it that is the same? The Master said, [silence].
"Partial or universal? The Master said, "Riding a great Peng within the shadow of a needle-point; casually pushing down the moon at the edge of the sky.
"Who shares true wisdom? The Master said, "The ghost cave of Black Mountain. "Who is a fellow practitioner in the ultimate sense?
The Master said, "A lantern entering a pillar. "Which one shares in the Great Matter? The Master said, "The Great Elephant of Jiazhou and the Iron Ox of Shanfu. "..."

"What thing has a single substance? The Master replied, "A bowl slipped off a mound. The Master retired to the Eastern Hermitage. Shortly thereafter, he was afflicted with a slight illness, whereupon he wrote this verse:
"Coming, there is nowhere from which one comes; Going, there is nowhere to which one goes. In a flash, the profound pivot is turned— Even Buddhas and Patriarchs are at a loss.
He passed away while sitting in the lotus position. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the slopes of North High Peak.
Chan Master Zuteng Zijing of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Gao family of Fuzhou. Ringing the bell, he addressed the assembly:
"A single mold produces a finished form, yet it remains full of elegance; On level ground, he instructs others not to rest content.
If you wish for a majestic resonance to resound through the universe, You must surely ascend one more floor."
Chan Master Caoyuan Sheng of Jianfu Temple in Raoyou was a native of Nanjian. He composed a verse on Lingyun’s Rock, which says:
Clouds come and clouds go, yet they have no intention; Clouds come and clouds go, yet they have no mind. When existence and non-existence are cut off, where is the numinous?
A solitary peak stands abruptly, its greenness reaching to this day.
Chan Master Wanyan Zirou of Yinjing in Taiping Prefecture was a native of the Chen family of Chaozhou.

Once, ascending the hall, he cited the story of Chan Master Tianyi Huai regarding the phrase, "A wild goose flies across the vast sky, its shadow sinking into the cold water. He offered this verse: "A lone wild goose cries out in the autumn across the vast sky;
The Persian merchant offering his treasure has a nose like a hook. The wind sweeps white clouds back to distant peaks; At twilight, the moon hangs on high."
The tips of the willow threads.
In the Chan verse on the transformation of salt by Chan Master Qian’an Huiguang of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture, he says: “Water and mud are boiled together in one place;
when the water dries and the mud is spent, snow-flakes of salt bloom. Seizing the moment to lift it up, its price reaches the heavens; the official seal is clearly manifest.”
Who would dare to dispute this?
Layman Zhang Zi, a Court Gentleman, styled Yuoqi and named Gongfu, was a descendant of the Prince of Zhonglie. He held the office of Academician of the Secretariat.
He visited Mian’s Chou Chamber, where Monan gave him instruction; thereupon, while discussing the "Puppy" koan, he suddenly heard the sound of a bell.
Awakening through Sound. The verse says: With a single stroke of the bell, the faculty of hearing is blocked; from the side of the lump of flesh, a thief is driven away.

When someone asks me what school I understand, I say: "The face of the Śūnyatā-deva is black. He wrote to inform them of his realization and subsequently cleared his path among the forest groves, wandering leisurely in a small garden by the South Lake.
Sometimes wearing a simple cloth cap and trailing his robes through the woods, he came and went chanting and singing, dwelling in profound serenity.
Yet he forgot to return home. He once said: "The sages of old have said that only one who is not defiled by worldly sentiments is able to preach the Dharma and deliver sentient beings.
For within the *Glorious Treasury* (*Ābhāsvara-garbha*), what is not a playful manifestation?

If the mind is ever pure and free from all grasping and attachment, one can constantly enter the samādhi of non-differentiation amidst the realm of differentiated phenomena; thus, one may travel everywhere through brothels and wine shops."
In the place of practice (*bodhimaṇḍa*), the sounds of drums and music all discourse upon Prajñā.

Yet, if one is aware that emotions create barriers and the environment shifts as it pursues its source, one is like a bird stuck in birdlime—every movement injures its life. How, then, could such a person understand what is meant by "preaching the Dharma to deliver sentient beings"?

For more than seventy years since the restoration of our sagely dynasty, the traditions and refined customs of the ancient houses have almost entirely fallen into decay. Only those who have heard of the exemplary models of their predecessors remain.
One who recognizes the refined eccentricity of Nanhu must surely chant at length: "Human life does not exceed a hundred years, yet one constantly harbors anxieties for a thousand years.
Days are short and nights are long; why not ride upon the light of candles to roam? Once they met, [Nanhu] did not act as a mere guest of this life.
Later, he donated his residence to establish Huiyun Temple and invited Mian to serve as its founding abbot.
Chan Master Wuzhun Shifan of Jingshan in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Wolong Xian, the nineteenth-generation successor in the lineage below Mount Nanyue.
He was the son of the Yong clan from Zitong in Jianzhou; he was nine years old [when he entered the monastic life].

Having left the household life, he requested instruction from an elder regarding the method of sitting meditation (*zazen*). The elder asked, "What is this 'meditation,' and who is it that sits? The Master investigated this day and night.
One day, while on the toilet, he attained realization upon bringing the previous dialogue to mind. He then went to visit Fozhao at Yuyang Monastery.
Fozhao asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Jianzhou. Fozhao asked, "Have you brought your sword with you? At these words, the Master let out a shout.
Zhaoxiao said, "This was Wutouzi; chaos ensued. When they reached Lingyin, Poban served as the First Seat.
While traveling together at Shisun, a practitioner there requested instruction on the "Monkey Child" koan. As the Master stood by his side, he attained great enlightenment.
Initially he resided at Qingyuan in Mingzhou; later, by imperial decree, he presided over Jingshan. Ascending the hall, he said: "At Vulture Peak they pointed to the moon;
at Caoxi they spoke of the moon. Passed down from generation to generation, they have taken a turtle and certified it as a soft-shelled turtle.
Elder Fan usually has a mouth hanging on the wall that has never been moved. Today, for no reason, he has entered this gateway. Now that the matter has come to this, [only...]”
Having sifted through it from east to west, I could not avoid picking up an old almanac and marking out a few points therein.

I shall describe these places where people have been misled to you all, simply so that Guo Da, Li Er, Deng Si, and Zhang San may know that it is cold in the spring and hot in the autumn across Jiangnan and Liangzhe.
Even so, the Yellow River clears itself but once every three thousand years. [He ascends the hall.]
If we discuss this matter directly, it is simply straightforward, essential, and easy to understand; yet most people create their own difficulties and obstacles for themselves.
Therefore, when I sometimes see people on the eastern or western corridors bowing in greeting, I merely lower my head to receive them.
In truth, there is nothing else to it: I simply want everyone to recognize that this old man is from Sichuan.
He was a native of Longqing Prefecture. If you were to recognize him, you could engage in some local dialect with him and speak some local talk.
For now, let us not yet discuss whether you recognize this Elder; first, let each of you know your own native place.
Do you also know how it is? At the Upper Hall in Fenghua, one of the eight districts of the six counties of Mingzhou, [the Master] said:
"It cannot be named; it cannot be described; it cannot be grasped; it cannot be relinquished. It is simply thus. But tell me, what have you attained?

Three people testify that a tortoise has become a turtle. Emperor Lizong summoned him into the Xuzheng Hall; his responses were detailed and clear, and he was granted a golden-embroidered *saṃghāṭī* robe. Furthermore...
An imperial edict was proclaimed for him to ascend the seat at Ciming Hall to preach the Dharma; the Emperor listened from behind a curtain. He was granted the title Fojian.
On the first day of the third month in the Jiyou year of the Chunyou era (1249), he fell ill. He then ascended the seat and addressed the assembly, saying: "This mountain monk is both old and sick."
"I have been unable to engage in idle chatter with you all. Now, exerting myself, I shall bring forth everything I have not previously spoken and shake it all out before you.
He then rose, shook his robes, and asked, "How much is there? Having said this, he returned to the abbot's quarters.
On the fifteenth day, he gathered the assembly and gave them his final instructions. That night, he wrote a verse: "When I came, I was empty-handed; When I go, I am empty-handed again."
He departed, stark naked. Seeking further to inquire into the ultimate truth, he crossed the Stone Bridge at Tiantai and passed away in a mere moment.
His entire body was enshrined in the Yuanzhao Hermitage.

Chan Master Shitian Faxun of Lingyin in Lin’an Prefecture was the son of the Peng family from Meishan. Initially, while traveling to visit Shishuang, he paid his respects at the stupa of Lei Qian and composed a verse, saying:
"A single thought of your compassionate countenance is fundamentally unobstructed; why must you suddenly display such eccentricity?
Your heart’s desire to level the high and accommodate the low is so earnest that it vexes Master Lei into a night of busy toil. It was because of this that the Master’s name became renowned.

Chao heard of the renown of Dao-wang of Qionglong Po-an and went there to rely upon him. In the meditation hall, when the master raised the story of the World-Honored One holding up a flower and Kāśyapa smiling, the teacher said:
"A scorched brick strikes and freezes through to the bottom; red-eyed one bumps into a firebrand. Po-an marveled at this in secret.
Initially, he resided at Gao-feng in Su-zhou, and later moved to Feng-qiao, Zhong-shan, Jing-ci, and Ling-yin. There, he addressed the assembly:

"Attain only the root; do not worry about the branches. What do you call this "root"? What do you call this "branch"? "The pine and cypress remain green for a thousand years, yet they do not enter the minds of the fashionable. The peony blooms red for a single day, yet the gentlemen of the city all become drunk.

When a mountain monk speaks thus, if there be anyone who does not agree, such a person is my fellow student. Disciple Shi Jun painted a portrait of the Master and requested a eulogy.
