He said, "The final phrase has been entrusted to Chushan. The assembly was quite surprised by this. The following day, he suddenly manifested illness and retired to Baoshou Temple to prepare for his end.
He calculated that his entire body should be interred on the mountain behind the monastery.
Chan Master Jican Cijue of Yunju in Nankang Prefecture was a native of Shu. He cited a monk’s question to Xie County: “What is the place where a student secretly applies the mind?
Xie County said, “Rolling a ball in a bustling marketplace. The monk asked, “What is the meaning of this?
Xie County said, “Invite everyone to watch. The Master composed a verse: Rolling a ball in the bustling market, everyone watches; A gust of pure wind [sweeps through].
The wind blowing on one's face is cold. To settle the chaos, there is no need for a double-edged sword; to bring life back, what necessity is there for the nine-return elixir?

When the Master first ascended to Yunju, he stayed overnight at the Yaotian village. One night, he dreamed that the deity of the monastery, Anle Gong, said to him, "You have only the karmic connection for a single bowl of gruel with this mountain.
The next day after noon, he arrived at the temple. After the evening discourse was concluded, he met his fellow monks.

Two monks had quarreled so fiercely that their dispute reached the temple authorities, and as a result, the Master was summarily expelled according to the standard treatment for new arrivals. The Master harbored deep suspicion and resentment.
Several years later, a scholar from Shu who held office at court and was a personal friend of the Master invited him to fill the vacant seat at Yunju.
The Master joyfully accepted the command; however, before he could set out on his journey, his dream came true: he passed away while staying at Yaotian Village.
Chan Master Wengwen Wenli of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Lingyin Yue. He was the son of the Ruan family in Lin’an, Hangzhou.

His ancestral home was at the foot of Mount Tianmu. When the master was six years old, he accompanied his mother to gather mulberry leaves, carrying a basket. Suddenly, he awoke and thought of the basket he was carrying.
"Who is this person? Thinking thus, he conceived the aspiration for renunciation. At sixteen, he received ordination and studied under Master Huanxuan.

Xuan presented him with the public case of "I grant you thirty blows," but the teacher did not find resonance with it. He then went to visit Master Fozhao. Fozhao asked, "For one who comes in such a manner, who is your true master?
The teacher suddenly attained realization of the meaning. On another day, Fozhao asked, "Is it the wind that moves, or is it the banner that moves?"
"What about the Sangha? The Master said, "When the object meets its owner, the eye stands upright. Again he asked, "It is not the wind moving, nor is it the banner moving;
where do you see the Patriarch? The Master said, "Lift off the skull-cap. Zhao Xī admired his brilliance and took him as his secretary (shuji).
After some time, he heard Songyuan preaching the Way at Jianfu Temple in Raozhou. In the meditation hall, Songyuan questioned a monk: "It is not the wind..."
"Movement is not the movement of the banner. As soon as the monk hesitated, the Master struck him with his staff. Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly forgot all intellectual understanding.
He went to study under [Zhaozhou] and received his seal of approval. In the fifth year of the Jiading era, he began teaching at Guangshou Huiyun in Lin’an, and later moved to Nengren and Jingci.
In his quarters, he would frequently raise the koans of "the southern mountain bamboo shoots" and "the eastern sea cuttlefish. Whenever a student hesitated, the Master would immediately—
He struck the meditation staff three times, and there was no one who could settle upon it. Later, he moved his residence to Fiquan and ascended to the abbacy of Tiantong.
On the day he opened the hall for formal discourse, a monk asked: "When the Master sees Buddha Zhao, what is it like? The Master said: "There is jade within the stone. The monk asked:
"After seeing Songyuan, what is it like? The Master said: "There is no oil in the sand. A monk asked: "Observing the directions, one knows where they go; as for those who go..."
He did not know what the Master’s intention was. The Master said, "The village ahead has not yet been reached, and the inn behind has not yet been passed.
A monk who had come forward went straight into the abbot’s quarters and said, "I, this humble monk, have a formal petition to submit to the Master.
The Master asked, "Where is the defendant? The monk replied, "The Master is he himself. The Master said, "What grievance or enmity do I have with you? You have come without cause."
[The Master] spoke. He seized [Hu] and said, "Worthy friend! Worthy friend! Hu, the *vina*, came forward to take his leave. The Master asked, "What is your name? He replied, "Zhihu (Wisdom Tiger).
The Master stepped back and made a gesture of fear. Hu hesitated; the Master immediately returned to his quarters. He ascended the hall and said:

"In the depths of late winter, the cold is extreme and the myriad trees are withered and broken. Only the plum blossom possesses a tenfold air of pure elegance. Beyond the wild bridge and flowing waters, amidst the thatched huts..."
Leaving the short fence by the side, the mountain monk does not understand the intent of the Eastern Emperor; he sniffs the cold fragrance three times and stands in the evening sun.
Entering the hall: The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it arises only by relying on conditions. Since conditions do not exist, from where could the Dharma be established?
The dragon pool pouring down a thousand-foot waterfall is not the condition; the wild goose peak soaring ten-thousand-fathom high in the freezing cold is not the Dharma. Those with clear eyes—
When a patch-robed monk arrives here, what should he do? Even if he were bold and discerning, this mountain monk would not let him off even if his staff were broken.
Why? Because it is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life. Entering the hall: In every matter there is no obstruction;
green mountains cast their shadows beyond the slanting sun. In every dharma there is no discrepancy; ancient trees before the railing are swarming with crows. Do you not see, O Prince of Taiyuan?
The Venerable Fu traveled to the ends of the earth to Yangzhou; at the fifth watch, he heard the painted horn blowing, scattering plum blossoms.
Even unto this day, he has not yet reached home. On the occasion of the Imperial Birthday, he ascended the hall and sat; in the crystal palace hung the "night-bright" curtain.
He is a seamless unity, difficult to encompass, yet responding to all conditions without error. From of old, this station has been honored and exalted. Furthermore—
How can one raise and chant a single phrase with the whole body in reverent offering? The wondrous leaves respond to all capacities, entering together into the tribute;

let the various paths be allowed their own provisional distinctions. On the anniversary of Master Hongzhi’s passing, he ascended the hall: "Beyond the night-bright curtain, before the jeweled mirror stand."

Originally there is no duality; how could there be partiality or perfection? At such a time, who ultimately occupies the position of correctness? "The ancient ford is empty of people, the frosty moon is cold;

the wind is still among the reeds, and the herons sleep. The Master was particularly profound in the *I Ching*. During the Quan and Chun periods, various Confucian scholars greatly propagated the School of Daoxue;
the Master associated with them, yet he directly investigated them through the School of Mind-learning (*Xinxue*) without yielding in the least. This was Zhu Xi, the Dark Sage (Huiweng).

When Yang Wenyi asked about the meaning of "Do not fail to be reverent," the Master joined his palms and demonstrated it to him. When Yang Cihu asked about the power of "not deceiving," the Master replied with a verse:
"This power is clearly found in non-deception; How many people can truly understand non-deception?

If you wish to clarify the phrase that fully encompasses both the elephant and the rabbit, Look at the moment he ascends the steps with his ceremonial tablet held upright. The Master retired from the monastery and lived in leisure upon the banks of Liangzhu.

The assembly of monks gathered to strike the bell for him as they would for any other resident of the monastery. As he was about to enter nirvana, he said to his attendant, "Who will build a seamless stupa for me?
The attendant asked, "Please, Master, show us the model for the stupa. The Master replied, "Exert yourselves; do not go out during the day. Then, with a serene countenance, he passed away.
Chan Master Wude Juetong of Huazang in Changzhou ascended the hall on the occasion of the Green Sprout Festival: "Shatter a single mote of dust and the Great Sutra emerges;
The soaring hawks and leaping fish become even more distinct. Do not look with the eyes, but look with the mind; Already you see the repeated striking of ice within the fire.
Soaking black beans, one’s whole life is obscured; One must speak of the bountiful harvest beyond the kalpas. The silk is spun into white snow."
The mulberry trees are deep green; the yellow clouds of rice have been harvested, and the grain is now turning green.
This was Chan Master Daxie Zhongqian of Xuedou in Qingyuan Prefecture, a native of the Ying family of Yiwu, Jinhua.

In his youth, upon seeing the *Mind-King Inscription* by the Great Master Fu (Dashi), he vowed to leave the household life. He first met Xian’an, who regarded him as a vessel of the Dharma yet restrained his [ambitions].
Rui said, "If you do not eliminate the habitual tendencies of the Confucian school, how can you reach the state of great rest and great repose?
You should become like a person made of earth or wood. The Master studied this morning and evening until he attained realization; consequently, he named himself "Daxie" (Great Rest).
Later, upon meeting Songyuan, one day he heard the story of Bimozhi Holding the Pole. Suddenly, he cried out, "Alas! How can anyone bear to remain dissatisfied?"

Yuan held up his bamboo whisk and said, "I strike you because you cannot bear it. As the Master was about to offer a word in response, the whisk suddenly came down upon him; he was utterly at a loss for a reply.
Yuan let out a thunderous shout, and the Master immediately attained sudden enlightenment.
Chan Master Yun’an Puyan of Daochang Mountain in Anjī Prefecture offered this verse in praise of Zhaozhou:

"Without cause, he lifted up the seven-pound robe; How many practitioners of Chan have fixated on its meaning! They all take refuge in the 'Qingzhou' [robe] as their nest, Failing to realize that the spring colors lie in Jiangnan."
Chan Master Shankaikai of Jinshan Yanshi in Zhenjiang Prefecture ascended the hall and, citing the story of Mian’s “Breaking the Sand Pot,” offered this verse:
Fayan brought it up and was already deceiving himself; Needlessly, he wrongly matched it to the broken sand pot. Now, throughout the entire world, it cannot be concealed;
It brings calamity to the monastic groves and burdens the descendants.
Chan Master Xilian of Shiyuan Longxiang in Wenzhou was the son of the Ma family of Huya. A monk asked:
"In the past, when Emperor Xiaozong summoned Chan Master Fozhao Guang for an audience and asked, 'What did Śākyamuni accomplish during his six years in the mountains?
Fozhao replied, 'I thought Your Majesty had forgotten. What was the meaning of this? The Master answered with a verse: The Great Root...
A great vessel, a great cultivation; in a fleeting turn of the pivot, one reaches the ultimate source. For ten billion years there has been but one Buddha;
the Snowy Mountains have never separated him from the Dragon Palace.
Chan Master Shaoshi Guangmu of Ruiyan in Taizhou offered this eulogy for the Fourth Patriarch: "Purple clouds fly atop Mount Poutou;
Three times he declined the imperial summons in the green mists. Though his 'stale goods' have no further use, He should not have handed them down to a mere grandson."
Chan Master Beihai Xin’s verse on the occasion of Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty and the clam says: Mixing water with mud, busy with such affairs;
He was exposed by that [clam], which was far too audacious. Though he silently accorded with the Sovereign’s intent, He has already cast his whole body into the boiling cauldron.
Chan Master Zhao of Nu’an composed a verse on the occasion of Nanquan carving a Buddha, which says: Held in both hands, it is difficult to cover;
As before, with both hands, he hands it back. On a pillow of pure breeze, sleep is deep and sound; Birds fly and flowers fall upon the path before the crags.
Chan Master Guyuan Dao of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture composed a verse on the story of Shitou clearing weeds, saying:
Shitou cleared the weeds to test the heroes; Dana was muddled, his eyes not yet lofty. Had he known how to turn back and walk the living path, To this day he would not have burdened his descendants.
The Layman Lu You, styled Wuguan and nicknamed Fangong, was a descendant of Lu Dian and a native of Shanyin in Yue.
He once asked Songyuan, "May I hear about the learning transmitted through the mind? Songyuan replied, "Since it is transmitted through the mind, how could it be obtained from hearing?
Gong attained realization and offered this verse: "Several times I drove my carriage into the imperial city; Whenever I encountered a monk, I treated them all alike."
His eyes were both blue; this morning he first realized the distinctiveness of the Chan school. To speak of existence and discuss emptiness, one must listen with the eye.

Zen Master Qingxi Yuan of Jingci Monastery in Yuanzhou, successor to Zen Master Tiantong Jing, ascended the hall and said: "Since Bodhidharma came from the West, he has occupied a single sitting mat."

The divine light of that deity performed three prostrations and simultaneously occupied [the space], causing later generations of descendants to divide their territories and demarcate their boundaries.
Members of the monastic community pluck the weeds and gaze at the wind, traveling from Wu to Yue morning and evening; to the South is Tiantai, to the North is Wutai.
Have you ever, upon the tip of your staff or the sole of your straw sandals, actually trodden upon it? After a long silence, he said: "Be careful not to step on it."

Chan Master Chijue Daochong of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Jianfu Sheng. He was the son of the Xun family from Wuxin. His natural disposition was extraordinary;
having failed in his attempts at the jinshi examination, he received instruction under Master Shaohui at Miaoyin Monastery in Zizhou. In the third year of the Shaohui era, he crossed the Gorges.
At that time, Cao Yuan was appearing in the world as Miaoguo. The Master went to visit him; upon hearing the words he spoke as he entered the gate, he attained realization.

Cao Yuan had him attend at his side for three years. Then, departing to travel to Mount Shu, he offered this verse: "There remains but one pair of destitute hands, which must scratch the itchy places throughout all quarters.
He then went to study under Songyuan at Lingyin. Songyuan’s teaching style was steep and formidable; [the Master] stayed there for eight months, living beneath a straw raincoat.
He was not permitted to enter the room. Someone reported that he had lost his man. Yuan said, "I have opened the door with eight characters and allowed him to stay;
he is simply himself—he just missed the mark right before my face. When the Master heard these words, both his mouth and ears were silenced.
He saw clearly that when Cao’an was at Miaoguo and Guipeng, laughter, jesting, anger, and abuse were all skillful means for the sake of others. From that time on...
He caused the tongues of the old monks throughout the world to hang down in doubt. He first resided at Tianning in Jiaxing;
after only half a year had passed since he moved to Xuefeng, an imperial edict appointed him to succeed at Tiantong. When the seat at Yuyang was vacant, he concurrently served as its abbot.
Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The tools used at Tiantong do not apply here at Yuyang; the tools used here at Yuyang do not apply at Tiantong. Nevertheless, though they are used in this way—"
Attaching. Where there is no attachment, function has a surplus. One arrow, two eagles, falling at the hand’s touch. Ascending the hall:
In the monastery of Perfect Enlightenment, every mote of dust has a path. Sitting and cutting off coming and going, the present and the past are suddenly emptied. Thirteen here, fifteen there.
"The sequence of before and after is not off by even a hair’s breadth—this is laughable! The Yellow-Faced Gautama has yet to know where it lands. He ascended the hall and said:

"There is one person who, in a single thought-moment, suddenly realizes [enlightenment] and falls into the ranks of the Buddhas. There is another person who, for kalpas on end, remains a *icchantika* (one devoid of faith) and does not wish to become a Buddha.
Now tell me, which of these two deserves to receive the offerings of devas and humans? After a long silence, he said: "A butterfly pierces a fragrant path; the pair..."
His eyebrows were wet. Bees plundered the remaining flowers; his two thighs were stout. He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three are without distinction.
What is the past mind? The Master said, "Set it aside and wait until it is cold, then look.
The monk asked, "What is the present mind? The Master said, "You ask and I answer. The monk asked, "What is the future mind? The Master said, "Next time."
Ascending the hall, he said to you all: "What is the Buddha of the past? The Master said, "Last year’s plum blossoms. "What is the Buddha of the present?
The Master said, "This year’s willows. "What is the Buddha of the future? The Master said, "The color and fragrance remain as they were.
"What is the differentiated wisdom of the past? The Master struck the meditation seat with his whisk.
[The student] asked from the left: "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the present? The Master struck the right side of the meditation seat with his whisk.
[The student] asked: "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the future? The Master made a single dot in the middle of the whisk. [The student] said:
"Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings have no front or back; the oceans of lands in the ten directions are gathered within a single hair. He then prostrated. The Master then said:
The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended.
Since these three minds cannot be apprehended, what do you call "discriminating wisdom"?

If one sees through this thoroughly, the Buddhas of the three periods of time have never for a single moment not been turning the Great Dharma Wheel upon the crowns of everyone's heads. Come here and test it further!

"Shoulders side by side, feet together—what is the use of seeking that bowl? With his staff, he drove them all away at once. Not long after, he was summoned by imperial decree to move to Mount Jingshan.
One day, bidding farewell to the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One, when approaching his parinirvāṇa, addressed the assembly, saying:
'You should carefully contemplate my body of purple-golden hue; gaze upon it until you are fully satisfied, lest you have cause for regret later. Today, [I am likewise here]..."
The next day, he was gone. The Master said, "Throughout his life, the World-Honored One exhausted every skillful means;
yet at the moment of death, he could not find life when seeking it, nor could he find death when seeking it. I, however, am not like this: when I wish to go, I go;
when I wish to leave, I leave. Even the eight-armed Nala cannot stop me. That night, he rose from his seat and passed away within a short while.

Chan Master Shuangshan Yuan, a successor of Chan Master Yinjing Rou, offered this verse on the story of Emperor Taizong’s exhortation to arouse the Bodhicitta: "Ten thousand miles of songs celebrate the Sage’s transformation;
Gentle breezes and falling rain bring joy to woodcutters and farmers. Were it not for the three cries at Mount Song, Who would know the formless [Buddha-nature]?"
Zhentai Ping. The twenty-second generation descendant of Nanyue,
the Dharma heir of Chan Master Jingshan Fan.
Chan Master Xueyan Zuqin of Yangshan in Yuanzhou first studied under Tiejue Yuan while examining the koan of "The Dog Has No Buddha-nature.
Subsequently, he went to Jingci and then to Tianmu. Paying his respects at Tianmu, he said:
"Have you not seen how Linji asked Huangbo for the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma three times, and each time was struck with a severe blow? Finally, [he attained realization] toward..."
Daiyu assisted him from below, struck him three times with his fist, and said, "It turns out Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much at all;
you should simply look in this way. Later, while at Jingshan for many years, he failed to attain thorough awakening.

One day, while walking in the Buddha hall at Tianmu, he looked up and saw a great ancient cypress tree, whereupon the obstructing mass within his breast suddenly dispersed. He first took up residence at Tanzhou.
Longxing later resided at Mount Yang. He served as abbot for six monasteries. Entering the hall, he said: "The white ox on the open ground—black, black—is nowhere to be found when one seeks it.
The mountains are green and the waters are blue; they seem to exist, yet they are as if non-existent. Seen with the eyes and heard with the ears, they are but faint and blurred.
One does not care for them at all, yet the hooves and horns remain. As soon as you stir, their tracks have already vanished. Under the moon, [he sits] idly."
He plays the short flute. Before the wind, he lets go of the long tether. A-he-he! How extraordinary! Now, even if you try to follow him, you cannot go;
he moves freely through the east, west, south, and north, opening his furnace. Entering the hall, he said: "A forge neither cold nor hot; gold and brass, half real and half false.
Cast into vases, platters, hairpins, and bracelets, yet they end up as firewood in the shape of the character 'Pin' (品). Tell me, what is this?"
"How far apart are Zhaozhou’s 'no guest' and 'no host' dialogues? If you have doubts, seek another teacher. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The cold wind is piercing and snow falls from the distant sky. Not only is it impossible to find their trace upon the flames of a red furnace;
even when one enters deep into the reeds, it remains difficult to discern. Often, when people reach this point, ten out of twenty will all claim they have realized the realm of 'one color.'"
This matter—do you not realize it is precisely like flowers in the sky or dust in the eye? At this very moment, tell me: is it the cold of heaven or the cold of man?
After descending from the seat, he circled the hall to drink tea. Because of watching the puppet performance, he ascended the hall [and said]:
"Ghost faces and god heads are pulled by the strings; god heads and ghost faces are pulled by the lines and threads. How many observers and viewers think..."
This is a beauty in red powder. On the stage, she performs a wondrous dance, holding a light silk white fan in her hand.
This mountain monk cannot help but pull back the curtain for everyone. Tapping his staff, he said: "A clever monk sees it at once upon seeing it."
Chan Master Duanqiao Miaolun of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Xu family from Huangyan in Taizhou.
At the age of eighteen, he shaved his head at Guangci Monastery in Yongjia. He went to Ruiyan to see Guyuan, where he heard the koan of "Three Pounds of Flax" and came to doubt it.
Suddenly, while [passing through] Lengqia, he realized that even mosquitoes, insects, and ants can perform their functions without verbal expression. He attained sudden enlightenment.
He then visited Wuzhun at Xuedou. Wuzhun asked him, "For what reason does a dog have consciousness? and commanded the Master to provide a response.
After thirty turns, he still did not attain realization. The Master asked, "Is there no expedient means? Zhun answered with a verse by Zhenjing.
At that moment, he stood transfixed for a long while; suddenly, upon hearing the sound of the wooden board, sweat poured from his entire body. Thereupon, he was finally liberated.
He traveled from Shijian Monastery to Ruiyan Guoqing, and finally arrived at Jingci. Ascending the hall, he said: "In the mountains of Jing there is jade;
those who obtain it do not find it within the mountains themselves. In the waters of Chi there is a pearl; those who pick it up do not find it within the waters themselves.

So too, monks have the 'True Person of No Rank'; those who realize him do not find his entry and exit within the face-gate. He then suddenly took up his staff, held it crosswise, and said: "Do you understand?"
"Ma! A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou. He ascends the hall and says: "Deshan lowers his head; Jia Shan nods his head; Jueyi raises a finger;
Xuansha strikes and breaks off his big toe. Holding up his staff, he says: "All of these do not go beyond the tip of this mountain monk’s staff.
How is this to be seen? He plants the staff on the ground and says: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to all under heaven. Up.

The Hall Master raised up the case of Chan Master Daguan Ying, who addressed the assembly, saying: "The seven Buddhas are the subjects of nature; the myriad dharmas are the slaves of the mind. Now tell me, where is the master?

He then gave a shout himself and said, "From the seven Buddhas downward, they all show their heads. Again, he responded himself, saying, "Each shall attend to his own duties. The Master [Zhaozhou] said:
"To call the seven Buddhas 'subjects of nature' and to point to the myriad dharmas as 'slaves of the mind'—[is this not a mistake?]"
Daguan claimed to himself that he had found the path of transcendence; yet, when it came to shouting at himself and responding to himself, he was still acting within the realm of a slave.
When has the true master ever been seen even in a dream? Do you all wish to see him? With a single sweep of his whisk, he said:

"A spring breeze stirs at dawn, causing a hundred varieties of flowers to bloom throughout the gardens. He then assembled the community for his final audience, entered his room, and composed a letter.
He took his leave of the various mountains. When Duke of the Wei State sent an emissary to inquire privately, saying, "The Master was born at Tiantai; why did he die at Jingci?
the Master replied, "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. He then wrote a verse and passed away.
Chan Master Xiyuan Hui of Tiantong in Mingzhou composed a verse on the story of the Sixth Patriarch transmitting the robe, saying:

He did not become a woodcutter, but became a miller; He used only his own strength to test the quality of the grain. Whether he knew he had trodden upon it or not, The rice and the husks alike reached the alms bowl.
Chan Master Bieshan Zu-zhi of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Yang family from Shunqing in Sichuan. At fourteen, he received full ordination.
Upon hearing a monk reciting the words of Sixyan, he was filled with joy; at that time, Yan was residing at Qionglong in Suzhou, so he went there immediately to follow him.
While reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he came across the passage concerning Maitreya’s tower opening and then closing again; he felt as if waking from a dream.
He then composed a verse on Lingyun’s seeing peach blossoms, which read: "A single red dot amidst ten thousand greens—how many rejoice, and how many resent?
Yan approved of it. Finally, he met Wuzhun at Xuedou; Wuzhun recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma and treated him with increasing respect.

Jùn would sometimes deliver blows with his staff and shouts simultaneously, withholding not even a single word of leniency. Whenever the Master attempted to respond, he was immediately silenced and unable to utter a word.
Through this, his reliance on intellectual understanding was completely lost. After some time, he spoke up and said, "All the skills I have cultivated throughout my life are but dead dharmas."
Now, seeing this old man, I have finally found the path to life. Shortly thereafter, he was transferred to Mount Jing; the Emperor commanded that the Master share his seat with him.

In the *Bǎoyù* era, the year *Bǐchén*, he received imperial edict to reside at Tiantong. With but a single bag and a single bowl, he dwelt in a thatched hut. On the first day of the ninth month in the year *Gēngchén*, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"The clouds are thin and the moonlight is fresh; the trees have shed their leaves, and the mountain’s bones are revealed. Since heaven and earth first came into being, how many [have truly seen it]?"
His eyes remained vivid. When someone came to inquire after him, the Master said, "I cannot meet you; each of you must strive for yourselves.
Ten days later, at midnight, he called his attendant and entrusted him with his final instructions, saying, "Hold the assembly in high esteem. He then crossed his hands and passed away in peace.
Chan Master Yuepo Ming cited a monk’s question: "When both mind and Buddha are forgotten, what then? Huì replied, "The old woman selling fans shields her eyes from the sun.
The Master composed a verse on it: The old woman selling fans shields her eyes from the sun; A single style of wind and spirit flows forth from the house.
I tell this to the traveler who has not yet returned home: Why need you go outward to eat *pōzhā*?
Chan Master Huanxi’s verse on the saying “Mind itself is Buddha” says: “Mind itself is Buddha—arsenic and wolfsbane.
To raise the dead and restore life, it requires no more than a single dose.”
Master Xishi Dan raised the following case: A monk asked Nanquan, "When the Master returns to his quarters, with what will you point [to the truth]?

Nanquan replied, "Last night at the third watch, I lost my ox; when I rose at dawn, I had lost my fire. The verse says: With slave-like faces and cringing knees, he runs about asking others. How shameful to see him at Qili Tan, clad in sheepskin robes!

Though Wen Shu was noble as the Son of Heaven, Zi Lu remained a commoner. *Note: The final line appears to be a fragment or a corruption of a traditional couplet regarding the relationship between King Wen Shu (King Wen) and Zi Lu. In this context, it likely serves to illustrate the contrast between worldly status and spiritual integrity.*
View this as an old friend.
Master Ning Chanyue, Yunyin Tui of Hangzhou, ascended the hall and said: "After the rain, the mountain colors before one's eyes are verdant;

amidst the assembly, the breeze is warm and the birdsong is joyful. He struck his meditation seat once and said: "It is laughable that the Old Barbarian (Bodhidharma) lacked the wisdom of transformation at Shaoshi."
He sat before the peak for nine years. Ascending the hall, he said: "The thousand peaks stretch as far as the eye can see, their verdant hues filling the void. Willow catkins drift like cotton wool.
Pity the True Man of No Rank, who has been sleeping in the grass and under the dew all this time. *Ayya!* This spring is passing by once more;
when will it be the year of our return?"

Zen Master Yujue Hui of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou, a successor of Zen Master Lingyin Xun, went to study under Shitai. Shitai brought up the "Seven Years of Cloud Gate" koan, but no one could provide a response.
Suddenly, as a monk was just crossing the gate, Shitai said, "Xuefeng rolls the ball. At that moment, the Master, who had been standing by, suddenly [attained realization].
He attained realization. Spontaneously, he spoke a verse: "Yunmen’s 'Seventh Day,' Xuefeng’s 'Rolling the Ball,' white artemisia and red smartweed, the bright moon and a solitary boat.
Tian nodded in approval. He ascended the hall and, citing the occasion when his ancestral teacher Baiyun opened the hall and offered incense, said:
"Among you are fellow practitioners of the robe and bowl who have benefited me with even a single word or half-verse; together we shall extend our gratitude. As for this mountain monk..."
Having just settled for two or three years, an old friend has come from afar to offer his congratulations. This is no mere matter of a few words or phrases;

how could there not be a bit of incense to serve as an offering? To burn *fengxiang* (maple incense) is to engage with the realm of Bodhi; to burn *huangshu* (yellow-ripe incense) is to speak of the Buddhas and the Patriarchs.
Now, lighting this single burner fiercely and brightly, I also wish for everyone throughout the entire world to know that it is from Zhejiang.
This place is the site of Chuanyuandao in Jiaxing Prefecture within the Western Circuit. Now tell me, what kind of incense is being burned?
After a long silence, he said: "It does not descend from the pavilion.
Chan Master Xuewu Ke of Zhongzhu, Hangzhou, ascended the hall and said: "Withered mulberry trees know the wind of heaven; the sea knows the tide of heaven."
"Cold! But tell me, what does this patch-robed monk know? He knows that rice is made from grain.

Even if you were to understand it thus, there will come a day when Old King Yama demands payment for the meal. The Master, seeing that the Song dynasty had already fallen, resigned from his monastic duties.
Chan Master Mo’an Jue of Jinshan was well-acquainted with the Master and held his spiritual conduct in high esteem. At that time, the Yuan troops were descending upon Jiangnan.

Anmen was coerced by General Bayan into staying within his tent. They traveled together to Wulin, where Anmen spoke to Bayan on behalf of the Master, requesting that he be invited to ascend to the abbacy of Lingyin.
Anmen personally carried the letter of invitation and knocked at the Master’s door. The Master pulled back the bolt and revealed half his face, asking, "Who are you?
Anmen replied, "I am an old acquaintance of yours, such-and-such. The Master dropped the bolt and said:
"I do not know you. For although Master Gai lived beyond the secular world, he maintained himself through loyalty and integrity;

thus, he did not deign to accept the summons from Lingyin. Later, Chan Master Duanjiang En praised him, saying: "Forty years have passed since the Snow Hut is no more, yet his lofty wind remains as it was.
When Prime Minister Buyan bowed at his bedside, he refused to come to Cold Spring for his sake."
The Night Session of Chan Master Xiangchuan Rugong of Yuyang, Mingzhou, Successor of Chan Master Lianzhao Riti of Tiantong: "The Shaoshi [Patriarch’s] abode has no gates;

it is as if one can pass through with ease. Standing patiently through the deep night, listen as I speak of east and west. Baoning Moku called to the assembly regarding this karmic cause, saying: "There is expedient means here, and there is also..."
"It is indeed so. There is illumination, and there is function; it is simply that you must not understand it in such a way. Take care!
Master Xing Gong of Shilin at Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: A monk asked an ancient worthy, "What is the eye for reading sutras?
The ancient worthy held up his fist. The Master said: "If you call this the eye for reading sutras, it is still just a fist."
"Head. He called it a "fist," yet it is also the eye for reading the scriptures. When one arrives at this point, what is to be done? Zisu addressed the assembly, saying:

"Where it is difficult to distinguish between 'back' and 'touch,' and when the light of discernment is lost before the pivot of action, even empty space is pierced through—how could it stop at rotten cowhide?

(Zhuyun said: "The former master not only lost his eye for reading the scriptures, but moreover did not recognize the fist; instead, he gave rise to arbitrary interpretations within empty space. But tell me, how would Ciyun have handled it? Liang...")
Jiurui said: "The palm leaves unfold the Flower Treasury World; ten thousand acres of spiritual sprouts, their conditions turning like clouds. Entering the hall, he said:

"The mountain is still, the bees' legs grow heavy as they attend to the flowers; the forest is empty, the bamboo shoots reveal their bright flesh within their sheaths. Leaning on the railing, one unconsciously becomes dazed, until a yellow oriole calls out once more.
If Sike had spoken thus, he would have deserved thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because he would not have been fit to follow after sounds or pursue forms. Entering the hall...
The Hall. In this watery land, the waters are vast and the ground is mostly damp. In the sixth month, the flower mosquitoes have mouths like iron;
rising at midnight, they leave one utterly vexed. Utterly vexed—what is to be done? There is a fan by the bedside; for no reason, it has snapped again.
Chan Master Xuzhou Pudu of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou was a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Huazang Tong. He was a native of Jiangdu in Weiyang and surnamed Shi.

Having left the household life, he traveled extensively to visit various masters without attaining realization. When he was asked, "Who is it that does not act as a companion to the myriad dharmas? the Master replied, "Gold."
Below the incense burner was an iron *Kunlun*. [The Master] said, "I thought this short fellow had some merit; it turns out his understanding is only like this.
The Master bowed deeply and paid homage, saying, "Thank you, Preceptor, for your witness. Later, after taking up residence, he ascended the hall and said:
"When a false man speaks the True Dharma, the True Dharma is entirely false. When a true man speaks false dharma, the false dharma is entirely true. He then struck the meditation staff once.
The Master said, "Is it wrong? Is it right? He then struck his staff once and said, "Do you speak? Do you not speak?
"If one can discern and distinguish within this very point, then even a house made of gold is not considered noble; what glory is there in jade food and brocade robes? He then ascended the hall.

The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are but the awakening of one’s own nature. Originally, there is no person who is deluded or awakened; it simply requires realization today.
Since there is no person who is deluded or awakened, what is there to realize? [He] struck the meditation pillar once and said: "A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them;

they are followed by the warbling oriole as it flies over the low wall. In the year Dingshou of the Zhizhi era (1277), he was commissioned to Mount Jing; this was written during the aftermath of a fire. Volition.

It appeared that his restoration of the Dharma was about to reach its fruition. Suddenly, manifesting a slight ailment, he requested a brush and wrote in large characters: "Eighty-two years, I have steered the bottomless boat;
now I turn it over and return, with the bright moon filling the sky. Having cast down the brush, he passed away.

Chan Master Jue’an Zhen of Chengtian Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xuedou Qian. A Dharma Master from Huazang Monastery, acting under imperial command, was about to establish a lecture hall for doctrinal exegesis.
The Master said, "If you can preach Chan, I will follow your lead and change [the schedule]. If I cannot preach the teachings, you must change [your plan]."

"I shall follow you. Thereupon, he beat the drum and ascended the hall. Entering the five teachings with a single shout, he revealed the core of our school—the one cap worn upon the crowns of a thousand sages.
The lecturer wept as he prostrated twice, begging for repentance before withdrawing.
Chan Master Xutang Zhiyu of Jing Mountain in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Daochangyan. He was a native of Siming. Once, he ascended the hall and said:
"If words are sufficient, one speaks all day long yet never exhausts the Way. If words are insufficient, one speaks all day long yet only exhausts phenomena. Now, tell me, what is the Way?"
All things are either one or two. If you say they are one, why is the guest mountain high and the host mountain low?

If you say they are two, why does [the Zhuangzi] say that "heaven and earth are but a single finger" and "all things are but a single horse"? If you can distinguish the black from the white within this, I will return your money for the straw sandals.
Otherwise, I simply wish that next year’s silkworms and wheat may ripen, so that Rāhula’s child may receive a single coin.

When the Master was first residing at Jingci Monastery, an imperial messenger delivered an edict asking: "Zhaozhou traveled on pilgrimage at eighty years of age; why did Xutang remain a mountain dweller for eighty years?
The Master cited Zhaozhou’s verse on the story of his pilgrimage to Linji: "Zhaozhou only set out on pilgrimage at eighty; Xutang again took up residence on the mountain at eighty.
There is another pivot that expands the Buddhas and Patriarchs. [The Emperor] bestowed upon him the title "Ninefold [Patriarch]."

The Emperor was moved within his palace; he had the verse presented back to him in response, and the Sovereign was greatly pleased. He specially bestowed five hundred *shí* of rice and one hundred rolls of silk.
Those who resided at Yewang and Jingshan were likewise granted generous rewards. Within the hall, he uttered these words of instruction:
"Why do those whose own eyes are not yet clear take empty space to wear as trousers? Why do those who draw lines on the ground to create a prison [act thus]?"
Those who have truly penetrated this do not merely pass through. Why does one enter the sea to count the grains of sand, yet stand on tiptoe upon the point of a needle?
Chan Master Shifan Yan of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou offered a verse on the karmic occasion of Mazu Daian expelling his head seat:

"A single string of *maṇi* jewels, confronting you directly at the opportune moment. It deceived the head seat to death; it left Moliya (Changli) in doubt to death. He exhausted all these depths of poverty."
Artifice. From the beginning, he never knew the *Chunqiu*.
Chan Master Shixi Xin Yue of Jingshan in Lin’an Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Kai of Jinshan; he was a native of Meizhou. A monk asked: "What is the Buddha?"
The Master said, "A short man watching a play.
Chan Master Jingci Jianweng Jing of Hangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Zhongxue Chong of Mount Jing, cited the case where Guishan asked Yangshan: "I am with you all day long..."
"What kind of matter have you settled by this deliberation? [Baizhang] drew a line in the air. Muzhou said, "If it had not been for me, you would have surely been deluded by him.
The Master offered this verse: "Though father and son are close, they deliberate together; How could one believe there are swords and spears within the breast?
Had that single stroke cut through then, The entanglements throughout the world would never have arisen again."
Chan Master Beishan Long of the Northern Mountains composed a verse on Niaoke’s blowing of a tuft of cloth: An eighty-year-old elder must practice with vigor;
The blowing of the cloth-tuft brings forth renewed calamity. A man who sheds blood for three thousand li— An old monk upon the branch of a withered tree.
Chan Master Gaofeng Yuanmiao of West Tianmu Peak in Hangzhou,
a successor in the twenty-first generation under National Teacher Yangshan Qian of the Southern Peak (Nanyue), was the son of the Xu family of Wujiang, Suzhou. At fifteen, he...
He left home to become a monk and first visited Duanqiao at Weishui Mimi Temple. Next, he went to see Xueyan at Beijian, carrying incense to seek instruction.
As soon as he offered his greetings, Xueyan struck him out. Thereafter, whenever anyone entered the gate, Xueyan would immediately ask, "Who brought this corpse for you to drag here?
Before the sound of the question had even faded, he would strike them out. One day, he beheld a portrait eulogy (zhentan) of Master Wuzu Yan, which said:
In a hundred years, there are thirty-six thousand mornings; turning back and over again, it is originally this very man.
Suddenly, he broke through the doubt regarding the "corpse. When Xueyan was residing at Nanming, the Master went there to visit him.
Xueyan asked, "Who dragged a corpse here for you? The Master gave a shout. Xueyan raised his staff; the Master seized it and said, "Today, you shall strike me!"
"No," [Zhaozhou] replied. Yankou asked, "Why can you not strike him? The Master shook his sleeves and departed.

One day, Yankou asked, "When you are bustling about during the day, can you maintain mastery over yourself? The Master said, "I can maintain mastery. [Yankou] asked, "Can you maintain mastery within the dream?"
The Master said, "You have attained mastery. Yuan asked, "When one is fast asleep, without dreams, without thoughts, without seeing, and without hearing, where is the master?
The Master was speechless. Yuan instructed him, saying, "From this day forward, you need not study the Buddha or the Dharma.
You need not investigate the past or the present. Simply eat when hungry and sleep when tired. As soon as—"
Upon waking from sleep, he shook off his lethargy and thought: "Where, after all, does this master of one awakening reside and establish his life?
The Master then resolved to enter Longxu. After five years had passed, while a monk was pushing a pillow that fell to the floor and made a sound, the Master attained great enlightenment.
At that time, a monk named Ruoqiong contracted an illness; the Master attended to him with great devotion and inspired him. [The monk] recovered from his illness.
He urgently sought a bath. Upon seeing his reflection in the hot water, he attained realization. He spoke a verse: "Thirty-six years of inversion; today, one great laugh.
The nostrils born of mother are wide open, releasing a featherless iron hawk.
The Master asked, "What are the nostrils born of mother? Jing held up his writing brush. The Master said, "And what do you call this 'featherless iron hawk'? Jing... [remained silent].
He cast aside his writing brush and passed away. Subsequently, he moved to Shuangji. In the spring of the Jīmūta year (1279) of the Deyou era, he entered Lion Rock at the Western Tianmu Mountains.
There, he fashioned a small chamber about one *zhang* square within a stone cave and inscribed it: "The Cave of the Death Barrier; it cannot be ascended without a ladder.

He removed the ladder to sever all attachments, so that even his disciples rarely had the opportunity to behold him. Instead, he left behind the discourse on the Three Barriers to test practitioners, saying: "The Great..."

If one has fundamentally realized the human essence and is liberated from birth and death, why does the life-root (*jīvitendriya*) not yet cease? The public cases (*gong'an*) of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are but a single principle;
why then are there those who understand and those who do not? A great practitioner of the Way should follow the conduct of the Buddha; why then do they fail to observe the *vinaya*?
When a response does not accord with the truth, the gate is closed and no further instruction is given. Thus it was sent by Xueyan in the Dingwei year of the Zhiyuan era.
The bamboo whisk and the verse say: "The Great Master is now gone; Xueyan knows the proper etiquette.
His empty fame fills the universe; I entrust it to Attendant Yuanmiao. When the assembly requested him to open the hall, he proceeded to the Stone Room and offered incense, saying:
"This single offering of incense does not depend on the sun and moon within a flask, nor is it the spring breeze beyond the kalpas. Several times..."
His father met a poisoned hand; he attained a state of eight-sided brilliance. Now, when he lets go, the earth shakes with six quakes;
when he brings it forth, it fills and pierces through empty space. But tell me, what about that one phrase where he neither brings it forth nor lets go?
He gives a shout and performs a woman’s bow, then burns [the incense] in the brazier as an offering to the former abbot of Yangshan, who wore horns and shed hair.
The old monk from beneath his nostrils, wishing to repay the grace of the Dharma-milk, then took his seat.
A monk asked, "What is the assembly where the ten directions gather together? The Master said, "Dragons and snakes are intermingled; ordinary people and sages meet.

The monk asked, "What is it that each and every one studies as non-action? The Master said, "His mouth swallows Buddhas and patriarchs; his eyes cover heaven and earth. The monk asked, "What is the selection of the Buddha?"
[The Master] said, "Ten thousand miles east and west, eight thousand miles south and north. [A monk] asked, "What is it like to return with one's heart empty after passing the imperial examination?
The Master said, "A movement of the countenance reveals the ancient path; do not fall into the trap of silent stillness.

The monk said, "If that is so, then every word reveals the ultimate truth, and every sentence points toward the source. The Master said, "Where have you seen this? The monk gave a shout. The Master said, "This too is like striking with a staff in the dark."
Yue said, "Just as the West Peak has gathered from the ten directions today to open this field for selecting Buddhas, what auspicious signs are there ultimately?
The Master replied, "The mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the myriad phenomena—sentient and insentient alike—all attain Buddhahood."

The monk asked, "Since all have already attained Buddhahood, why is it that students do not become Buddhas? The Master said, "If you were to become a Buddha, how could you cause the entire earth to become a Buddha?
The monk asked, "Ultimately, where does the student's fault lie? The Master said, "South of Xiang and north of Tan.
The monk asked, "Do you permit the student to repent? The Master said, "Prostrate yourself. The monk prostrated himself. The Master—
It is said: "A lion bites a man; a hound chases a clod. Entering the hall, he took up his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "Do you see?
Everyone has eyes in their sockets; unless one is blind, they certainly see.
He struck the ground once with the staff and said, "Do you hear? Every person has an opening in their ears; unless one is dead, they certainly hear. Since...
"Seeing and hearing—what exactly are these? [He strikes with his staff. "Let seeing and hearing cease for a moment.

Just as it was before the six sense organs were fully formed, and before sounds and forms had appeared—at that time of hearing what has not yet been heard and seeing what has not yet been seen—when it is precisely thus, by what ultimately do you verify it?
[He strikes with his staff. "I now guarantee this matter for you."
"It shall never be in vain. He strikes the ground with his staff. "After thirty years, you must strictly refrain from leaking any news.
Leaning on his staff, he descends from the seat. He presents the Dharma-robe for the assembly. It is woven from Shu brocade, cut from Wu silk;

draped like white jade, interspersed with gold. When forged into a single whole, even a needle cannot pierce it. At the points where the patterns interlock, the seams are difficult to find. Although...
However, Xifeng took the emptiness of all phenomena as his seat. Pointing with his staff at the robe, he asked, "Does it still fit this?
Leaning on his staff, he said: "The fragrance of heaven disperses upon the moss-covered stones; the five-petaled flower blooms in the campaka grove."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Outside the gate is a person who exhausts every stratagem to enter, yet cannot enter.
Inside the gate is a person who employs every skillful means to exit, yet cannot exit. Setting aside for a moment this inability to enter or exit, tell me:
when the person outside the gate and the person inside the gate meet, what is it like? 'Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful.'"
"To speak of it to one already sorrowful is to kill them with grief. He took leave of the assembly. "For thirty years on West Peak, I have recklessly preached Prajñā; my offenses fill the heavens.
At the end, there is but one phrase that I dare not burden the common people with; I shall take it upon myself alone. "Does the assembly know where this falls? After a long silence, he said:
"A difference of a hair’s breadth, and heaven and earth are set apart. He then wrote a verse, which begins: "Coming..."
He did not enter the Deadman’s Barrier; he departed without leaving the Deadman’s Barrier. A black iron snake drills into the sea of men, toppling Mount Sumeru.
He passed away peacefully. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the Deadman’s Barrier. He was fifty-eight years of age and forty-three years since his ordination.
Chan Master Chiding of Iron Ox at Lingyun in Hengzhou was the son of Wang of Taihe in Jixian.
At the age of thirty-one, he went to visit Chan Master Ken’an Qin and shaved his hair. He subsequently relied upon Xueyan at the fodder shed to practice the dhūta austerities.
Xueyan addressed the assembly, saying: "Brothers, when you apply yourselves to the practice of *kung-fu*, if for seven days and nights your single thought is uninterrupted—"
"Do not engage in mutual disparagement; there is no place for entry. Take this old monk’s head to serve as a dung-scoop. The Master silently understood his meaning.
Before long, he fell ill. He then took a wash-tub, went to a secluded spot, and sat upright upon it, maintaining single-minded right mindfulness with his eyes never closing for a moment.
After seven days and nights had passed and were nearly half over, he suddenly perceived that the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the grasses, trees, and thickets...
The forest pervaded the world like snow. The sky was bright, and beneath the sun, he stood alone and majestic, such that heaven and earth could not contain him.

After a long while, as if hearing the sound of wood being struck, he was startled into realization; sweat flowed from his entire body and his illness was cured. He leaped for joy, celebrating incessantly.
Early the next morning, he went to the Abbot’s quarters to relate this to Master Yan. Yan presented him with a *gong'an* to interrogate him, and his responses were unhindered. Furthermore—
He presented a verse, saying: "What is this 'bright and clear, numinous and intelligent'? By the time you blink your eyes, it has already been missed. The tally-stick by the latrine emits light;
look directly, and you will see that it has always been none other than myself. In the Wuyin year of the Zhiyuan era, he ordained him as a monk and bestowed the robe upon him.
The verse says: "This robe of the field of merit, free from marks, I now bestow upon you. After awakening to the clarity of the mind-ground, It will be like a dragon shedding sweet rain.
Furthermore, for six years he did not even let his side touch the mat. One day, while in the hall atop a cliff, he raised the question:
"When a deceased monk has died and been cremated, where does he go? He provided his own answer: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—these fully reveal the body of the Dharma King."

He immediately went to the abbot’s quarters and said, "Just now, when the Master expounded upon Prajñā, the stone lion in front of the Dharma Hall was so startled that it began to laugh and dance without ceasing.
Yunyan said, "Try to say something about it. The Master replied, "When spring returns beyond the kalpas, all things are withered;
mountains, rivers, and the great earth are not a single speck of dust. How can one speak of the Dharmakāya’s transcendence? It makes the blue-eyed barbarian of the Western Heaven fall over laughing."
Yanguan struck the table before him and said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—there is not a single speck of dust. What is this? The Master made a gesture as if overturning it.
Yanguan laughed and said, "One win, two wins. When the Master entered the room for private instruction, Yanguan asked, "Bring forth a single phrase regarding the point of intimacy.
The Master said, "I will not speak. Yanguan asked, "Why will you not speak? The Master picked up the object in his hand.
Xianghezi said, "This fellow has obtained something that isn't worth half a penny. Yan said, "A talkative fellow.

On another occasion while making a tour of the hall, the Master was sleeping with his body wrapped in a paper quilt. Yan summoned him to the abbot’s quarters and said in a stern voice, "I am touring the hall and you are fast asleep!
If you can speak a word, I will let you off; if you cannot, I will drive you down the mountain. The Master followed [Yan].
He replied: "The iron ox has no strength and is too lazy to plow the fields; with its rope and plow, it sleeps amidst the snow. The great earth and white clouds completely cover all;
there is nowhere for Deshan to lay his golden whip. Yanyuan said, "What a fine iron ox! Consequently, he took this as his title.
Later, while residing at Lingyun, he propagated the Way of Xueyan. In the winter of the Great Virtue *Ren-yin* year, he wrote this long verse and presented it.
The assembly gathered. At the end [of his discourse], he said: "This mundane world is not enduring; it is worn away day by day and month by month.

After thirty years, a single branch shall emerge from the current of the Peach Blossom Spring. A holeless flute shall be blown to sing the song of Great Peace. He was about to pass away the following spring.
When an attendant monk requested words of parting for the assembly, the Master said, "I have long since departed. Then, sitting serenely, he passed away.
When Chan Master Xinfan of Mount Daochang in Anjì Prefecture first established himself at Jianyang, Shiwu of Xifeng went to visit him.

The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Tianmu. The Master asked, "What instruction did you receive there? He replied, "'The myriad dharmas return to the One. The Master asked, "How do you understand this?
Shiwu was speechless. The Master said, "This is a dead word. What kind of person with a feverish illness would say such a thing?"
The Master taught him thus: "When there is a Buddha, do not dwell; where there is no Buddha, run swiftly past. Wuyi asked, "What is the meaning of this?
His answer did not accord with the Master's intent. The Master said, "This too is a dead word. Unaware of his own state, Wuyi broke into a cold sweat.
Later, when he entered the room, the Master again questioned him on the previous conversation. Wuyi replied, "One sees the road while mounting the horse. The Master [affirmed].
He rebuked him, saying, "To remain here for six years and still harbor such a view! The monk became indignant and left.

While on the road, he suddenly raised his head and, upon seeing a pavilion in the open air, attained enlightenment. Returning to the master, he said, "To not dwell where there is a Buddha is a dead word;
to rush past where there is no Buddha is also a dead word. Today I have understood."
"The living phrase has been understood. The Master asked, "How do you understand it? Wuyi said, "On the Qingming festival, the rain has just cleared;
the yellow oriole speaks clearly upon the branch. The Master nodded in approval.
Chan Master Wujikyuan of Kuangshan once received an injunction from Xueyan, who said, "Your merit is thin; it is not fitting for you to enter the world to save others.
He subsequently retired to live in seclusion on Mount Kuanglu. Having reached the age of one hundred, he sat alone in a thatched hut, remaining silent throughout the day.

Tianzhen had previously sought instruction from the Master but received no inspiration. Later, while encountering the Master in the latrine, Tianzhen hurried forward and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! At these words, Tianzhen was suddenly enlightened and attained release.

He merely waved his hand. The Master said, "Have you attained something? Zhen shook out his sleeves and left. He subsequently served [the Master] diligently for over a month, and day by day he became increasingly profound and subtle.
Chan Master Fangshan Bao of Ruishan in Taizhou, a successor of Chan Master Lun of Jingci, bestowed this verse upon Wujian: "This mind is utterly vast;
even empty space cannot be compared to it. This Way is exactly like this: receive its service and rest, ceasing all seeking outside."
Chan Master Juexiangjian’s verse on the occasion of Dongshan’s “The Path Does Not Exist” states: Dongshan has a path leading through Yunyan;
Where the way is severed, it is difficult for one to reach it. When the living road opens at the tip of the staff, Only then will you know there is not a hair’s breadth of separation.
Chan Master Zhuyu Jian composed a verse on Drum Mountain’s “Holy Arrow,” which says: "The young lad double-reins his jade steed as it neighs; A pale white spring robe is encircled by a green sash.
Returning at midnight beneath the flowers and the moon, The golden whip strikes down a flight of scattered crimson petals.
It further says: "Within the nine-layered city, it is not distant at all; Each arrow shot through successive layers is more than enough. Suddenly encountering the siege of the three armies..."
At the place of circumambulation, there is clearly a path leading straight to the heavens.

Regarding the verse by Chan Master Yueting Zhong, a successor of Chan Master Wuxue Yuan, on Mahākāśyapa’s expulsion of Mañjuśrī: "The young master in brocade robes is accustomed to wandering through the spring. White...
The foremost among the beautiful suffer much regret. Even the wealthy still lament that their households are too small. As for the poor, there is no help for it; what can one do with a single body?
Shuzhong Shan, Chan Master Zhuyuan Dao of Mount Zituo in Taizhou, a successor of Chan Master Yongyue Huiyong, once asked about the "Vzhou’s Dog" kōan. He was about to—
The Master opened his mouth. Zhong let out a shout and attained great enlightenment. He presented a verse, saying: "The dog has no Buddha-nature; spring colors fill the imperial capital.
Inside Zhaozhou’s East Monastery, a gourd hangs upon the wall. The Master then burst into laughter and said, "How can you understand it like this?
Zhong shook his sleeves and departed.
At the age of thirteen, Chan Master Gulin Qingmao of Baoning in Jinling became a monk.

Upon seeing an elder master cite the case of Gaoyuan who, when a monk failed to understand him, would seize him and say: "Your parents gave you this body; your teachers and friends have fulfilled your aspirations.

You are not pressed by hunger or cold, nor burdened by the toil of conscription. If you do not at this time resolutely apply yourself with diligence to accomplish the work of the Way," [he would continue to press the point].
"What face will you have to show your parents, teachers, and friends on another day? Upon hearing this, the Master could not help but shed tears.
He then knew there was one who could see beyond birth and death, and so he went to attend upon a virtuous teacher (*kalyāṇamitra*).
Thereupon, he set aside his body and mind, and for twenty years he applied himself with tireless diligence, never ceasing for even a moment. Later, he arrived at the assembly of Yuyewa Temple.
Those who have a slight understanding of the purity of touch have now attained this thorough realization. He resided at various monasteries, including Kaiyuan, Yongfu, and Baoning.
During the summer retreat, he gave a small-scale sermon upon recovering from illness: "The passage of years and months cannot be toyed with; old age and sickness do not wait for anyone.

For the past ten days or so, I have been beset by alternating chills and fevers; I sought the source of their arising but could not find it. Why? Because the physical form has detached from the mind."
Because it is like an illusion, once the physical form has departed, the mind is likewise like an illusion. The nature of the Buddha’s illness and the Patriarchs’ illnesses is also thus.
As the Fifth Patriarch, the Venerable Master, said: "When illness comes, it clings to skin and bone; Shake it off, and not a single thing remains.
He cannot take a step when walking, his voice is low; Yet his nostrils remain, still prominent. The Elder of the Fifth Patriarch spoke these words in such a manner.

One can only suffer from one's own illness but cannot cause others to be ill. Since one cannot cause others to be ill, when the time comes that one cannot gather [the illness] together, one will be unable to universally enter into the bodies of sentient beings to fully manifest their illnesses.

Since one cannot fully manifest the illnesses of sentient beings, the karmic consciousness will remain vast and indistinct, with no fundamental basis to rely upon. Great Assembly, for ninety days, let us abide together in this state of peace.
Dwell in stillness; whether moving or at rest, in cold or heat, you must naturally preserve and cherish yourself. A Small Session for the End of the Summer Retreat:
Time is easily lost, yet now the summer retreat has come to its close. By the steps, crickets chirp; among the trees, cicadas cry. The golden wind fans the wilds as yellow leaves drift down.
Within this very seeing and hearing, there is nothing else. Thus, throughout these ninety days, not a single thread of effort shall be wasted. Through kalpas...
Ignorance is instantly melted away and shattered; yet there is still more beyond this. To reveal the lion’s claws and fangs, there is a further deliberation within that state.
One cannot avoid brandishing a sword at the gate. Thus the ancients said: "It is like a wild goose flying across the vast sky, its reflection sinking into the cold water.
The goose has no intention of leaving a trace, and the water has no lingering reflection. It is simply this.
This numinous blade—whom would dare to compare with it? Beneath the Gate of the Great Sun, every day is like the third autumn month.

If you all can investigate and examine this well, you will surely achieve the fruit and fulfill the merit. At such a time as this, how is it? All myriad functions have ceased; the tortoise hides its six limbs.
The single nature is perfectly luminous; the crane emerges from its cage.

This is the verse by Chan Master Dongyu Dehai of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Gong of Jingci Monastery, on the theme of “Juzhi Raising His Finger”: "Profoundly deep and bottomless."
So lofty as to be beyond reach; the more one contemplates it, the further it recedes; the more one seeks it, the more difficult it becomes to find.
Chan Master Zhuyun Jingtan of Tianning Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture was the son of the Yan family of Pujiang, Wuzhou. When he grew up, he studied the impermanence of worldly things.
The Master [Jingtan] presented himself at the feet of Shilin Ma, surrendering his heart and requesting the Dharma. Shilin showed him, saying: "The wondrous function of the Buddha."
In all matters you encounter, do not be deluded. Upon hearing a single word from the Master, you attained awakening. You first resided at Zhiping in Wuzhou and then at Beichen in Suzhou.
A monk asked, "The various dharmas have already been heard today; I pray that you will now proclaim the intent of the Patriarch who came from the West.
The Master said, "The one who came from the West has no intent to proclaim. The monk asked, "Then what did Bodhidharma transmit? The Master said, "Nine years of facing the wall—how shameful!"
[The monk] was terrified and asked, "If that is so, then the Buddha-dharma pervades the world, yet the mouth that speaks of the profound remains closed.
The Master said, "Above all, do not mistake a bell for a water jar. A monk asked, "The ancients said one must study the 'living word' and not the 'dead word.
What is the living word? The Master said, "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it down. The monk asked, "What is the dead word? The Master said—
"Carrying it back home in a bottomless basket. He asked, "What about the phrase 'neither living nor dead'?
The Master said, "It is easy to distinguish flour from snow, but difficult to discern soot within ink. He asked, "The Three Sages have not yet attained it, and the Ten Saints find it hard to know;
what is this school? The Master said, "A holeless flute and felt clappers. He asked, "Who is the one who knows this? The Master said, "A deaf man."
"How could one possibly hear it? [The student] said, "I know that the Master is accustomed to this kind of pivot. The Master said, "A hawk flies over Silla.
[The student] asked, "What is the mind of nirvana? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru. [The student] asked, "What is discriminating wisdom? The Master said, "The four great oceans.
[The student] said, "In the end, these do not suffice at all. The Master said, "The Vajra King’s precious sword—can you wield it yet?"

[The Master] asked, “Can it be attained? [The monk] replied, “I beg the Master to cast his eyes high. The Master said, “You have split the conversation into two parts. [Zhuo] resided at Ciyun Zhaokong Temple on Mount Yu.

Purity. Merely seeing objects appear before one constitutes four propositions; yet you imagine yourself to be a person of great realization. With a quick mouth and fluent tongue, you have wasted a lifetime.

Chan Master Shaodai of Baolin on Yellow Mountain in Yunhuang, Jinhua Prefecture, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Ling of Jingshan. His family had long resided in Tongjiang, Yan.

His surname was Wu. He first ascended Mount Shuangjing to pay his respects to Xugu, from whom he received the essence of the single transmission. After a long time, he took his leave and traveled to consult various renowned masters.
He then remarked, "From this day forward, I know that the Dharma has no differing flavors. He returned once more to Mount Jing. At that time, Dongyu Hai was propagating the Way at Jingci Monastery;

Yan resided at Wulong; later, he moved to Baolin. One day, as he was about to pass away, the assembly requested that he write a verse.

Chan Master Zhuyuan Zhengyuan of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was the son of the Ouyang clan of Nankang.

Chan Master Jueyin Bencheng of Suzhou was a native of Yuxi in Jiahe. Initially, he followed Hu Shitang as his teacher.

Zen Master Gao Feng Wuxue was a successor of the Japanese National Teacher Musō Soseki of Tōsotsu-in. His secular surname was Minamoto; he was a native of Settsu Province. He was born during the reign of Emperor Uda.

At the age of eighteen, he became a monk; in a dream, he traveled to the two monasteries of Shushan and Shitou in China, where he encountered a man with a long, bushy beard.

The Chan Master Nantang Qingyu of Benjue Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture,

Thus, when the clouds part and the sun emerges, one’s function reaches its full majesty. Striking the mark of true substance, you practitioners are like the people of Sizhou meeting the Great Sage.
In the first year of the Yuantong era, while residing at Benjue Monastery, he ascended the hall and, looking over the assembly, said: "This..."
