The Master said, "If you detest the mundane and crave the sacred, you sever the roots of goodness of Prajñā.
If you sweep away delusion to seek the truth, you cut off the life-vein of all Buddhas. He raised his voice and shouted again: "Who is the real? Who is the deluded?
Who is the mundane? Who is the sacred? At these words, his mind suddenly opened wide in clarity.
Chan Master Shanjian of Guting was a native of Kunming in Yunnan. He took up the koan, "Where does it all return?
One day, while in meditative concentration, he heard a monk say, "To see nothing is true seeing. At these words, the Master experienced a sudden liberation.
In the year Yichou of the Zhengtong era, he went to Long'en to see Wujie. Wujie said, "It seems you have personally realized the place where you previously applied your practice."
One recitation. When the Master finished his formal offering and reached the point of "seeing the Truth," he joined his palms and remained silent.
Zhi said, "How is it that your realization of the Truth differs from mine? The Master spread both hands wide and said, "This is nothing other than that.
Zhi asked, "Does this still involve words and phrases? The Master replied, "In truth, there is not a single word. Zhi said, "Right here, in this state where there is not a single word—"
"I have finished providing testimony for you. The Master bowed and took his leave. Wujie asked, "Where will you go?
The Master replied, "I shall go to the crossroads to shout at the Buddhas and revile the Patriarchs. Wujie asked, "Will you come back?

The Master said, "I shall not fail to honor the countenance of the Master," and departed directly. He settled at Mount Dayong on Jintai, where disciples from all quarters gathered without ceasing. There was no end to them.
Fearing that he would leave the world too early, [Zhaojue] appointed him as the head seat (shouzuo). He asked, "Where else do you dwell?
The Master said, "In a place where the Buddhas and Patriarchs have not traveled. Zhaojue asked, "Is it permissible for others to come there? The Master said, "It is open and unobstructed.
Zhaojue asked, "Among the ancients of old, who possessed wisdom that transcends the patriarchs? The Master said, "Huangbo. Zhaojue asked, "Have you seen Huangbo?"
The Master said, "Even if it were Huangbo himself, he would still have to be expelled. Ji said, "How dare you speak such grand words here in my presence?
The Master said, "The True Eye is without partiality. Ji said, "Observing your understanding and views, I am not your teacher.
The Master said, "If one has no capacity exceeding the ordinary, how could one avoid being diminished and stripped away? Ji said, "So it is, so it is."
The Universal Sermon for Opening the Hall by Chan Master Foji Yigan Zhen, Dharma Heir of the Great Being Tian Su’an, says: "Layer upon layer of green mountains; flowing and surging green waters."
Attaining realization within this very assembly, one walks alone, transcending all. Even so, it is but ordinary tea and rice. An ancient worthy said:
"If you wish to exhaust the view across a thousand li, climb yet another story. Following the words of the ancients: "If the pivot does not leave its station, one falls into a sea of poison;
if speech does not startle the multitude, one sinks into common custom. If, amidst the spark struck from flint, one can distinguish the black from the white, then—flash!
To discern killing and giving life amidst a flash of lightning is to cut off all manifold distinctions and stand like a sheer cliff ten thousand fathoms high.

Do you know if there is such a time? You have already misjudged and ruined it. Nowadays, those who discuss Chan have their heels planted firmly on the ground and their nostrils reaching toward the heavens;
yet those who possess the true eye are as rare as stars scattered across the sky. Consequently, the views of partiality and correctness are not unified, and each establishes its own eccentricity.

Stubbornly clinging to one's own interpretations, one fails to penetrate the true principle. As it is said: "The True Dharma is difficult to uphold; false dharmas arise in competition. An ancient remarked:
"If there is ten parts of faith, there will be ten parts of doubt; if there is ten parts of doubt, there will be ten parts of awakening.

You may take all that you have seen with your eyes and heard with your ears throughout your entire life—your various understandings and observations, your extraordinary words and wondrous phrases, and your views on the Way of Chan.
Regarding the Buddha-Dharma, completely cast off all pride, conceit, and the like, leaving not even a trace behind. Focus solely upon a koan that you have not yet understood or resolved;
plant your feet firmly, straighten your backbone, and practice day and night. Where there is no place for inquiry, inquire;

where there is no doubt, doubt. Proceed until you reach a state where east and west cannot be distinguished and north and south are no longer discerned, remaining in a state of total, dazed stillness.
It is like a living corpse with breath; the mind transforms according to objects, yet when touched, it still knows.
If one shatters the skull, realization is not obtained from another—how joyful this would be for one’s entire life!

Sù (cut by 曹; same as 繅: to unwind the silk from the cocoon). Lài (cut by 洛代; to bestow). Qióng (cut by 渠營; red jade). Qù (cut by 得案; a small house). Xī (pronounced shén zhì; to bestow; also:

to walk, stand, or call out to change a name). Shǐ (cut by 上紙; to take things with the tongue). Dēng (cut by 抽庚; a type of cauldron with handles and feet). Yì (cut by 一入; fragrance permeating the clothing).

Dian (zhāng xiàn qiè; to dip an object into water). Huo (hù gǔ qiè; phonetic value hú. The character for "yǒng" is correctly written as zhì [zhì tú nǜ qiè; phonetic value tū]. It denotes an appearance of non-discrimination).
Li (lì dì qiè; li is the same as lín). Qióng (qú yíng qiè; qióng). Chān (chū jiǎn qiè; the light of the sun shining). Zhí (zhí jué qiè; to strike).

Chan Master Dongming Haizhou Puci was a successor of Chan Master Dongming Xian.
A native of the Qian clan of Changshu, Suzhou, he left the household life at Mount Poshan.
While listening to lectures on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he reached the passage, "There are only words and explanations; there is no real meaning," and harbored a doubt. He went to consult Master Wan.

Dongshan raised the previous conversation and bowed twice, requesting instruction. Dongshan immediately struck him twice on the head, pushed him back with a shove, and kicked him twice with his feet, saying, "This very thing is the true meaning.
The Master rose and said, "Excellent, excellent! You have truly exerted your heart and mind, Master."
Feng smiled and granted his request; he then received the formal entrustment and dwelt in a mountain valley within the cave for twenty-nine years.
A monk arrived and was inspired to seek out Dongming. The Master went to see him; it happened that someone had prepared a vegetarian feast.
Upon reaching the gate, the Master asked, "What is the flavor of today’s feast? Dongming replied, "One knows it only when it reaches the mouth; to speak of it is already far removed from the truth."

The Master asked, "What is it like when the flavor reaches the mouth? Ming immediately struck out the lamp and said, "If you can recognize where the light of the lamp has gone, the flavor will reach your mouth.
The Master was speechless. The next day, he sent an attendant to invite the Master. When the Master arrived, Ming asked, "Have you seen anyone?
The Master smiled and said, "I have seen only one person; I fear it would startle people were I to speak of it. Ming— [remained silent].
[The monk] said, "Even if one were to meet Śākyamuni in person, he would still be just an ordinary fellow. What harm is there in saying so? The Master said, "Wanfeng.
[The monk] asked, "Is this to record our seniority, or to discuss the Buddha-dharma? If it is to record seniority, there are a thousand people under Wanfeng’s assembly.
If it is to discuss the Buddha-dharma, you old *jaḷi* have not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma; what is there to be startled about?"
"If you have personally seen Wanfeng, where is Wanfeng right now? The Master was at a loss. The next day, Ming said, "If that is so, when did you ever see Wanfeng?
The Master returned to his quarters and for three days and nights forgot both sleep and food. By chance, a glass lamp fell to the ground, and he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
He went to present the circumstances of his realization. Ming said, "Old *jiaoluo*, you shall be a direct successor of Wanfeng."
The Master said, "The Abbot has thoroughly enlightened me; how could I possibly succeed to Wanfeng?

Ming then laughed and, having gathered the assembly, stepped out of his retreat, ascended the seat, and transmitted the Dharma (the discourse is recorded in the *Dongming Chapter*). When Ming passed away, the Master wished to return to Dongting, but the assembly requested that he succeed to the abbacy.
On the anniversary of Wanfeng’s death, the Master offered incense and pointed to the portrait, saying: "I nearly drowned you in this jar! Fortunately..."
"This is universal compassion. If it were anyone else, they could not be saved. This incense is offered to repay the guidance [received].
He gave a shout and said, “I only laugh at you, a headless teacher who protects your own shortcomings and treats the Buddha-dharma as mere human sentiment.
He unfolded his sitting cloth and prostrated, saying, “This single offering of incense is for the Elder of Dongming; with one sincere heart, he spurred me on toward the profound cave.”

Having reached the source of the school, he gave two consecutive shouts and said: "How could a single word exhaust the Heart of Universal Compassion? For a thousand ages, descendants shall repay and praise this kindness.
This one incense offering is for the power of my former teacher’s guidance; had I not been favored by him, how could there be this day?
When you come here in the future, you will have no choice but to receive thirty blows of the staff. This is truly a way to repay that which cannot be repaid."
"Thank you. He gave a shout and said: "Where the grace received is deep, that is one's home; only when there is milk does one know it is one's mother.
Rising from his prostrations, he spoke this verse: "The source-head resides only within the shout; The Three Essentials and Three Mysteries are called Host and Guest.
The five blows must be understood by the person beneath the words; The four patterns must be clarified within the phrases. Finally, the true mechanism is the phrase of life and death."
"The secret within lies in the lineage of the teacher. To shatter my form and grind my bones is to repay the teacher’s virtue; with this profound resolve, I shall requite the Buddha’s grace.
Weeping bitterly, he returned to the abbot’s quarters. On the eve of his passing, he spoke a verse, saying: "Ninety-six years in the world, seventy-four years as a monk.
Amidst so many contradictions and errors, at one glance before Dongming, they all vanish. With his whisk, he struck [the air].
Yuanxiang said, "From Śākyamuni until my sixty-second generation, there have been countless old monks. He then drew another circle and said, "Most of them find their resting place here.
*Duh!* With these words, he set down his brush and passed away. In the first year of the Jingtai era, his entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the right of Dongming.
In the Tianjie Monastery, Chan Master Da-chan Huitong of Juefeng, a native of the Shao clan from Zhenghe in Jianning, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Zhanshi.

He left home at Mount Dou and first studied under Zhou, the Mountain Master. He then closed himself in retreat at Yan’ou Hermitage. Next, he studied under Xuegu (the account of which appears in the "Xuegu Chapter"). One.
In the evening, he had an insight and immediately spoke this verse: "Holding the axe of pure wind in hand, I split open the crown of Vairocana;
The teachings of the Buddhas of the three thousand worlds, I bring them all back, one string after another. He went to see Xuegu, who asked, "Bring me back the original phrase (huatou).
The Master said, "The entire great earth is this huatou; I ask the Master to raise it himself. Xuegu asked, "What is 'all dharmas return to the One'?"
"Where does the 'one' return? The Master said, "The myriad dharmas do not abide; because the one does not cling, there is a state of equanimity with no place to return.
[The student] said, "Quickly give me back my verse on 'no-return'! The Master said, "Severing all across the realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, the whole mind is devoid of a single thing.

When drifting clouds have completely dispersed, the solitary moon-disk shines alone. [The student] asked, "What is 'existence'? The Master said, "Existence upon existence is fundamentally not existence."
The void opens its single mouth; the entire mechanism is put to great use. It reveals the hand of universal mastery. He asked, "What is 'non-existence'? The Master said:
"Non-existence after non-existence is not non-existence. It is vividly present, just as it is. Face-to-face, no one recognizes it. He raised his fist and questioned Dayu:
"When the thirtieth day of the twelfth month arrives, where will you hide your body and evade your fate? The Master said: "This..."
This dilapidated and ruined house has concealed birth and death for countless kalpas. This morning, with a casual stroke of the hand, it is overturned;
the void is exhausted, and all is revealed in its nakedness. He said: "So it is, so it is. In the autumn of the Gui-si year of the Chenghua era, he arrived at the capital, Beijing.

The eunuch Huang Gao built a temple for the Master, and upon petitioning the Emperor, it was granted the name Zhengfa (Orthodox Dharma). On the day the hall was opened, a monk asked: "What is it like for one who has no eyes?"
"Who can blow the flute so that it sounds? The Master said, "Prostrate yourself, and I shall tell you. The monk prostrated. The Master said, "It sounds! It sounds!
How could one be without eyes? The monk attained realization. Later, he returned to his former mountain and resided at Jun Peak.

On the seventeenth day of the second month in the fourteenth year of the Hongzhi era, he passed away. His verse says: "In human life, reaching seventy is rare since ancient times; add to that one more..."
A truly rare occurrence! If you ask this old monk where he has gone, he is laughing joyfully within the great void. He passed away while bathing.
[This concludes the record of] Chan Master Tiancheng Qi, the Dharma successor.

Chan Master Jinshan Bao of Zhuozhou went to visit Chushan. Chushan asked, "Facing south to gaze at the Northern Dipper, with a nimble head looking at the blue sky—what matter does this statement clarify?
The Master said, "Venerable Sir, you had better keep your mouth shut. Chushan said, "Not yet.
The Master said, "It might work for deceiving others. Chushan said, "As for the application of differentiation, nothing can be achieved without the eye of wisdom."
[The Master] said, "If you wish to penetrate and clarify the true teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, you must possess the correct eye that passes through the barrier.

I do not know what this 'correct eye that passes through the barrier' is. The Master let out a loud shout. Yunshan said, "Having attained the correct eye, one should clarify the ultimate pivot beyond.
[Yunshan asked,] "What is the ultimate pivot beyond? The Master said, "The bright sun at midday in the blue sky. Yunshan said, "I have not yet even dreamed of it."
[The Master] was looking on. The Teacher said, "The wooden man pulls the jade thread; the stone woman passes the golden needle.
Xuefeng said, "This is the wondrous mystery not transmitted by the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past. How do you understand it? The Teacher stepped forward and prostrated once.
Xuefeng said, "Quickly speak that turning-phrase! The Teacher said, "The rain makes the mountain colors more exquisite; the wind comes and the bamboo shadows shift. Xuefeng was about to—
The Master picked up his staff, let out a shout, and then swept his sleeves and departed. Mountan said, "I grant you thirty blows.
The Master returned to him, approached, and with palms joined, said, "I thank the Master for his compassion; your deep probing and painful piercing were most thorough.

The Mountain said, "Though you have waves that overflow the heavens, you lack the stillness of the profound waters. The Master again folded his hands and remained silent. The Mountain said, "It is like this..."
"It is so. Chan Master Tang’an Zanyuan Yan was asked by Chushan, "What is the single word of ultimate principle?
The Master said, "There are lips, but they cannot speak. Chushan said, "Why then can the wind through the pines and the flowing water speak? The Master said, "Because they—"
[The Master] was silent. Yaoshan said, "Tell me, what did he say? The Master asked, "What did you ask just now, Reverend?

Yaoshan said, "In a place where sound and resonance are utterly extinguished, is there still anything to be said? The Master replied, "If it exists, it certainly exists; it is simply that one does not hear it.
Yaoshan said, "Setting aside the hearing for a moment, tell me: what did he say? The Master then raised his fist.
Deshan said, "Is there anyone who can hear it? The Master pointed to the incense burner and said, "This one, however, can hear it.
Deshan asked, "Why can this one hear it? The Master replied, "Because it has ears. Deshan asked, "You also have two ears; why can you not hear it?
The Master said, "Even though I cannot hear it, I cannot deceive it for even a single moment. Deshan [nodded].
He said, "I grant you twenty blows. The Master then prostrated himself.
Chan Master Haiyun Shen of Ta Yuan Fu asked Bchu Shan upon hearing the sound of a bell, "Do you hear it?
The Master replied, "I hear it. Shan asked, "What do you say it is? The Master then mimicked the sound of the bell. Shan said, "As for the bell itself—"
"Before the sound has been struck, where does the resonance abide? The Master said, "Before it has been struck.

Daoshan asked, "After the sound of the bell has ceased, where does the resonance return? The Master said, "After the sound of the bell has ceased. Daoshan said, "The ear is the faculty; the resonance is the object."
"Who is it that knows the echo? The Master said, "It is not the mind that echoes; it is not the echo that is the mind. Shanzhao asked, "Does the mind have an echo?
The Master said, "Although the mind is not the echo, the place where the echo arises is distinct. Shanzhao asked, "When there is no echo, where does the mind abide?
The Master said, "The substance of the mind is serene; it does not arise following the echo, nor does it perish following the echo. This is because both..."
"The ears are empty and penetrating; therefore, application is unimpeded. Baizhang said, "Are you perhaps speaking of principles?
The Master replied, "How could I not speak of them? Baizhang took up his staff and struck him; the Master then bowed.

The ancient Chan Master Jichuan Hong of Yuzhou asked Chushan, "When a tiny gnat sucks dry the vast ocean, where do the fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs find a place to dwell and establish their lives?
Chushan said, "If your consciousness-ocean were empty, the fish and dragons would naturally undergo their own transformations.
The Master said, "I wonder where this tiny gnat is right now? Chushan said, "It is on your eyebrows."
[The Master] said, "The water-jelly flies up to the Ultimate Heaven (Akaniṣṭha), enters the eye of Maheśvara, and performs a dance.
Why is it not seen? Shan said, "How many people have lost their nostrils at this very place where it is not seen!
The Master asked, "I wonder, what is the true eye of Maheśvara? Shan shouted, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. Shan said, "The gate of the face."
Both eyes are entirely without concern; a single point atop the head illuminates heaven and earth. The Master said, "At Lianhu Bridge, I have pointed directly at people for them.
Why then do those with clear eyes fall into the well? Shan said, "High mountains have no perilous paths; level ground has deep pits."
The Master asked, "What is the matter of direct pointing? Sanshan said, "A stone lion upon a jade balustrade; a white egret amidst red lotus flowers.
The Master said, "I thank the Master for his answer. Sanshan said, "Be careful not to give rise to intellectual interpretations based on the words.
The Master bowed.
When Chan Master Dayun Xing of Xiangyang Prefecture was returning from descending Mount Chushan, he encountered Xingkong Ben on the road.
Duan’an came out to meet them. Chushan asked, "Where have you been? Xingkong replied, "I know where the Master has been.
Ben said, "The weather is bright and warm today. Duan’an remarked, "It is no easy matter for the Master to climb the mountain. Chushan—

Master Gu looked at him and said, "What do you say? The Master replied, "The assembly has been standing for a long time; I ask the Master to return to the temple. Mount San said, "Where is that temple?
The Master said, "The sound of the bell rings well. Mount San laughed and said, "Your head and horns are somewhat similar, and your nostrils are the same.
Once you have arrived home, I shall give each of you twenty blows of the staff. The assembly bowed together once, and Mount San turned around and walked away.
While Chan Master Haiju of Shijing was in retreat, Chushan struck the gate once and said, "I request to see the master within the gate.
The Master stood with hands folded and body bowed. Chushan asked, "What is your daily practice?"
The Master said, "Look at Zhaozhou’s 'No-Character' (Wu). Shan asked, "What is the meaning of 'No-Character'?
The Master said, "An unperforated iron hammer hurled right in your face. Shan asked, "What was Zhaozhou’s intention? The Master said, "It is simply because his compassionate heart is so earnest."
"His liver and gallbladder lean toward others. Mount Shàn said, "If one does not involve oneself in existence or non-existence, how can one realize it?
The Master said, "When I reach this point, there is no place for the mind to function. Mount Shàn said, "That is already the mind functioning.
The Master said, "I do not even know that. Mount Shàn said, "Who says you do not know? The Master said, "Even 'one who speaks' is not it. Mount Shàn said, "It is so. The Master bowed.
Liyun took up his staff and said, "Wait until you come out of the pass, and I will give you a beating.
The Master said, "I am not even inside the pass right now. Liyun struck the gate once with his hand and said, "What about this? The Master gave a shout.
Mount [Shishuang] said, "Not yet; speak further. The Master said, "The numinous mechanism is without obstruction; walls and barriers are utterly transparent. Mount Shishuang then gave a shout.
The Master stepped forward, made a formal inquiry, and said, "I thank the Master for his instruction. Mount Shishuang said, "The weather is sweltering;
take good care of yourself."
Chan Master Changsong Daxin Zhenyuan was the son of the Zhang family of Sanchi.

He went to attend upon Chushan and asked, "Regarding that place where the words of the Buddhas and patriarchs of all ages fail to reach, and the path where their practice does not arrive—please, Master, point this out directly for me. The Master held up his staff and said, "Huh? The Master [Changsong] then gave a shout.
Chushan struck him. The Master shouted again. Chushan struck him once more and said, "Is this how you take a beating? The Master then seized the staff.
Zhaozhou said, "What are you hitting? Shishuang gave a shout. The Master bowed. Shishuang asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "Fundamentally, there is neither movement nor stillness. Shishuang asked, "Why have you come here? The Master replied, "The place from which I come is also not real.
Shishuang asked, "Whom do you travel with? The Master replied, "A wild crane soars alone beyond the Milky Way; a clear moon shines solitary within the universe. Shishuang—
[Shan] asked: "If you suddenly encounter a fierce tiger on the road, how will you avoid it? The Master said: "Where is the tiger? Shan then made the sound of a tiger.
The Master made a gesture of fear. Shan said: "In that case, have you personally encountered a tiger?
The Master then made the sound of a tiger. Shan laughed heartily and said: "I heard that you had overturned the Tripitaka and extensively studied both internal and external classics."
Ji said, "I have mastered the teachings of the various schools and the hundred masters. Is that not so? The Master said, "In my place, there is not even a single word.
What do you mean by 'the hundred masters'? Shan said, "What about here? The Master said, "What kind of mental activity is the Master's?
Shan said, "What kind of mental activity do you say it is? The Master said, "But rather, this is my own fault. Shan said, "I grant you two blows."
"Will you accept ten more blows? The Master said, "I will not. Xuefeng said, "Why will you not? The Master said, "If I were to accept them, I would be failing the Master.
Xuefeng said, "In that case, you do not fail me, then? The Master said, "It is a grievance.
Xuefeng asked, "During the twelve periods of the day and night, what do you apply your mind to? The Master said, "I simply keep my two eyes open."
Zheng opened his eyes and stretched out both legs to sleep. Yanshan asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "The bright moon shines upon cold plum blossoms;
the frost beats upon sparse wood leaves in the cold night. Yanshan said, "Is it only this? Is there something else?
The Master said, "A red bird flies from the branch of an ancient tree. Yanshan said, "Try to speak a single phrase before your parents were born."
The Master said, "One cannot speak it. Shan asked, "Why can one not speak it? The Master said, "He has no mouth; therefore, one cannot speak it.
Shan said, "And yet you say he has no mouth. The Master said, "I thank the Master for his reply. Shan said, "The final phrase reaches the sturdy barrier;
it cuts off the vital ford, allowing passage neither to the mundane nor to the sagely. How do you understand this? The Master said:
The clay ox enters the sea and swallows the old dragon’s pearl. Yunmen said, "Not yet. The Master stepped forward, joined his palms, and stood in silence.
Yunmen said, "So it is, so it is."

Chongshan Yitian Zhiji, the Imperial Preceptor of Beici Monastery in Songpan, was a native of Peng County. He possessed extraordinary features from birth. At the age of twelve, he took Yueguang as his teacher.
Later, he succeeded Huixin to reside at Songpan. At that time, the tribes of the frontier were inconsistent in their submission or rebellion;
the Master dwelt at the border to pacify and transform them, and there were none among the tribes who did not submit to him. During the Tianfu era, he was repeatedly conferred titles.
National Teacher Chushan came to visit him. The Master presented his realization. Chushan asked, "What is the meaning of 'Mu'?
The Master said, "A drawn sword from its scabbard; its cold light pierces the Dipper and Ox. Chushan asked, "Why did Zhaozhou say 'Mu'? The Master said:
Baoji said, "The Persian chews ice and snow; he does not realize his teeth are cold. Shishuang said, "Set aside existence and non-existence—how can they be joined?
The Master said, "In the deep night, who takes the hand to wander together through the imperial streets? Shishuang asked, "Is there anything further beyond this that is extraordinary?
The Master said, "Every house has its moon in autumn; everywhere there are flowers when spring comes. A pair of clear, bright eyes."
"Where did you scatter the dust and sand? The Master said, "Excellent.
Chan Master Changyun of Yishan in Zhongxi went to visit Chushan. Chushan asked, "Virtuous One, from where have you come?"
The Master said, "Mount Liuzhi. The Mountain Master asked, "I have heard that Mount Liuzhi has fine tea; is this so? The Master said, "It is no different from what we have here.
The Mountain Master asked, "What is it like here? The Master said, "Just this. The Mountain Master asked, "What is its flavor?"
The Master said, "I am unfit to serve you. Xuefeng said, "Try bringing it here for me to see. The Master made a gesture of offering tea.
Xuefeng said, "This is merely turned by the power of the wind; it will ultimately fall into decay. Set aside movement and stillness, and try speaking another phrase.
The Master then prostrated himself in full obeisance. Xuefeng asked, "What is your Dharma-name? The Master replied, "Changyun. Xuefeng asked, "What is your religious title?"
The Master said, “Hidden Mountain. Yunshan asked, “If it is hidden within the mountain, how can it emerge from the mountain?

The Master said, “It is simply because last night a crane carried it across the highest pass. Yunshan asked, “What if it provides rain for the world? The Master said, “It spreads throughout the entire realm.
Yunshan asked, “What if it is suddenly blown apart by a fierce wind? The Master said, “It remains as the clear blue sky as before.”
Bai Zhu. Shanxiao praised him.
Shijing Huotang Zu’an Chan Master was the son of the Ju family of Chengdu. He studied the Dharma for transcending the world under Chushan.
Shan was reading the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. The Master went before him and asked, "What you are reading is merely 'lettered Prajñā' (*akṣara-prajñā*).
As for setting aside these letters, I wonder, what is true *Prajñā*? Shan then held up the sūtra and said, "Do you understand?
The Master said, "I do not understand. Shan said, "Can it be called 'letters'? The Master said, "I do not call it letters."
Ziming asked, "What is it? Sanshan replied, "The true emptiness of *prajñā* is certainly not comprised of words and letters; yet, it is also not separate from them. Why is this?
It is because the nature of words and letters is empty, and thus there is no duality between it and the essence of *prajñā*.
The Master asked, "Within this non-dual emptiness, can the names and phrases of these *prajñā*-words and letters still find a place? Sanshan replied, "Non-duality."

In the void, names and words are fundamentally severed, and there is neither truth nor falsehood. Yet the Buddhas of the past, the World-Honored Ones, provisionally employed names and words to speak of it.
This is what is called "not destroying names and words while accomplishing Prajñā. Wisdom within wisdom does not abandon them; through the realization of this single dharma, one fulfills Bodhi.
Is this not the realm of Mañjuśrī, rather than the vision of the Two Vehicles? The Master said: "If that is so, then as for names and forms—"
“By nature it is detached; is even this teaching itself non-teaching? Shanshan said, “This very state—without marks, without names, without attainment, and without teaching—is true *prajñā*.
The Master then picked up the scripture and asked, “Tell me, what is this? Shanshan gave a shout and said, “What do you say it is?
The Master also shouted. Shanshan then snatched the scripture away and, holding it up again, said:
"The hundreds of thousands of samādhis and immeasurable subtle meanings all flow forth from this single fascicle of scripture.
Do you, my son, know the origin of this single fascicle? The Master snapped his fingers once. Baoshan said, "You have now attained the functioning of Prajñā-wisdom.
He then handed the scripture to the Master, saying, "You must still read it through from beginning to end, word by word and phrase by phrase, before returning to join me."
"Deliberate upon this. The Master then took back the scripture, bowed once more, and withdrew.
Chan Master Changhui of Sanchi, a native of the Li clan of Jianzhou, went to visit Chushan.
Chushan asked, "Where have you been staying all this time? The Master replied, "I am by nature empty and without self; therefore, I do not dwell in the realm of marks."
Dongshan said, "When both existence and non-existence are discarded, how is it? The Master said, "Not departing from this very place is itself the wondrous field of enlightened nature.
Dongshan said, "I do not ask about this very place; but setting aside words, movement, and stillness, what then?
The Master said, "Although you, Master, hold fast at the essential ford and cut off the tongue, how can you deny that the whole body is manifest?"

Lù said, "Do not speak so confusedly. The Master said, "When it comes to practicing benevolence, one does not yield; how could I dare to engage in private calculations? Lù asked, "What is it that you calculate?
The Master said, "I calculate that which cannot be calculated. Lù nodded and said, "Have you not been passing your time in vain throughout the six periods of the day?
The Master replied, "I have indeed applied myself to the practice of the 'Mu' (No) koan. Lù asked, "What is it?"

[The Master] said, "No character. The Master said, "Just now, as you went up the mountain, you were so full of weariness. [Zhaozhou] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "The autumn moon is cold when the wind blows;

the old plum tree is frigid under the weight of snow. [Zhaozhou] said, "Give me back your verse on 'No Character' (Wu). The Master said: The moon is cold when the wind blows; The plum tree is frigid under the snow. If you wish to know the meaning of "No Character," Look at the face of Zhaozhou.
"Non-existence is not non-existent, nor is it a place of non-existence. Clouds disperse across the vast sky, and the moon stands solitary. From antiquity to the present, it has never been obscured.
If you wish to have your name inscribed in the charts of the patriarchs, Master Shanshan said, 'I have heard that you have studied the Tripitaka;

is this true? The Master replied, 'Venerable Sir, please do not slander me. Shanshan said, 'White is paper, black is ink. After all,..."* *(Note: The text provided ends abruptly with "畢竟," which translates to "after all," "in the end," or "ultimately.")*
“That is the Sūtra. The Master said, “Preceptor, do you not wish to speak according to the fundamental principle? Sanshan said, “What is the principle that is not according to the fundamental?
The Master said, “The Sūtra? Sanshan said, “It may be similar, but it is not yet correct. The Master said, “How then is it correct? Sanshan said, “The Sūtra.
The Master said, “I thank the Preceptor for his answer. Sanshan said, “The Buddhas and Patriarchs fundamentally have no words to speak.”
"Whatever is spoken is not the ultimate truth. Furthermore, here there is no place for you to find understanding. It transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
Try and speak a single phrase. The Master remained silent for a long while, then prostrated three times before him and stood in his place.
Mount said, "This is that which has been attained by all Buddhas and patriarchs, and transmitted through twenty-three generations.
It is a realm where words cannot reach; it is received face-to-face and realized through a silent nod of mutual understanding. You must uphold and protect it well;
you should strive for this yourself. Be careful, be careful."
Cuiwei Wukong Chan Master was a native of Shaanxi. Chushan asked him, "Having overturned the great earth, there is not an inch of soil left;
having thoroughly exhausted the source, there is not a single thing remaining. How do you understand this? The Master replied, "All stars bow toward the North;
no water does not flow toward the East. Chushan said, "In this matter, is there still any need for the function of practice and realization?"

“None,” [Tian]shou replied. Dongshan said, “There is nothing lacking in actual practice; it is simply that no functional utility can be apprehended. Dongshan said, “Even this very state of non-apprehension cannot be apprehended.
What about you? As Tianshou was about to open his mouth, Dongshan let out a loud shout. Tianshou said, “The debt of your kindness is too great to repay.
Dongshan snapped his fingers and said, “If you understand, you have attained it. You should maintain and protect this realization with diligence.”
Chan Master Rulin of Yufeng in Shanfu was asked by Chushan, "Where do you apply your mind? The Master said, "There is no place where I apply my mind.
Chushan said, "If that is so, then you are wasting your time in vain. The Master said, "The void shatters into a hundred fragments;
it is vast, penetrating, and utterly clear. Chushan asked, "What is this matter of clarity? The Master said, "Recognize the East..."
“Your face—Heaven and Earth are entirely spring. Shan said, “Not yet. The Master said, “The face-gate and nostrils hang down heavily.

"In this state, there is not even a hair’s breadth of separation. Mountan said, "This is not yet the wondrous. The Master asked, "I do not yet understand; what is the wondrous?
Mountan said, "When both extremes are wiped away, only then does one see the person prior to the kalpas. The Master said, "I have received from my teacher the pointing-out of the Vajra-eye;

having died and come back to life, I no longer doubt. Mountan praised him, saying, "How brilliant! This monk is a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net. His utterances mark him as one who has transcended."
Zongbukai said, "I am a successor of Xixian Chan; I must further maintain this realization. Do not deceive yourself by any means. The Master said, "Heaven and humans bear witness.
I thank you for your seal of approval."
Chan Master Mingxuan of Baofeng in Nanjing,
a descendant of the twenty-eighth generation under Nanyue and a successor of Chan Master Cizheng of Dongming, was born into the Fan family of Wujiang, Suzhou. In his lay life, he was a carpenter.
While constructing a pagoda courtyard on a sea-going ship, the Master injured his foot with an axe; in great pain, he asked for wine to drink.

Hearing this, the boatman went to him and said, "The carpenter Fan’s injury to his foot just now was still forgivable. But if I were to chop off your head, would you be able to drink a thousand *shí* of wine?
At these words, the Master had an awakening. He immediately desisted from drinking and requested ordination as a monk. The boatman then—
As he was being tonsured, [Zhaozhou] said, "Today your head will fall to the ground. The Master said, "Though the head may fall, it is still the head of one who enjoys fine wine;
it does not fail to fall. He was then appointed as the fire-head (the kitchen supervisor). One day, while carrying firewood, Zhaozhou saw him and asked, "Why are you carrying thorns?
The Master replied, "It is firewood. Zhaozhou laughed heartily. The Master was bewildered. Zhaozhou said, "If it is firewood, take it away and burn it. The Master [did so].
The doubt arose: "What principle is the Master ultimately asking me about? I cannot answer. That evening, he applied himself with intense resolve to investigate this.
Unbeknownst to him, he was singed by a fire so that his eyebrows were burned away and his face appeared as if shaved by a razor.

When he looked into a mirror, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment. He presented his realization to Zhuanzi, who immediately struck him. The Master seized the staff and said, "This six-foot [staff]..."
"The staff has not been used for many years; today it must be taken up once more. Master Zhou laughed heartily. The Master presented a verse, saying: "Wherever the staff strikes, bloodstains appear;
Look closely at the hidden blade within the smile. If you are a truly heroic man of spirit, Even a dead man will dance and chatter while being struck by the staff.
Master Zhou said, "This verse alone is sufficient to succeed to my lineage. Later, the Master resided in Jinling.
At Gao Feng Temple, Tianqi went for an audience. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? Tianqi replied, "From Beijing.

The Master said, "In that very Beijing, is there not some other place to go? Tianqi said, "I am carefree wherever I am. The Master asked, "Have you ever been to Sichuan? Tianqi replied, "I have been there."
The Master asked, "How is the landscape of Sichuan compared to this place of mine? He replied, "Though the mountains and rivers differ, the wind and moon are the same.
The Master raised his fist and said, "Is there still this [fist]? He replied, "No. The Master asked, "Why then is it not there?
He replied, "It is not my realm. The Master asked, "What is your realm? He replied, "Even the Buddhas cannot know it; who would dare [to speak of it]?"
Qiang Anming said, "Master, are you not yourself attached to emptiness? The Master replied, "I will never make my livelihood within a ghost cave.
Anming said, "Among the ninety-six kinds of non-Buddhist paths in the Western Heavens, you are the foremost! He then struck his whisk and departed.
On the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month in the eighth year of the Chenghua era, he manifested parinirvāṇa.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the left of Dongming Temple.
Master Junfeng Tong, a successor of the Dharma lineage of Senior Monk Qingxiang of Junfeng in Shaowu Prefecture, asked: "What is existence? What is non-existence?"
"When existence and non-existence are both not reckoned with, what then? The Master said, "Existence is birth; non-existence is cessation.
When existence and non-existence are both not reckoned with, there is neither birth nor cessation. Therefore it is said that Buddha-nature is neither born nor extinguished.
Buddha-nature is self-nature; self-nature is Buddha-nature. Not reckoning with existence or non-existence, True Suchness is alone revealed. Self-nature..."

There is no distinction. To speak of existence is itself illusion; non-existence is itself transformation. When one does not calculate existence or non-existence, there is neither illusion nor transformation.
This is called "leaving illusion to realize awakening. Because one constantly awakens without dwelling [on anything], it is called the wondrous mind of *tathatā*. Existence is itself evil.
Non-existence is itself good. When neither existence nor non-existence is reckoned, it is neither evil nor good. Because birth and death are forever severed, it is called Bodhi;
thus it is called Prajñā; thus it is called the Wondrous Dharma; thus it is called the Wondrous Mind; thus it is called the Buddhas of the three periods;

thus it is called the Heart-Seal of the successive patriarchs. It is also named the Perfect Penetration of Self-Nature. Turning upside down and coming from the top, it is free and sovereign in every direction.
There is no sitting and no meditation; there is no cultivation and no realization; there is no concentration and no distraction.
I pray that the Master, out of compassion, will certify this emptiness. He further presented a verse, saying: "The nature of phenomena is empty and unimpeded; Equanimous observation is sovereign.
Severing the dualistic mechanism, This is called transcending the three realms. [The Master] declared: "You should preserve this deeply and not speak of it hastily."
Zen Master Tiancai Ying of Mount Jing in Hangzhou, a successor of Zen Master Tiance Xuan of Tianning, once said: "Master Mota stirred up waves upon level ground;
he struck empty space to produce a wooden wedge. Having returned with the lethal poison of the strike, he finally claimed to have personally seen Baoyue."
I do not know how many people’s eyes he has blinded. He was already mute, yet he opened his mouth to chatter.
Master Tiantong Xian, known as Yuzhi, of Bitong Monastery in Nanjing, a successor of Chan Master Dongfang Shao, asked: "There is a Tathāgata within Bitong Monastery."
"Could it be you, Master? The Master asked, "Does the Senior Monk see it? He replied, "Even if one were to see it, it would be like gold dust falling into the eyes.
The Master said, "How long has this fellow been dead? You have come to beg for his life. He turned and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
The next day, he ascended the hall and cited an ancient worthy who said, "Break open the Great Tang Empire and find someone who does not understand."

"There is no one who understands the Buddha-dharma. He further said, "I have traveled once around the South, yet I have not encountered a single person upon the tip of my staff who understands the Buddha-dharma.
These two statements are highly enigmatic; try to provide a response for them.
Zhizhe said, "In front there is no meeting with a village; behind there is no passing by a shop. The Master said, "Not yet. Speak again.
Zhizhe said, "If one does not meet a connoisseur, it is but a weary labor to discuss the cold of winter. The Master asked again, "You have traveled south to seek instruction;

what words or phrases did you encounter? Try to speak of them. Zhizhe recited the verse on his previous realization of the Way: "The lake's light rests upon my staff for three thousand acres; The mountain colors open before my door."
Five or six peaks: what meets the eye is, from the very beginning, a manifest reality. The meditation cushion does not now refine a stubborn emptiness;

with the scenery filling one’s gaze, there is enough for daily life. Who would distinguish between kin and stranger on level ground? Even if Bodhidharma had transmitted his secret instructions on the mind, were you questioned about them, you still would not recognize him.
The Master said, “Not so, not so. Zhizhe asked, “Why ‘not so, not so’? The Master said, “You do not negate it.”
"No. Such a person is neither right nor wrong. The Emperor of Liang and Bodhidharma both failed to perceive his potential; why trouble yourself by breaking reeds and sending someone after him?
Ancient and modern alike have fallen into the snares of others. Zhizhe asked, "How can one avoid falling into the snares of others?
The Master gave him a slap and said, "Is this falling, or is it not falling? Zhizhe immediately prostrated himself in thanks. All that he had harbored in his mind for years dissolved completely.
The ice melted away. As the Master was traveling to the Zongjing Hall on West Lake, he ascended the Dharma seat and said, "This place is perfectly suited for preaching the Dharma.

From the side, Zhixian cried out, "The preaching of the Dharma is already finished! The Master then descended from the seat and looked back, asking, "Which of these is my place for preaching the Dharma?
Zhixian replied, "The sword has long since departed. The Master smiled and nodded in agreement.
The Dharma-transmission verse bestowed by Chan Master Baofang Jin of Tiantu Mountain in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Ning of Yifeng, says: "The true nature is originally without nature;
The true Dharma is originally without dharma. When one thoroughly understands this absence of nature and dharma, Where is there anything that is not fully penetrated?"

was the son of the Jiang family of Zhongling in Nanchang. He paid his respects to Master Wushuo at Jingmenshou.
He shaved his head and was instructed to contemplate the saying: "Look back and see where one returns. Later, he visited many senior masters.

The Master struck him across the face with his palm. Later, he met Bao-feng, who granted him formal approval (*inka*).

Zen Master Jin-shan Bao asked, "What is it like when the mud ox at the bottom of the sea chews the moon as it runs? The Master said, "Not dwelling beyond the time of Wei-yin; returning to the path, one acts according to one's will.
He asked again, "What is it like when the stone tiger before the cliff cradles its cubs and sleeps? The Master said, "Only those who know the sound may be permitted to know the sound."
Qichu said, "If one is a connoisseur of the sound, the principle is naturally forgotten. He asked, "What is 'an iron snake boring into the diamond eye'?
The Master said, "The Snow Maiden boasts of her brocade within the brazier; the frog flaps its wings and flies all across the sky. He asked, "What is 'Kunlun riding an elephant while a heron leads'?
The Master said, "A clear breeze meets the ancient cliff; the green cypress trees shake their heads in confusion. He asked, "... (The text here is incomplete).

The Master said, "The falcon originally flies beyond the clouds. Vajra laughed and nodded his head, saying, "Within this there is one phrase that can kill and can give life, can let go and can seize. Ultimately, what is that one phrase? The Master let out a thunderous shout and then gave a *he*. He addressed the assembly: "There is no dharma in the mundane world; there is no dharma in the supramundane world. One who realizes this 'no-dharma' returns home to sit in peace.

If you can realize this Dharma-less state, then please stop and stay outside the gate. (Addressing the assembly: Do you all understand? The moon hangs from the tips of the locust trees, bright and clear;
the deluded call it a bow. Do you understand? The upper crescent is not yet like it; the lower crescent is likewise unfit. Do you understand?
A single wheel is personally held aloft; where else could one encounter the moon and stars? To the assembly: The crane loves the green pines as clouds offer jade;
the mandarin ducks sleep amidst purple smartweed as brocade adds its flowers. Fishermen’s songs mingle in the Wuling Stream; having missed the peach grove, do not utter such curses.
Do you understand? How many woodcutters have had their axe-handles rotted away, all for the sake of making ordinary people play at chess?

To the assembly: Wild flowers and weeds reveal the true mechanism. The sword is named "Great Void" (Gujue); butterflies fly through the garden as the clappers strike. The pearl is called "Night-Light";
on both banks, the reeds and chrysanthemums nod their heads together. Clouds rise to bring rain; along a single stretch of river, the ospreys fly with the gulls. Revealed.
Bound together as frost, I, this mountain monk, have here exhausted my sincerity in revealing it all. Yet there is one further message that remains unclarified.
⊕ Do you understand? He does not sit in the Hall of the Empty King over there; how could he consent to weed the fields while facing the sun?
Chan Master Fashou Daoji of Tianning Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Jigan. He was the son of the Zhang family from Xiuwater in his native prefecture.

While visiting Jigan, he happened to walk along the corridors when he heard the sound of a bell from the Buddha Hall; he attained sudden and profound enlightenment. He then proceeded to the abbot’s quarters. Jigan—
Wang Jian looked at him and said with a smile, "You are a thief! The Master said, "The thief has already been apprehended.
Wang asked, "Where are the stolen goods? The Master shook his sitting mat and said, "A mess! A mess! Wang said, "You are a liar; what is there to be a mess about?

The Master gave a shout and returned to the assembly. Master An was delighted and certified his realization. At the beginning of the Jiajing era, he resided at An-yin Monastery in Jinling. [End of Excerpt]
The Master raised his whisk and addressed the assembly, saying, "Do you see it? He then struck the whisk with it, saying, "Do you hear it?

Since you see it as soon as it is raised and hear it as soon as it is struck, the wondrous Treasury of True Suchness is beyond thought and deliberation; its functional application is cool and refreshing. How marvelous, how marvelous!
Yet you people yourselves are not men of integrity; instead, you look toward the doors of others to seek knowledge and seek an audience.
To conceal one's own treasures and be content with appearing as a beggar—this is surely because they think the various Buddhas have some other extraordinary matter.
When the butcher with the broad forehead cast down his blade and said, "I am counted among the thousand Buddhas," how could there be such circuitous turns or intellectual views?
You men of spirit, why do you not simply take this up and carry it forth? While residing at Tianning, [the Master] spoke thus because of the cawing of a flock of crows.
A scholar asked, "Which sound is good? Which sound is not good? The Master said, "In my place, all are the gateways through which Avalokiteśvara enters into principle.
Lu Guangzu of the Ministry of Personnel asked, "Was there no *Yī* before the drawing [of the trigrams]?
The Master said, "If there were no Fuxi, with what would one draw? Lu said, "What is it after the drawing? The Master said, "Originally there was not a single stroke."
Lu said, "The sixty-four hexagrams currently exist; how can you say they do not? The Master said, "Do not cling to words.
Lu said, "Let the various masters set aside words and observe the arising of a single line. The Master called out, "Lu! Lu responded, "Yes. The Master said, "From where does this single line arise?
Xiong Nan-sha, the Vice Prefect of Huzhou, asked, "Suppose someone were to come with a sword to take your head—what would you do?"
[Zhaozhou] said, "Head! Would you still hide and avoid it? The Master said, "If there were a general who does not blink his eyes, there would be a monk who does not fear death.
Zhaozhou made a gesture of brandishing a sword. The Master threw himself down. Zhaozhou said, "What a fine monk!
You have died beneath my blade. The Master rose up and laughed heartily, saying, "Why? Why? He asked, "Without eyes or ears..."
“Nose, tongue, body, and mind—what is their essential meaning? The Master said, “If you can utter a single phrase before your parents were born, then I shall answer.
A monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “The thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics. The monk said, “These are the Reward and Transformation Buddhas.
What is the Dharma-body Buddha? The Master said, “Do not cling to forms. The monk asked, “What is the Dharma? The Master said: [He remained silent.]

Jade rollers and lapis lazuli cases are not the Dharma. "The question you ask, *ācārya*, is far too clear. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Understand, *ācārya*. The monk responded, "Yes. The Master said, "And yet you say you do not understand. The monk asked, "What is a monk?

The Master said, "Robes embrace the snow beyond a thousand mountains; the mendicant’s staff drags through the clouds across the four seas. The monk asked, "Is there anything further above this? "There is nothing even 'downward'—how can one speak of 'upward'? Question: 'What was it like before Bodhidharma had not yet come? The Master said:
'The ancient mirror is clear and distinct, containing the myriad phenomena. Question: 'What was it like after he had come? The Master said:

'The myriad phenomena are clear and distinct within the ancient mirror. Question: 'How do you employ it? The Master said: 'If the Patriarch had not come, the ancient mirror would have remained buried. While sitting by a stream, a monk...
The monk asked, "What is the phrase of 'following the waves and chasing the currents'? The Master said, "On both banks, the spring breeze flows on without ceasing;

in the single stream, the falling flowers are ever fresh. The monk said, "I am at a loss for how to understand this. The Master said, "The dragonfly flies still slowly; the butterfly dances all too busily.
The monk said, "The Master has shown me the scenery. The Master let out a thunderous shout. The monk bowed. The Master [nodded].
The Master said, "That is not it; speak further. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "To weep until the blood flows is of no use;

it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. One day he manifested illness. Someone requested that he speak a verse. The Master said, "These are all mere literary embellishments;
they are not without further meaning. He gestured with his hand and passed away.

Chan Master Yuequan Faju of Yuzhi Hermitage at Tianchi in Huzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Bifeng Xian. Born into the Fu family of Jiaxing, he studied Confucianism from his early childhood and became thoroughly versed in the classics and scriptures.
Later, he followed a teacher at Zisheng Temple in Haiyan, where he constructed a separate quiet chamber to read the *Platform Sutra*.
He attained a realization. Later, upon hearing a monk cite the question asked of Dadian: "What is seeing one's nature? Dadian replied, "Seeing is itself nature. He could not help but laugh.
Subsequently, he built a hermitage on Wugong Mountain and composed two poems titled "Lake Light" and "Leaning on a Staff.

He went to study under Mengju. The Master asked, "How can one avoid falling into the trap of others? Mengju gave him a slap, and the Master immediately attained great enlightenment. He then moved [to another location].
While residing at the Yuzhi Jingśa Hermitage on Tianchi Lake, he ascended the hall and said: "The swift passage of time flows like a river; everyone says there are thirty-six decans [in a year].

Chan Master Wansong Huilin of Jing Mountain Wan Song in Hangzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Jintai Jue. He was the son of the Shen family from Renhe County in the prefecture.

Fundamentally there is no coming or going; it merely responds to conditions. Thereupon, he passed away.
Chan Master Wuyue Xiu of Tianmu was a successor to Chan Master Yeweng Xiao (Wuqu).
Wuqu went to visit him, and the Master said: "The coming of Bodhidharma from the West was to point directly to the human mind, so that one may see one's nature and become a Buddha;
it lies solely in taking this up directly beneath you. If you can believe this thoroughly, you may set down all external conditions and investigate a single phrase."
"All dharmas return to the One. Qiu You had an awakening. [The Master] entrusted him with a verse, saying: "Neither dharma nor non-dharma;
neither nature nor non-nature; neither mind nor non-mind. I have now finished entrusting to you the Dharma of the mind."
Chan Master Guyin Jingqin of Mount Doufeng in Jianning Prefecture was a dharma heir of Chan Master Shoutang Song. He was the son of the Cai family of Jianyang in the local commandery.

At the age of twenty-five, he paid his respects to the Abbot of Mount Chishi to leave the household life. He immediately asked: "People say that one must clarify the mind and see one's nature; is this not so?"
"Is this the place where my mind arises, that which I am aware of? Shishuang said, "This is the deluded mind, not the true mind.
To identify with this mind is to mistake a thief for one's own son. The Master asked, "In that case, do I then have no mind?
Shishuang said, "It is you who know there is nothing known, and who are aware that there is nothing perceived. Upon hearing this, the Master was instantly liberated from body and mind. Alone...
He realized his own nature; it was neither knowing nor not-knowing, neither awakening nor not-awakening.

Having encountered Chan Master Jinghuang of Quanzhou, he was instructed to contemplate the koan "The myriad dharmas return to one. Later, while traveling through Nanyang to Jiuming River in Shu, he attained realization midway.
He visited Shoutang at Wushan Temple and subsequently received formal certification (inka). His *Tihui ji* (Collection of the Essence of Ambrosia) circulates in the world.

a descendant of the thirty-first generation of Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Tianqi, was born into the Xi family of Guozhe, Shaowu.
The Master [Zhaozhou] entered the monastic order at Qiying Monastery. He attended lecture halls and, day and night, investigated the four-line verse of the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū.
One day, suddenly hearing the neighing of a horse, he attained a sudden and great awakening. He went to see Master Qichu; as soon as he prostrated himself, Qichu struck him.

Every day he was scrutinized by the Elder. The Master said, "The Venerable One is one who forgets the world while in the world, and forgets thought while in thought.
How could I possibly scrutinize him? Qiji asked, "What does 'forgetting the world while in the world' mean? The Master replied, "To realize that things are not things."

A monk asked, "What is it like when one is mindful yet forgets mindfulness? The Master said, "In the mind, there is no mind. The monk asked, "When both mind and objects are forgotten, what is it like?
The Master said, "Mount Hua rises steeply; Mount Taihang is lofty. After he took up residence, a monk asked, "What is the original face? The Master said, "The Stone Incense Pavilion.
The monk asked, "If one goes directly in this way, what then? The Master said, "You have lost it."

The monk was speechless (Xiaoyan performed a bow on behalf of the monk, saying: "The entire realm gazes upon it universally"). One day, he suddenly vanished. Two years later, he returned to the mountain in the seventh month.

On the eve of the new moon, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Because my mind has not yet attained full realization, I shall travel abroad once more. The mountains and rivers of Wu and Yue stretch out in vast obscurity;
with a single staff I shall shoulder the sun and moon. At Longquan Temple, my discourse shall be especially long. He then cast his staff to the ground, sat in the lotus posture, and passed away.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the right of the temple.

The World-Honored One remained silent for a long while, whereupon the outsider suddenly realized the Buddha’s intent. He then said: "Since..."
"This does not involve existence or non-existence. 'For a long while' is also merely a conventional name. At that very moment, the outsider attained great enlightenment. What did he realize?
As Yan was about to respond, the Master covered Yan’s mouth with his hand and said, "Stop, stop! You still have it hanging on your teeth!"
Yan suddenly said, "It can be said that the patch-robed monks of the Eastern Land are not equal to the heterodox practitioners of the Western Heaven;
they are truly far behind. He then presented a verse, saying: "I laugh at myself for my past practice of copying models, How many times it has been red, how many times black.
Now, having thanked my master, I return to my hometown; Who cares whether I have attained anything in my life? The Master also expressed great joy, saying, "How extraordinary! This...
The verses are the words of one who has attained the stage of the supreme fruit.

One day, while receiving food, his bowl suddenly fell to the ground. He had a sudden realization. Subsequently, upon reading the *Zongjing Lu*, he attained great enlightenment.

How is it unbound? Thus we know that Master Baizhang skillfully guided beginners for this very purpose.
These are merely deceptive and empty words; in reality, he was neither able to tie nor able to untie it.

Suppose there were a bold fellow like Meng Bala who came forth and said, "I can tie a knot where Great Master Baizhang could not tie one, so as to cause all the monks in the world to lose their bearings and find no way out. He would likewise be able to do so regarding Great Master Baizhang.

Chan Master Wuqu Ruokong of Jiewei Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Yaoweng Xiaoshan. He was a native of the Shi family of Xiushui in the prefecture. By nature he was compassionate and benevolent, and he devoted his mind to the inner scriptures (Buddhist texts).

Upon hearing a cock crow, he attained realization and received confirmation from the Elder. He then shut himself away in retreat and addressed the assembly: "For over thirty years I have visited and paid homage to the patriarchal masters of the ten directions and requested their instruction.

On the seventh day of the seventh month, gather all your cleverness within yourself to eat it; swallow this exquisite and marvelous skill all at once, leaving not even a trace behind.
In the past, you played with cleverness and lost your true nature; from now on, embrace simplicity and maintain your honest ignorance.
Flying through clouds and riding on mists—all shall become empty. A hundred clever tricks are not equal to one word of sincerity. What is this one phrase of sincerity?
Two [times] two; one [time] one. Holding up his whisk, he said: "This thing has never been clever or ornate.

On the sixth day of the eighth month of the Gengchen year of the Wanli era, he manifested a slight illness and spoke this verse: "Coming into life and departing from death are like empty flowers; Departing from death and coming into life are but a single dream.
This skin bag is entrusted to the god of fire (Cing-ding-kung); The white bones cross the broken bridge along with the multitude. Hehe! The bright moon is clear."

He chanted and played with the wind. (Buddhist Master Fang said: "The leather bag has already been entrusted to the fire god; the white bones shall all return to the Broken Bridge. Ultimately, with what will he chant the wind? With what will he play with the moon? After a long silence, he said:

"The three periods of time grasped together serve as my staff; The ten directions are originally my old *kāṣāya*. The clay ox and stone tiger know [it]."

His mother suddenly heard the sound of a great thunderclap shaking the earth one clear day, and shortly thereafter he was born. He suffered the hardships of orphanhood from childhood, and upon reaching adulthood, he did not...
He lived comfortably amidst the secular world. At the age of twenty-two, he took Daji of Guanghui Temple as his teacher, shaved his head, and received full ordination, aspiring solely to the Way.
He ascended Zili Ridge to visit Wumen, who asked him, "The Ten Sages and Three Worthies have already perfected sacred wisdom;
why then do you say that the Way does not clarify this principle? Wumen replied in a stern voice, "The Ten Sages and Three Worthies you already know. As for...

"What is the meaning of this? Speak quickly! The Master’s response did not accord with the truth. One day, while carrying a basket to wash vegetables by the water, a stalk of vegetable suddenly fell into the stream.

It spun around following the current, and though he tried to catch it, he could not grasp it. The Master suddenly attained realization and leaped for joy. Carrying his basket back, he entered the hall of hearing and seeing.
Nanquan asked, "What is that? The Master replied, "A basket of vegetables. Nanquan said, "Why do you not speak differently? The Master said: [I have already spoken].
"Please do not ask me further, Preceptor. Next, he went to visit Da'jue. Upon returning, he attended Wumen.
During a session by the brazier, Wumen asked, "Every person has an original father and mother; where are your parents now? The Master replied, "A single fire has burned them away.
Wumen said, "If that is so, then you have no parents? The Master said, "They exist, but they are only the Buddha-eye."
[The Master] looked but did not see him. [The Master] asked, "Do you see him? The Teacher replied, "I also do not see him. [The Master] asked, "Why do you not see him?
The Teacher replied, "If I were to see him, he would not be my true parents. [The Master] said, "Excellent! The Teacher then composed a verse, saying:

"The original true parents have never been separated from us throughout kalpas. In rising and sitting we rely upon their power; in cold and warmth we share their knowledge. When we meet, we do not..."
He saw him. Although they met face-to-face, they did not know one another. He asked, "Where is he now? and presented the matter clearly to the Master.
The Master heard this and said, "So it is, so it is. [The monk] went straight to Zhongnan. Later, he appeared in the world at various places such as Gaozuo, Niushou, and Yuantong.

One day, while ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "Is there anyone? Is there anyone? At that time, a monk came forward and prostrated. The Master struck him across the back with the staff and said, "Too much!"

The Master asked, "What are you saying? The monk replied, "I have not yet uttered a single word; why do you call me talkative? The Master struck him again, saying, "A second offense will not be tolerated.

He ascended the hall and said: "The courtyard is moist with dew, the steps are slippery; The mountain path is lost amidst trailing vines. Zen practitioners often inquire about the meaning of the Patriarchs;
Last night, carrying his sandals, he returned alone to the West. He held up his staff and pointed, saying, "Look! Look! The Patriarch..."
The Master also came over the mountain gate. He called for an attendant to say, "Give me [this person]," and immediately drove him out. Now tell me:
he was precisely seeking the Patriarch, yet when the Patriarch himself arrived, why did he personally drive him out? After a long silence, he said: "It is on account of you all;
those who would wear this must not treat it as an ordinary matter. He ascended the hall and said: "A single arrow at the gate; whoever comes—"
