The Master let out a thunderous roar and gave a shout. Xuefeng Chi said, "What a fine shout! The Master gave two more shouts in succession and returned to his place. Xuefeng Chi looked at the Master and said, "Give one more shout and see.
The Master immediately left the Dharma Hall. Xuefeng Chi returned to the Abbot's quarters. The Master followed him in and said, "Just now I struck the gong for the Master.
Thereupon, Xuefeng Chi beat the drum and ascended the hall, where he conferred upon the Master the robe and whisk. He then commanded him to enter the room and gave him further instructions.
Having repeatedly supported the Buddha-dharma, the Master presented a verse, saying: "If I, this humble one, were to support the Buddha-dharma, I would leave him [the opponent] to do as he pleases;
in the end, I would simply give him thirty blows of the staff. Do not say that I am being explicit in bestowing rewards and punishments.

When Master Chi passed away, the Master guarded the reliquary shrine for three years. In the forty-fifth year of the Wanli era, the assembly requested him to succeed to the seat and propagate the Dharma. Subsequently, he resided at...
At Tongxuan in Tai, Jinsu in He, Huangbo in Min, and Yuwang and Tiantong in Ming—on account of the snow, he ascended the hall and said:
"Yesterday was green mountain; today is white snow. O brothers, this is good news.
Wild deer and travelers leave footprints at every step, yet only the horn-hanging antelope is utterly breathless. From of old, the hunting dogs have found it difficult to seek him out."
"You must raise your eyes high to attain it. He ascended the hall; without taking his seat, the Master stood before it and said, "This monk is gasping for breath and cannot speak.
He then coughed and spat phlegm onto the floor, saying, "Brothers, try to say something! After a long while, no one stepped forward.
The Master wiped it away with his foot and returned to his quarters. Ascending the hall again, he said, "The first stroke cuts off everything."
At the critical ford, as soon as one leans an ear toward it, one loses the family treasure. From the beginning, the Buddha-dharma has not conformed to human sentiment;
thus it is said: "To emerge from the crowd, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to overcome the victor, one must be a lion’s cub. Entering the hall, he said: "Speaking in silence."

When it is time to speak, he remains silent. The Great Gate of Generosity stands open without obstruction. How can one compare this to Linji’s little servant boy, the "white-handed thief" who wields his bare hands with total mastery?
He lets out a shout. Ascending the hall, he raised his staff and said: "If you raise one, you must not raise two.
To let one pass is to fall into the second. He threw down the staff and said: "The old monk has fallen into the second. Now, what about the first?"
How could he possibly raise the question? He simply descended from his seat and ascended the hall. "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is [Buddha-nature];

they let go from emptiness. The tabby cat and the white ox, however, do know that there is; they ascend to heights by relying on the earth. Letting go from emptiness, there are no sentient beings to be saved.
Rising from the earth, one transcends the Buddhas and surpasses the Patriarchs. When one has transcended the Buddhas and surpassed the Patriarchs, all sentient beings have been saved;
yet when the sands of the Ganges of Buddhas have no sentient beings left to save, how could the Buddhas ever have saved a single person?

Even so, if you suddenly cut off both ends and cast open the middle—if a phrase that suddenly emerges is difficult to discern—how do you speak it? "Donning the straw raincoat and tilting the bamboo hat."
Beyond a thousand peaks, he leads water to irrigate vegetables before the Five Elders. Entering the hall, he said: "If you have not yet reached Tiantong, it is natural to harbor doubts;
but once you have reached Tiantong, the ice melts and the walls crumble. Why is this so? Have you not heard it said: 'Hearing a name is not as good as seeing the face'?"
The face has already been seen; what kind of matter has been accomplished within the portion of each person? When a single film is in the eye, empty flowers fall in confusion.
Entering the hall: Today is the fifth day of the fifth month. The administrators and heads have requested that this old monk ascend the seat to respond to the occasion.
This old monk has no stratagem at hand. How could vermilion powder or burning wine possibly suffice? It is simply not possible. Yet, one must...

Furthermore, there was not even a single copper coin to buy glutinous rice. After deliberating until his resources were exhausted and his strength spent, he suddenly attained that which the wealthy do not have in excess and the poor do not lack—a true gateway to the Dharma of equality.

It was precisely this that could transform the customs and change the mores of the world. He then raised both fists and said: "I shall simply offer these two large *zong* (rice dumplings) as sustenance."
Great assembly, let yourselves bite at it horizontally or vertically as you please;

if you suddenly bite into your own portion, everyone will be thoroughly satiated, sparing yourselves from being tormented by poverty and parched by hunger. Why is this so? Because, in the end, you have lost your own treasure.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Everyone says that the retreat has been concluded, yet they do not realize that at Tiantong, there is no such thing as 'concluding' or 'opening' a retreat.

Whether it is concluded or opened need not be discussed at all. It is simply that from dawn till dusk, I have been driving the assembly about—either carrying bricks or moving tiles, hauling earth or lifting stones. When I see you lagging behind even slightly, I am either shouting or scolding you."
"How do you all understand this? Do you still know where this old fellow of Tiantong stands when he acts for others? 'Three lives, sixty kalpas.
A monk asked, "When meeting on a narrow path and one's skull is shattered to pieces—at such a time, where does the True Man of No Rank establish his dwelling and sustain his life?
The Master said, "'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. The monk said, "If that is so..."
"Then ten thousand *li* are cloudless, and a single wheel shines far and wide as it departs. The Master said, "He deserves thirty blows right under his heels.
A monk asked, "A single drop from Caoxi flows straight through to the Dragon Pond. What is the matter of flowing straight through to the Dragon Pond? The Master said, "It pierces through the skull.
The monk asked, "How do you speak the phrase regarding the source being distant and the flow being long? The Master said, "Simply give him..."
[The monk] asked, "How is it when one has gone? He asked, "What is the realm of Jingu (Golden Grain)? The Master said, "Sandy fields and mulberry groves across the four wilds.
[The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Gazing from the peak of Jingu. [The monk] said, "I have already received your instruction regarding the person and the realm;
how is it for the matter of ascending the hall after the drum is struck? The Master said, "Behold him! Look up to him! [The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?"
The Master struck him and said, "This is still the family style of old times. The Master struck him again and said, "You understand this as the family style of old times.
A monk asked, "What are the Three Jewels? The Master said, "One meal of fried cakes and two meals of congee. The monk said, "I am not asking about those three satiations.
The Master said, "The old monk observes them daily. A monk asked, "Does one who has attained great enlightenment still have likes and dislikes?"
"No. The Master said, "One can love people; one can hate people. The monk replied, "This is the worldly teaching of the Confucianists;
how could it be the matter of great awakening that transcends the world? The Master asked, "Who are you? The monk hesitated, and the Master shouted at him and drove him out.
He then asked, "What is the path of unsurpassed bodhi? The Master said, "A layman wearing a monk’s official hat. The monk asked, "Ultimately..."
"What skillful means are there? The Master replied, "It is best for you to seek it within yourself.

The Master presided over the Dharma for twenty-five years, receiving people according to their fundamental nature (*benfen*), regardless of whether they were beginners or those with long-standing training; he acted solely in accordance with the mandate.

Consequently, many heroes under his seat emerged as preeminent talents. In the fourteenth year of the Chongzhen era, the year of Xinsi, the Master harbored the intention to retire and departed, staff in hand.
In the first month of the *Renwu* year, he arrived at Tongxuan Mountain and thereupon stayed to embody [the teachings].
Previously, the official Tian of the Imperial Clan had entered Tiantong Monastery, bringing a purple robe for the Imperial Noble Consort Tian to request the Master to preach the Dharma.

Later, when the Master reached the secondary capital, he was invited by the Abbot of Baoren Temple—whose appointment was due to his connection with the Second Ancestor—to renovate the monastery; the Master accepted this charge.
Regarding this matter, he received the Emperor’s gracious decree to dispatch an official to welcome the Master.

The Master firmly declined, stating that he was fortunate to dwell in the mountains, where he could sufficiently engage in spiritual cultivation to repay the grace of the state; through these words, his intention to transcend the mundane world was also revealed.
On the fourth day of the seventh month, he manifested a slight illness. At noon on the seventh day, he ascended his meditation couch and sat upright;

in the space of a brief moment, he passed away in stillness. He was seventy-seven years of age and forty-seven years since his ordination. His stupa was enshrined on the southern mountain of Tiantong.
Chan Master Tianyin Yuanxiu of Qingshan in Changzhou was the son of the Min family from Yixing in the same prefecture.

He received the tonsure under Longchi and took up the koan of "the state before one's parents were born. One day, while unfolding the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he attained realization at the passage where the Buddha rebukes Ānanda, saying, "This is not your mind.

At that time, he encountered Longchi traveling north; the Master was instructed to lock himself in retreat and investigate the karmic conditions of the ancient masters. Thus, he traversed the various causes and conditions of the ancients.

There was nothing he did not reveal. Only when a monk questioned him regarding the dialogue concerning "The single path to nirvana for the Bhagavāns of the ten directions" at Qianfeng, the monk harbored doubts.
Suddenly, upon hearing a donkey bray, he attained great enlightenment. His verse says: "Hearing suddenly the bray of a donkey, I am startled awake and break into laughter."
Ten thousand distinctions and a thousand variations; neither sound nor form, yet a clamor. Understanding the gate, he hastened to pay his respects at the imperial pool and offered this verse:
"Others say the northern lands are cold; I say the southern regions are warm. It is man who does not perceive the cold and the warmth; it is the destitute man who knows them."
Dachi accepted this. One day, in the meditation hall, the Master asked, "What is it like when there is a vivid, solitary clarity?
Dachi replied, "Wait until you reach that state, and I will tell you. The Master then gave a shout. Dachi said, "Have you still given rise to a conceptual mind?
The Master shook his sleeves and departed. On another day, for some reason, Dachi put on a short tunic, lifted a chair, and performed a woman’s bow toward him.
The Master said, "You, Senior Monk, wait while I bow to you as my teacher. The Master smiled and presented this verse: "The wooden man raises his voice with a laugh;
Who recognizes him when he puts on his clothes? Yesterday he was seen as a manly hero; Today he has become an old woman.
Chixiao said, "This verse is most agreeable to the old monk's mind. (The year being the 48th year of the Wanli era.)
He resided at Qing Shan and later at Baon. Ascending the hall, he said: "To not allow a single speck of dust to stand is still halfway there;
to cut off all streams is still to remain outside the gate. Now tell me, what is the phrase for arriving home? He looked left and right and said:
"The Bodhisattva Guanyin buys a sesame cake with money; when she lets go of her hand, it turns out to be a steamed bun. Those who arrive—
Only when one can be as upright within as the sky universally covers and the earth universally supports;

when one can contain Mount Sumeru within the ears and hold the four great oceans within the eyes—only then does one have the capacity for discourse. If this is so, then where exactly does such a person sit with their whole body?
Do you understand? "A few sounds of the clear chime lie beyond right and wrong; a solitary idler dwells between heaven and earth. (End)
The Hall. Zen is not a matter of intellectual understanding; the Way transcends all merit and achievement. The wondrous essence is profoundly still, and the true mechanism is uniquely revealed.

It cannot be conceived by the mind, nor can it be imagined by thought. It cannot be proclaimed in words, nor can it be illuminated through silence. It cannot be seen in form, nor can it be sought through sound.
Yet, with a single thought turning the light back upon itself, one is identical to what is originally possessed. If this is so, then [the teaching of] Śākyamuni...

When Old Śākyamuni beheld the morning star, what did he see? If you can penetrate this point here, you will instantly transcend the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* and cut off the heads of both the *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas.
You will then wear clothes and eat food according to the occasion. Yet, there is still the path that goes beyond—where is Śākyamuni right now?
*Ei!* He is emitting light and shaking the earth upon the eyelashes of all of you.
"Simply do not touch it. If you touch it, you shall receive thirty blows of the staff. Why? Have you not heard it said: 'A man of substance has the will to pierce the heavens;
he does not walk where the Tathāgata has walked'? [He] planted his staff and addressed the assembly: 'This old monk dwells in a dilapidated courtyard.

“Wood, tiles, and rubble, together with all people, turn the Great Dharma Wheel. It awakens the great potential and great function within all people.

You must not, under any circumstances, let it pass you by face-to-face. If you let it pass, you will only know that affairs pursue you before your eyes, without realizing that old age descends upon your head.

"What is the 'concealing the point' (zangfeng) regarding phenomena? The Master said, "Radishes from Huzhou; ginger from Xuanchuan.
"How is it the 'concealing the point' regarding both phenomena and principle? The Master said, "Where there is water, the moon is reflected; where there are flowers, they do not fail to bear spring.

[The student] arrived. The Master said, "Every word reveals the truth; every step loses the track. [The student] asked, "What is it when the meaning reaches but the phrase does not? The Master said, "It is right upon the tip of the tongue, yet one cannot bring oneself to spit it out no matter how hard one tries. [The student] asked, "What is it when both the meaning and the phrase reach? The Master said, "When the meaning and the phrase are both present, they are like a dragon soaring through the void, leaving no trace behind. The student bowed. The Master said, "If you wish to understand the Way, you must first understand yourself. If you do not understand yourself, you will not understand the Way. If you understand yourself, you will naturally understand the Way. If you do not understand the Way, you will not understand yourself. If you understand the Way, you will naturally understand yourself. Therefore, understanding the self is called 'understanding the Way,' and understanding the Way is called 'understanding the self. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not far off; it is simply that people create complications for themselves. If you wish to see the Way, you need only look at your own mind. Your own mind is the Way; there is nothing else. If you seek the Way outside your own mind, you will wander endlessly in birth and death. If you seek the Way within your own mind, you will immediately realize the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be sought; it is something to be realized. If you seek it, you will lose it; if you realize it, you will find it. If you do not seek it, you will not lose it; if you do not realize it, you will not find it. Therefore, do not seek it, and do not fail to realize it. This is what is called 'realizing the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be grasped; it is something to be let go of. If you grasp it, you will lose it; if you let it go, you will find it. If you do not grasp it, you will not lose it; if you do not let it go, you will not find it. Therefore, do not grasp it, and do not fail to let it go. This is what is called 'letting go of the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be practiced; it is something to be lived. If you practice it, you will exhaust yourself; if you live it, you will be free. If you do not practice it, you will not exhaust yourself; if you do not live it, you will not be free. Therefore, do not practice it, and do not fail to live it. This is what is called 'living the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be attained; it is something to be entered. If you attain it, you will be attached; if you enter it, you will be liberated. If you do not attain it, you will not be attached; if you do not enter it, you will not be liberated. Therefore, do not attain it, and do not fail to enter it. This is what is called 'entering the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be spoken of; it is something to be experienced. If you speak of it, you will be wrong; if you experience it, you will be right. If you do not speak of it, you will not be wrong; if you do not experience it, you will not be right. Therefore, do not speak of it, and do not fail to experience it. This is what is called 'experiencing the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be known; it is something to be forgotten. If you know it, you will be deluded; if you forget it, you will be enlightened. If you do not know it, you will not be deluded; if you do not forget it, you will not be enlightened. Therefore, do not know it, and do not fail to forget it. This is what is called 'forgetting the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be seen; it is something to be heard. If you see it, you will be obstructed; if you hear it, you will be unobstructed. If you do not see it, you will not be obstructed; if you do not hear it, you will not be unobstructed. Therefore, do not see it, and do not fail to hear it. This is what is called 'hearing the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be thought about; it is something to be contemplated. If you think about it, you will be distracted; if you contemplate it, you will be focused. If you do not think about it, you will not be distracted; if you do not contemplate it, you will not be focused. Therefore, do not think about it, and do not fail to contemplate it. This is what is called 'contemplating the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be analyzed; it is something to be integrated. If you analyze it, you will fragment it; if you integrate it, you will unify it. If you do not analyze it, you will not fragment it; if you do not integrate it, you will not unify it. Therefore, do not analyze it, and do not fail to integrate it. This is what is called 'integrating the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be measured; it is something to be encompassed. If you measure it, you will limit it; if you encompass it, you will include it. If you do not measure it, you will not limit it; if you do not encompass it, you will not include it. Therefore, do not measure it, and do not fail to encompass it. This is what is called 'encompassing the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be sought externally; it is to be found internally. If you seek it externally, you will wander in the world of phenomena. If you find it internally, you will return to the source of reality. Therefore, do not seek it externally, and do not fail to find it internally. This is what is called 'finding the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be grasped with the intellect; it is to be grasped with the heart. If you grasp it with the intellect, you will be caught in the net of discrimination. If you grasp it with the heart, you will be free from all attachments. Therefore, do not grasp it with the intellect, and do not fail to grasp it with the heart. This is what is called 'grasping the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be cultivated; it is to be cultivated by nature. If you cultivate it, you will create artificiality; if you cultivate by nature, you will be spontaneous. Therefore, do not cultivate it, and do not fail to cultivate by nature. This is what is called 'cultivating the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be maintained; it is to be maintained by non-action. If you maintain it, you will create effort; if you maintain by non-action, you will be effortless. Therefore, do not maintain it, and do not fail to maintain by non-action. This is what is called 'maintaining the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be taught; it is to be taught by example. If you teach it, you will be verbose; if you teach by example, you will be concise. Therefore, do not teach it, and do not fail to teach by example. This is what is called 'teaching the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be transmitted; it is to be transmitted by realization. If you transmit it, you will be partial; if you transmit by realization, you will be complete. Therefore, do not transmit it, and do not fail to transmit by realization. This is what is called 'transmitting the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be preserved; it is to be preserved by emptiness. If you preserve it, you will be bound; if you preserve by emptiness, you will be liberated. Therefore, do not preserve it, and do not fail to preserve by emptiness. This is what is called 'preserving the Way. The student bowed and departed. The Master said, "The Way is not something to be hidden; it is to be hidden by non-manifestation. If you hide it, you will be secretive; if you hide by non-manifestation, you will be transparent. Therefore, do not hide it, and do not fail to hide by non-manifestation. The Master said, "Sometimes I lean alone against the courtyard railing, idly gazing at four or five branches of plum blossoms.
He asked, "What is it that reaches neither the meaning nor the words? The Master replied, "The falling flowers flow away with the stream; they vainly burden the wandering traveler.

One day he sighed, saying, "My body has long been afflicted by illness; it is so emaciated and frail that I shall likely be of no further benefit to the world. He then gathered the assembly to give his final instructions.

Regarding his final affairs, he spoke with great earnestness and did not cease until the end. He passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the right of Qingshan.
Chan Master Baopu Dalian of the Jingming Hermitage in Huzhou was the son of the Luo family of Lin’an, Hangzhou.

Having lost both parents in childhood, he entered the monastic life at Miaoyan Monastery on Green Mountain. He received full ordination at Yunqi and, after attending lectures, renounced scholastic study.

While practicing Chan at Shuangjing, he entered the retreat period. One day, while leaning against the urinal bucket, he attained great enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "Since childhood I lost my mother; I have searched for her everywhere in foreign lands.
Suddenly we meet face-to-face—there is no need for further deliberation. He then visited Longchi, entering the abbot’s quarters.
He made a circular gesture with his sitting cloth, performed three prostrations with the cloth unfolded, and upon finishing, he gathered the cloth and gave a single sweep of his hand.
He departed. In the afternoon, he entered the Abbot’s quarters once more. Yuanchi asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "I am a disciple of Yunqi in ancient Hangzhou.
Yuanchi said, "What Dharma does Yunqi teach? The Master said, "Yunqi does not teach the Dharma. Yuanchi said, "Neither do I teach the Dharma here.
The Master said, "I have come from afar specifically to observe your style; why do you say you do not teach it?"
Fahui said, "This old monk’s teeth have become sparse and missing. The Master said, "The Way does not reside in the teeth. Fahui said, "That is no longer the case.
The Master said, "The Way has neither past nor present. Fahui said, "In that case, you have understood, Venerable.
The Master said, "I do not know if it is permissible to say one has understood. Fahui said, "I have already said so. The Master then paid his respects.

He bowed and departed, saying, "To take a mistake and follow it through. He also said, "Everyone is hidden within the weeds. Later, after he had taken up residence, a monk asked, "What is the 'knife that kills'?
The Master said, "The curtain hangs down, confining the young swallows. The monk asked, "What is the 'sword that gives life'? The Master said, "A hole in paper lets out a foolish fly.
A monk asked about the story of Xiangyan climbing the tree; the Master called out loudly, "One person!"
Question: "When Xiangyan fell and died, [the Master] said, 'It is merely a case of great alarm over a small matter. The Master replied, 'Human life is no small affair.
In the eighth month of the second year of the Chongzhen era, he manifested a slight illness. As he was about to depart, the assembly requested his final word.
The Master said, "I have a verse on the correspondence of daily life. He sat cross-legged and passed away. The verse says:
Black and white walk side by side, yet they are of the same age; In lush, verdant grass, they sleep wherever they find it. At once, the autumn sky is cleared of all clouds.
● "In the deep night, where is one's home?
This was the dialogue between Jingshan Yu and Feng'an Xueqiao Yuanxin Chan Master. [Yuanxin] was the son of the Zhu family from Ningbo’s Qian County.

At the age of nine, he heard the *Amitābha Sūtra* being recited and perceived that even the waterfowl and the trees were all reciting the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. From that time on, he resolved his mind [upon awakening].

At the age of twenty-nine, he left the household life and began traveling as a mendicant. Each day he remained in a state of mental blankness, possessing only a single point of inquiry that he could not understand.
For two years he struggled in vain to find an entry point. Later, he visited Master Miaozhen on Mount Qinwang.
The Master recounted the incident concerning the monk with supernormal powers. A monk asked him, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from India.
The one with supernormal powers said, "I have heard there are three Indias; which India have you come from? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk was speechless.
From that time on, the Master’s state of doubt suddenly arose. The following day, he gripped his staff and went to the Stone Head; holding it aloft, he...
He said, "From which India have you come? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Suddenly, the past and future were severed, like the sun’s disk emerging from the sky.
He spoke a verse: "The stone is pressed against the spine; I turn over, and my ribs are exposed. Reflecting upon this carefully, Even to move, I cannot.
Again he let out a shout: "Zhang San has committed murder; Li Si must repay the debt of life. Then he returned to Tiantai.
Seeking confirmation from others, he looked up and saw the three characters "Ancient Yunmen" (古雲門), whereupon he attained great enlightenment. On the road, he composed a verse:
"Once I ascended Mount Tiantai, the clouds grew deeper; I stepped upon my straw sandals until their strings were severed.
The five hundred bhikṣus left no trace; Seeing him now, I shall break their sinews. Thereafter, while clearing away brush to establish a hermitage at Shuangji, he visited Yunqi Hongluo.
Chichi’s Lineage. In the forty-third year of the Wanli era, he resided at Qianzhi Hermitage on Mount Jing.
In the eighth year of the Chongzhen era, Huang Duanbo, the Magistrate of Hangzhou, invited him to ascend the hall at the Great Hall. He exclaimed: "Heave! Heave! Heave!
This is the Mount Jing of the Tang and Song dynasties. Striking his whisk, he said: "Eighty-one people have passed through here; it is not merely of today."
Jingshan is not the Jingshan of a single day. A thousand years of permanent residence in one morning’s assembly of monks.
Today, the Patriarchal Command is being put into action; the ten directions are cut off at once. Tell me, is there an auspicious omen or not?
The bell tower grows ears; the Buddha Hall again conceives. Huang Gong stepped forward and asked, "What is the bell tower growing ears? The Master picked up some fresh incense.
The Master pointed to him and said, "This is what you will eventually grasp. [The official] asked, "What is the Buddha-hall that is also pregnant?
The Master said, "It has already given birth. The official bowed and said, "It must be the Great Master’s preaching of the Dharma that makes this possible.
The Master then said, "Now, by the request of all the donors, we have invited the Elder to ascend the lion seat to restore the desolate ancestral hall and support the crumbling legacy."

As for "Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat," let us not ask about "the daughter-in-law riding the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it. Speak a single phrase! Is there anyone who can say it?
With one sweep, he strikes open the moon over the golden palace; among the ten thousand households, there is none that does not shine.
On that very day, the newly appointed Governor Yu Da and a multitude of lay practitioners invited the Master for a vegetarian feast at the Han Cui Lou.
The Master said, "This old man is sixty-six years old this year. He then rotated his fingers, saying: "Bing, Ding, Wu, Ji, Geng. After a long while, he spoke again.
"How strange it is to see you dragging people here and there! It turns out the Water Buffalo has entered the natal palace (*mìnggōng*).

It drags through mud and water, nudging east and poking west. Nevertheless, fortunately, there is plenty of water and plenty of grass. Huang Gong asked, "When there is plenty of water and plenty of grass, what is it like?

The Master said, "It kills one with satiety. Gong asked, "Is the Water Buffalo still dozing? The Master said, "A thump!"* *Note: "A thump" (pū) is a non-verbal response indicating a sudden realization or a state beyond conceptualization. In this context, it signifies that the buffalo has transcended the duality of sleep and wakefulness.*
Facing the autumn river, the white moon flies; the egret crashes into the reeds. Master Yu said, "In such a state, you have gone into the realm of uniformity.
The Master said, "The reeds turn into black ash and fly; the egret does not crash into the ranks of the reeds.
Master Yu said, "Today is the first day of the sixth month; has the Great Master ever experienced this sixth month? The Master said, "There is you."
"Did you see it? Yu said, "Truly, these fine flakes of snow are a pity; they fall amidst the snow, yet no one recognizes them.
The Master said, "What need is there for recognition? Yu said, "If it were brought here and fashioned into a snow lion, what would happen if someone pushed it over?
The Master said, "There is no need to push it over; I shall sit upon the ground myself. Huang said, "One must still support it before it can stand."

When the Master was traveling as a wandering monk (*yātrā*), he looked up and saw the ancient Yunmen, attaining great enlightenment. He made a vow to propagate the single school of Yunmen.
In the winter of the Guiwei year, he began teaching at Dongta; his offering of incense to seek dharma transmission first succeeded that of Longchi. Later, he resided at Yunmen.
One day, he manifested illness and wrote a verse, saying: "Little children! On the road of birth and death, one must be carefree.
Under the bright moon and frosty dawn, I shall drink a cup of tea and pass away while sitting. This was the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month in the year of Dinghai.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at his native mountain.

Chan Master Yuanhu Miaoyong of Puming Monastery in Jianning Prefecture was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Xingshan Guang; he was the son of Zheng [family] from Haining, Hangzhou, and entered the monastic order.
At Xingshan Temple in Jiaxing, he received his formal training under Nanming. Previously, he had visited Wuhuan, who bestowed upon him the essentials of Chan.

One day, while reading the commentary on the *Siyi Fantian Jing* (The Scripture of the Brahma Heaven of Further Benefit) in the meditation hall at Mount Jing, he attained a realization. He immediately presented a verse on non-arising (*amutpāda*) as follows:
"Who dares to shatter the iron walls and silver mountains? A thief’s body is suddenly pressed against me. Looking at one another, it is revealed to be the original."
They were acquainted with one another. At that moment, [Zhaozhou] felt abashed and his smile faded. Mingjian saw through him and rebuked him. He served [Mingjian] for several years.

When Mingjian fell gravely ill, the Master visited him morning and evening. Mingjian responded by saying he had no color left in his face. One day, Mingjian cited a verse by Xiangyan and questioned the Master.
As soon as the Master opened his mouth, Mingjian let out a shout. When the Master again prepared to speak, Mingjian shouted once more. The Master then... [pointed].
Shou wrote a verse of entrustment, saying: "There is no dharma to be transmitted, nor a mind to be received; it is entrusted to one who has no hands, severing the sinews of empty space.
Later, upon reading the account of Baiyun’s awakening through the karmic conditions of the Fifth Patriarch, he finally attained a state of complete liberation and unimpededness.
While enjoying the new moon with Master Xueqiao, Xueqiao pointed at the moon and said, "Where has that other half gone?
The Master remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you understand? Xueqiao replied, "I can only get half of it. The Master said, "Where has that other half gone?
Xueqiao also remained silent for a long while. The Master said, "I can only get half of it. (The 12th year of the Chongzhen era).
Abiding in Universal Radiance, he addressed the assembly: "If one were to discuss the Buddha-dharma, this sick monk would have no place to set his teeth.
Today, by chance, I saw the new mountain gate; seizing my staff, I wandered and played, passing through Guozi Ridge straight to Huoshao Bridge.
I lost my footing and fell into a deep ravine. Fortunately, the old Buddha Hall was willing to come and rescue me. Not only..."
"Let us rescue one another and mount the neck [of the ox]. Returning to the New Mountain Gate, we shall cry out our grievances. We cannot avoid having the sick monk adjudicate this:
the New Mountain Gate deserves thirty blows of the staff, and the Old Buddha Hall likewise deserves thirty blows. Justice must not be rendered crookedly.
After a long silence, he threw down the staff and said, "The staff suddenly moves with an expression of anger. Everyone, let us go home."
They went into the heated room. The Chief Censor Huang Chenghao, having been promoted to Guangdong, came into the mountains to bid the Master farewell.
He asked, "I beg the Master for instruction on a single phrase for my departure. The Master said, "When you encounter people three thousand *li* away, do not speak of this in error.
The Master was close friends with Furi (Furitsu). When Furi was residing at Xuefeng, the Master was invited by Puming to open a Dharma hall; Furi accompanied him.
The various donors and patrons invited the Master to appear in the world, but he declined their request firmly on the pretext of illness.

whether north, south, east, or west, one moves with spontaneous freedom. Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring mountains layer upon layer of chaotic green; the spring waters shimmer with empty azure.

In the thirteenth year of the Chongzhen era, while presiding over the Huayan Assembly at Gunan Man, he ascended the hall and said: "In the Dharmadhātu of the Avataṃsaka, principle and phenomena are unimpeded;
in repentance and the elimination of calamities, one stroke wins both prizes. He then suddenly took up his staff and said, "The Venerable Dushun has arrived!"

The New Year’s Day Lecture for the Birthday of Master Dong. On the first day of the new year, the light wind and clear sun are auspicious. Great assembly:

from before the time of Vipaśyin Buddha (Viyūṇā-rāja) until the present moment, whether there are buddha-fields or no buddha-fields, within that span there have been unspeakable numbers of days and months, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of years, and unspeakably unspeakable...
It is said that when a kingdom is established, there are no days that do not follow this principle:

from the very first day, the imperial wind sweeps vast and boundless across the eight directions, and the elders of the wilds sing of joy throughout the myriad regions without end. Now, suppose there is an individual who appears in the world and happens to encounter such a day—what then?
Having received the legacy of ritual, music, poetry, and history, they will surely don the ceremonial cap and fasten the sash.
The Master ascended the hall, cast down his staff, and said: "This falling is not something other. He then raised it again and danced, saying:

At the peak of Taibai, a thousand divergences are cut off; beneath the bridge of Qingguan, a single pulse flows eternally.

Chan Master Fushitong Gui of Suzhou Ba’en Temple was the son of the Li family of Pinghu. At nineteen, he shaved his head and donned the robes at Putuo.

Gathering it all up: it is neither form nor mind, neither like nor different. When you wish to use it, use it; when you wish to discard it, discard it. When you wish to act, act;

The Hall. Our late Master was not born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month in the year of Yihai; our late Master did not die on that same day.

A momentous matter, yet you seek it at the lips of those with intellectual knowledge. When you see someone say "it is thus," you immediately understand it as being thus;
when you see someone say "it is not thus," you immediately understand it as being not thus; when you see someone say "it is so," you immediately understand it as being so;
when you see someone say "it is not so," you immediately understand it as being not so. If you study in this manner, such is the way you will be entangled.
Sheshan said: "As for me, this mountain monk, I truly have no particular excellence. I simply recognize you all: when you go, I seal it;
when you stay, I break the seal. Even if you neither go nor stay, that is still not the news of having arrived home.
Leaning on his staff, he said: "Since leaving Sudhana, there has been nothing else; the gates of the pavilions remain open all day long. Evening.
Consider this: A great man, a hero of noble spirit, thrusts his body into the mouth of a fierce tiger and rubs his head against the head of a venomous snake;
even this is not considered extraordinary. Yet, if one hesitates, falters, or fails to advance, one will strike against a skull and leave corpses strewn for ten thousand miles.
Therefore, the veteran generals of the school rush through the blades like flowing water and pass through the flames faster than the wind; they shift the constellations and move the heavens.
Stars thunder and lightning flashes; he drives the oxen of the plowmen and snatches the food from hungry men.
Like a king wielding a sword, he has mastery over killing and giving life. A lion roams about, seeking no companion. Is there anyone like this?
Did you not see that at that time, when the Great Master Linji received three heavy blows from Huangbo, he immediately attained realization? He then returned to the ribs of Dayu.
[The Master] makes a fist. "Tell me, why is it like this? He lets out a shout and says, "A man-child has his own ambition to soar to the heavens;
he does not travel where others have trodden. He lets out another shout. Grand Master Xueqiao arrives and asks, "You were over there; why are you now here?
The Master replies, "A single drop of ink forms two dragons. Xueqiao says, "I do not understand."
Yun was present as a *xiá* (misty glow). The Master said, "Today I have let the Great Master off with a pardon.
During tea, Xue said, "In my daily practice, I teach people only to recite the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. The Master said, "How many people have misunderstood the Great Master’s intent?

Xue said, "Even if one does not misunderstand it, one is still far from it. The Master said, "The Great Master should not deceive people. This occurred while they were walking in front of the mountain gate.
Seeing a dog barking, Xue said, "This fellow has no Buddha-nature. The Master replied, "But you have just scratched the Great Master's itch.
Xue laughed heartily. As the assembly was about to pay their respects, Xue looked to his left and right; the assembly stood waiting.
The Master said, "They are all honest fellows. Xue said, "In a lion’s den there are no other beasts;
why then do you say they are honest fellows? The Master said, "Who would dare to raise their hand before the Great Master?

Master Shanzu asked, "Śākyamuni’s 'closing the room' and Vimalakīrti’s silence both belong to the realm of expedient teachings (*upāya*). They do not fall within the present moment. Please, Master, speak."

[A student] said, "A single phrase. The Master said, "Before you have even asked, it has already been answered. [The student] asked, "Who can testify to this? The Master said, "Liao the Bearded at the crossroads.

[The student] asked again, "It is known to both you and me that our late teacher did not settle his affairs; how will you bring them to completion for him? The Master said, "To add further grievance and suffering to the midst of heaven.
[The student] said, "Were it not for you, brother, I would not understand. The Master said: *Note: This dialogue is from the *Wumenguan* (Gateless Barrier), Case 19.*
"When meeting people, never fail to raise the matter correctly. He asked again, "For ten years we have been fellow students, our singing and clapping never separated.
As you depart for Lian-an, Brother, will you see me? The Master said, "In a place where there is no one, we shall look at each other with hands pressed to our foreheads (*zhua'e*).

He said, "He has no face; what is there to look at? The Master said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. He asked, "Setting aside the raising of the mallet and the brandishing of the whisk for a moment, [what of] this brand-new [reality]?"
The student brought forward a doctrinal phrase. The Master said, "A single palm, a single handful of blood. The student said, "One must be an elder brother like you to attain this.

The Master said, "That is my own fault. He asked again, "To discuss the profound and explain the subtle is what the sages of old condemned; to blink an eye or raise an eyebrow is the current decadence of Chan.
Setting aside these two paths, what is your true way of acting for others? The Master said, "I do not teach."
He ruined the men and women of the household, saying, "It is too much! The Master said, "Dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish, but a patch-robed monk is difficult to deceive.
At Mount Nanyue, at Yinxianyan, Master Shanzitongji of Qingshan asked, "What is 'hiding the point within the principle'?
The Master replied, "In the Hall of Emperor Liang, he said, 'I do not know. The Master asked, "What is 'hiding the point within the phenomenon'? The Master [replied]...
Yangshan said, "This morning it rained, yet when the water falls to the ground, it does not dry. Dongshan asked, "What is 'both principle and phenomena conceal their sharpness'?

The Master replied, "Walking, one does not go out the door; sitting, one does not occupy the main hall. Dongshan asked, "What is 'neither involving phenomena nor principle, both conceal their sharpness'?"
The Master said: "An octagonal grinding stone runs through the void.
*Wudeng Huiyuan Xulüe*, Scroll Four, Part Two (End).
Phonetic Glossary: Yūn (pronounced *yú yún*; meaning deep and vast water). Càn (pronounced *jí chǎn*; meaning to press or urge).
